Ben tre quarti del Sole erano oscurati alla vista e assumeva la forma di una falce o di una luna nuova, e nel momento in cui il firmamento ha assunto un colore violetto chiaro, quando l'eclissi era al massimo, alcune persone hanno avuto lievi brividi lungo la schiena, simili a quelli provati al tempo della cometa di Halley. Ma vi sono molte persone superstiziose che si spaventano alla minima provocazione.

Si dice che sabato sera più strumenti diversi siano stati puntati sul vecchio Sole che mai prima nella storia del mondo, poiché la scienza lavora costantemente a perfezionare nuovi strumenti per lo studio dell'astronomia, dei fenomeni aerei, ecc., e tutti questi sono stati messi in servizio, ma lo strumento popolare per osservare la bella e attraente scena offerta dall'eclissi era il vecchio pezzo di vetro affumicato. Esso attenuava il bagliore del Sole — e di bagliore ce n'era, eccome — e dava a chi aveva il vetro affumicato un'ottima occasione di vedere l'eclissi da casa o dal posto di lavoro.

Mai prima d'ora un'eclissi totale è avvenuta in alcun luogo del mondo offrendo tanti siti accessibili per l'osservazione. Per i profani come per gli scienziati lo spettacolo si è rivelato insieme nuovo e interessante, e centinaia di persone si erano procurate vetri affumicati per assistere al fenomeno.

Spedizioni di scienziati erano state inviate a Lick, Yerkes, monte Wilson, all'Ufficio Meteorologico e ad altri osservatori per assistere all'eclissi attraverso vetri appositamente costruiti.
text.ja:
ラレドの民間人と軍人は、土曜日の晩の日食に大きな関心を示し、6時過ぎには数千の人々が、この地方では1世紀のあいだ二度と見られない光景—ほぼ皆既の日食—を目にした。太陽は優に4分の3が視界から隠れ、三日月、つまり新月の形をとり、日食が最大となって天空が淡い菫色になったころには、ハレー彗星のときに味わったのに似た軽い寒気が背筋を走った人も少数いた。しかし、わずかなきっかけで怯える迷信深い人は多い。

土曜日の晩には、世界の歴史上かつてないほど多くのさまざまな器具が老いた太陽に向けられたという。科学は天文学や空中現象などの研究のため、新しい器械を絶えず改良しており、それらすべてが使われたからだが、日食が見せる美しく魅力的な光景を見るための人気の器具は、昔ながらの燻したガラス片であった。これは太陽のまぶしさ—確かにいくらかまぶしさはあった—を殺し、燻したガラスを持つ人に、自宅や勤め先から日食を見る絶好の機会を与えた。

皆既日食が、観測のできる場所をこれほど多く提供しながら世界のどこかで起こったことは、かつてなかった。素人にも科学者にも、この見せ物は目新しく興味深いものとなり、何百人もが燻したガラスを用意して現象を見た。

科学者の遠征隊が、特別製のガラスを通して日食を見るため、リック、ヤーキス、ウィルソン山、気象局、その他の天文台に派遣されていた。

text_orig: Mr. Lawson, cashier at the M. & M. bank arrived on the Princess Alice last evening and is at his post of duty today, giving our good citizens all the money they want. Mr. Lawson has been away for about a month and declares he has enjoyed every minute of his visit. Most of which time has been spent with his people, going to the beaches and motoring to places of interest. Mr. Lawson tells about going to Chehalis to see the eclipse and the wonderful sight it afforded the visitors who motored in thousands there to witness this interesting phenomenon.

text.zh-Hans: M. & M. 银行出纳劳森先生昨晚乘爱丽丝公主号抵埠，今日已在岗位，任我们的好市民要多少钱给多少钱。劳森先生离开约一月，自称每一分钟都过得快活。大半时间陪家人，逛海滩，驱车游览名胜。劳森先生说起前往切哈利斯观日食，说那里成千游客驱车去看这有趣的现象，景象奇妙。
text.zh-Hant: M. & M. 銀行出納勞森先生昨晚乘愛麗絲公主號抵埠，今日已在崗位，任我們的好市民要多少錢給多少錢。勞森先生離開約一月，自稱每一分鐘都過得快活。大半時間陪家人，逛海灘，驅車遊覽名勝。勞森先生説起前往切哈利斯觀日食，説那裏成千遊客驅車去看這有趣的現象，景象奇妙。
text.en: Mr. Lawson, cashier at the M. & M. bank arrived on the Princess Alice last evening and is at his post of duty today, giving our good citizens all the money they want. Mr. Lawson has been away for about a month and declares he has enjoyed every minute of his visit. Most of which time has been spent with his people, going to the beaches and motoring to places of interest. Mr. Lawson tells about going to Chehalis to see the eclipse and the wonderful sight it afforded the visitors who motored in thousands there to witness this interesting phenomenon.
text.fr: M. Lawson, caissier de la banque M. & M., est arrivé hier soir sur le Princess Alice et se trouve à son poste aujourd'hui, donnant à nos bons citoyens tout l'argent qu'ils veulent. M. Lawson était absent depuis environ un mois et déclare avoir savouré chaque minute de sa visite. La plus grande partie de ce temps a été passée avec les siens, à aller aux plages et à faire des promenades en auto vers des lieux intéressants. M. Lawson raconte qu'il est allé à Chehalis pour voir l'éclipse et le merveilleux spectacle qu'elle a offert aux visiteurs qui s'y rendaient par milliers en auto pour assister à cet intéressant phénomène.
text.es: El señor Lawson, cajero del banco M. & M., llegó anoche en el Princess Alice y hoy está en su puesto de trabajo, dando a nuestros buenos ciudadanos todo el dinero que quieren. El señor Lawson ha estado fuera cerca de un mes y declara que ha disfrutado cada minuto de su visita. La mayor parte de ese tiempo la pasó con su familia, yendo a las playas y recorriendo en automóvil lugares de interés. El señor Lawson cuenta que fue a Chehalis a ver el eclipse y la maravillosa vista que ofreció a los visitantes que acudieron por millares en automóvil a presenciar este interesante fenómeno.
text.it: Il signor Lawson, cassiere della banca M. & M., è arrivato ieri sera con la Princess Alice ed è oggi al suo posto di lavoro, dando ai nostri buoni cittadini tutto il denaro che vogliono. Il signor Lawson è stato via per circa un mese e dichiara di essersi goduto ogni minuto della visita. La maggior parte del tempo è stata trascorsa con i suoi, andando alle spiagge e in automobile in luoghi interessanti. Il signor Lawson racconta di essere andato a Chehalis a vedere l'eclissi e dello spettacolo meraviglioso che essa ha offerto ai visitatori, che a migliaia sono giunti in automobile a vedere questo interessante fenomeno.
text.ja: M. & M. 銀行の出納係ローソン氏は昨晩プリンセス・アリス号で到着し、今日は持ち場におり、善良な市民たちが望むだけの金を渡している。ローソン氏は約1か月留守にしており、訪問の間の一分一分を楽しんだと言っている。その大半を家族と過ごし、海岸へ行ったり、名所へ車で出かけたりして過ごした。ローソン氏は、日食を見にシェハリスへ行ったことと、この興味深い現象を見るために何千人もの訪問客が車で押し寄せたその素晴らしい光景について語っている。

text_orig:
People of Hood River and their guests, who viewed the total eclipse of the sun from the northern section of Hood River county at points from which both Mount Hood and Mount Adams were visible, were privileged the rare sight of beholding one mountain in ghost-like shadow while the other was resplendent in the rays of the afternoon sun.

Mount Hood was without the zone of total eclipse, while Adams was near the center of the zone. Those who saw both mountains declare that the contrast between the two snow peaks was the most impressive incident of the eclipse.

text.zh-Hans:
胡德里弗人及其客人，在胡德里弗县北部可同时望见胡德山与亚当斯山之处观日全食，有幸得见一奇景：一山沉在鬼魅般的阴影里，另一山却沐浴在午后阳光中熠熠生辉。

胡德山在全食区之外，亚当斯山近全食区中心。两山都见到的人称，两座雪峰的反差，是日食中最动人的一幕。
text.zh-Hant:
胡德河人及其客人，在胡德河縣北部可同時望見胡德山與亞當斯山之處觀日全食，有幸得見一奇景：一山沉在鬼魅般的陰影裏，另一山卻沐浴在午後陽光中熠熠生輝。

胡德山在全食區之外，亞當斯山近全食區中心。兩山都見到的人稱，兩座雪峯的反差，是日食中最動人的一幕。

text.fr:
Les gens de Hood River et leurs invités, qui ont vu l'éclipse totale de Soleil depuis la partie nord du comté de Hood River, en des points d'où l'on voyait à la fois le mont Hood et le mont Adams, ont eu le privilège de la rare vue d'une montagne dans une ombre fantomatique tandis que l'autre resplendissait dans les rayons du Soleil de l'après-midi.

Le mont Hood était hors de la zone d'éclipse totale, tandis qu'Adams était près du centre de la zone. Ceux qui ont vu les deux montagnes déclarent que le contraste entre les deux pics neigeux a été l'incident le plus impressionnant de l'éclipse.
text.es:
La gente de Hood River y sus invitados, que vieron el eclipse total de Sol desde la sección norte del condado de Hood River, en puntos desde los que eran visibles tanto el monte Hood como el monte Adams, tuvieron el privilegio de contemplar la rara vista de una montaña en una sombra fantasmal mientras la otra resplandecía bajo los rayos del Sol de la tarde.

El monte Hood quedaba fuera de la zona de eclipse total, mientras que el Adams estaba cerca del centro de la zona. Quienes vieron ambas montañas declaran que el contraste entre los dos picos nevados fue el incidente más impresionante del eclipse.
text.it:
La gente di Hood River e i loro ospiti, che hanno osservato l'eclissi totale di Sole dalla sezione settentrionale della contea di Hood River in punti da cui erano visibili sia il monte Hood sia il monte Adams, hanno avuto il privilegio della rara vista di un monte in un'ombra spettrale mentre l'altro era splendente nei raggi del Sole pomeridiano.

Il monte Hood era fuori dalla zona dell'eclissi totale, mentre l'Adams era vicino al centro della zona. Coloro che hanno visto entrambi i monti dichiarano che il contrasto tra le due vette nevose è stato l'episodio più impressionante dell'eclissi.
text.ja:
フッドリバーの人々とその客人のうち、フッドリバー郡北部の、フッド山とアダムズ山の両方が見える地点から日食の皆既を眺めた人々は、一方の山が幽霊のような影に包まれているときに、もう一方の山が午後の日の光に輝いているという、めったにない光景を目にする特権に恵まれた。

フッド山は皆既の帯の外にあり、アダムズ山は帯の中心の近くにあった。両方の山を見た人々は、二つの雪の峰の対照が日食の最も印象深い出来事であったと断言している。

text_orig:
Members of a road crew, who observed the eclipse during a pause from their labors, tell of an amusing incident furnished by a big yellowhammer overtaken away from home when the total eclipse came.

The men say that the big bird evidently was unable to see in the dim light of the eclipse. It was also apparently badly frightened. The bird, in its mad rush to get home to wife and babies, went dashing madly through the tree tops, coming in frequent contact with the boughs.

text.zh-Hans:
筑路队的几个人在歇工间隙观日食，说起一桩趣事，主角是一只大黄锤鸟，全食来时正远离家巢。

他们说那只大鸟在日食的昏暗中显然看不见，又似乎吓得不轻。它发疯般赶着回家，奔向妻与幼雏，在树梢间乱冲，不时撞上枝丫。
text.zh-Hant:
築路隊的幾個人在歇工間隙觀日食，説起一樁趣事，主角是一隻大黃錘鳥，全食來時正遠離家巢。

他們説那隻大鳥在日食的昏暗中顯然看不見，又似乎嚇得不輕。它發瘋般趕着回家，奔向妻與幼雛，在樹梢間亂衝，不時撞上枝丫。
text.en:
Members of a road crew, who observed the eclipse during a pause from their labors, tell of an amusing incident furnished by a big yellowhammer overtaken away from home when the total eclipse came.

The men say that the big bird evidently was unable to see in the dim light of the eclipse. It was also apparently badly frightened. The bird, in its mad rush to get home to wife and babies, went dashing madly through the tree tops, coming in frequent contact with the boughs.
text.fr:
Des membres d'une équipe de travaux routiers, qui ont observé l'éclipse pendant une pause de leur travail, racontent un incident amusant fourni par un gros pic doré surpris loin de chez lui quand l'éclipse totale est venue.

Ces hommes disent que le gros oiseau n'a manifestement pas pu voir dans la faible lumière de l'éclipse. Il était aussi apparemment fort effrayé. L'oiseau, dans sa course folle pour rentrer auprès de sa femme et de ses petits, s'est précipité éperdument à travers la cime des arbres, entrant fréquemment en contact avec les branches.
text.es:
Miembros de una cuadrilla de camineros, que observaron el eclipse durante una pausa en sus labores, cuentan un incidente divertido protagonizado por un gran pito sorprendido lejos de casa cuando llegó el eclipse total.

Los hombres dicen que el gran pájaro evidentemente no podía ver en la luz tenue del eclipse. También estaba, al parecer, muy asustado. El pájaro, en su loca carrera por llegar a casa con su esposa y sus polluelos, se lanzó enloquecido por las copas de los árboles, chocando con frecuencia contra las ramas.
text.it:
I membri di una squadra stradale, che hanno osservato l'eclissi durante una pausa dal lavoro, raccontano di un episodio divertente fornito da un grosso picchio sorpreso lontano da casa quando è giunta l'eclissi totale.

Gli uomini dicono che il grosso uccello evidentemente non riusciva a vedere nella luce fioca dell'eclissi. Sembrava anche, a quanto pare, molto spaventato. L'uccello, nella sua folle corsa per tornare a casa dalla moglie e dai piccoli, si è lanciato come impazzito tra le cime degli alberi, urtando di frequente contro i rami.
text.ja:
仕事の合間に日食を観察した道路作業班の人々が、皆既が来たとき家から離れたところで追いつかれた大きなイエローハンマーが引き起こした愉快な出来事を語っている。

男たちによれば、その大きな鳥は日食の薄暗い光の中ではどうやら見えなかったらしい。また、ひどく怯えているようでもあった。その鳥は、妻と雛の待つ家に帰ろうと狂ったように急ぎ、梢の間を猛然と突き進み、しばしば枝にぶつかった。

text_orig:
The Solar Eclipse To-day.—As in this city about eleven-twelfths of the surface of the sun will be covered by the moon at the time of greatest obscurity, about 6 o'clock p. m., there will be an unusual darkness for that hour, but disappointment will probably be expressed by most spectators at the amount of daylight which will still remain. The darkness will not be so great as it is when one-twelfth of the sun is just above the horizon at its setting. The line of shade will creep gradually up over the disc of the sun, covering the lower limb regularly in its progress. At its greatest obscuration, about eleven-twelfths of the sun's surface will be darkened, and the small rim unobscured will be the upper section of its disc. About fifteen minutes will elapse between the ending of the eclipse and the setting of the sun. Outside of the line of totality there is comparatively little to see. The illumination of the sun's light will be very perceptible, even if the day should chance to be cloudy, but at this distance from the line it will still give as much light as 100,000 full moons. Possibly the planet Venus may be visible, about twenty-four degrees from the sun, toward the southeast.

To non-scientific observers, an ordinary opera-glass, muffled with a piece of colored or smoked glass, or even the smoked glass without the opera-glass, will afford sufficient means of watching the wondrous changes during this remarkable phenomena. The following observations may be made without instruments:

1. As the eclipse advances it is desirable to obtain some notion or measure of the degree of darkness

2. At what distance from the eye can a book or paper, exhibiting type of various sizes, be read?

3. Hold up a lighted candle nearly between your eye and the sun. At how many suns' breadths distance from the sun can the flame be seen?

4. If you are in an elevated position remark the changes of color and appearance of the surrounding objects in the landscape.

5. If you see the spots of light, formed by the intersecting shadows of the boughs of the trees, remark whether they exhibit the same form of the sun.

There are numerous simple philosophical instruments in the possession of all; such as thermometers, barometers, and even hygrometers. All observations made with these will be invaluable.

A correspondent writes of the coming eclipse as follows:—“Few people trouble themselves to think what the effect would be if the eclipse of Saturday were to last any length of time, and the sun were blotted from the heavens. Philosophy declares that not only would a horror of darkness cover the earth, but the moisture of the air would be precipitated in vast showers to the earth, and the temperature fall to a fearful point of cold, nothing less than 130 degrees below zero, Fahrenheit. The earth would be the seat of darkness, and more than Arctic desolation. Nothing could survive such freezing cold a moment, more than one could breathe in scalding water. In three days after the cooling process began, nothing created would be alive but the monsters that wallow in deep ocean, and the eyeless reptiles that make their haunts in caves which penetrate far underground. The thought of this possibility will add a zest to the inspection with “smoked opera-glasses” which will absorb the community about 5.30 this afternoon.”

text.zh-Hans:
今日日食。本城今日约下午六时食甚，日面十二分之十一为月所掩，就此时而言，天色将异常昏暗，然观者多半将怅然于所余日光之多。其暗不及日将落、日轮仅十二分之一尚在地平之上时。食影将渐渐上蔽日轮，下缘依次为所掩。至食甚，日面约十二分之十一暗，所余未蔽之小边，乃日轮之上段。食终至日落，约隔十五分钟。全食带之外，所可见者较少。纵逢天阴，日光之减亦必显然，然距全食带如此之远，所余之光仍抵十万轮满月。金星或可得见，距日约二十四度，在东南。

非专门观天者，以寻常观剧镜蒙以有色或熏黑之玻璃，即不用观剧镜而仅用熏黑玻璃，亦足以观此奇象之变幻。无仪器亦可作下列观测：

一、食渐进，宜略测天色昏暗之度。

二、距目几何，书册纸张上各号字尚可辨读？

三、举点燃之烛，近于目与日之间。距日几个日径之远，犹能见烛焰？

四、若在高处，请察四周景物之色与貌有何变化。

五、若见树枝交叠之影投成光点，请察其形是否仍如日形。

人人家中多有简易之格致仪器，如寒暑表、风雨表，乃至湿度表。凡以此测得者，皆极可贵。

有通信人论将至之日食云：——「少有人肯思及，若星期六之日食久而不已，日从天上抹去，其后果将如何。格致家谓，不独黑暗之恐怖将笼罩大地，空中水气亦将化为大雨倾注于地，气温骤降至可怖之寒点，竟低至华氏零下一百三十度。大地将成黑暗之薮，荒凉过于北极。如此严寒，物无能活片刻者，犹之沸水中不能呼吸。降温既始，三日之内，凡受造之物皆死，惟存深海中翻滚之巨兽，与穴居地底深处之无目爬虫。念及此事之或有，则今日下午五时三十分许，合城持『熏黑观剧镜』凝望之际，益增其趣。」
text.zh-Hant:
今日日食。本城今日約下午六時食甚，日面十二分之十一為月所掩，就此時而言，天色將異常昏暗，然觀者多半將悵然於所餘日光之多。其暗不及日將落、日輪僅十二分之一尚在地平之上時。食影將漸漸上蔽日輪，下緣依次為所掩。至食甚，日面約十二分之十一暗，所餘未蔽之小邊，乃日輪之上段。食終至日落，約隔十五分鐘。全食帶之外，所可見者較少。縱逢天陰，日光之減亦必顯然，然距全食帶如此之遠，所餘之光仍抵十萬輪滿月。金星或可得見，距日約二十四度，在東南。

非專門觀天者，以尋常觀劇鏡蒙以有色或燻黑之玻璃，即不用觀劇鏡而僅用燻黑玻璃，亦足以觀此奇象之變幻。無儀器亦可作下列觀測：

一、食漸進，宜略測天色昏暗之度。

二、距目幾何，書冊紙張上各號字尚可辨讀？

三、舉點燃之燭，近於目與日之間。距日幾個日徑之遠，猶能見燭焰？

四、若在高處，請察四周景物之色與貌有何變化。

五、若見樹枝交疊之影投成光點，請察其形是否仍如日形。

人人家中多有簡易之格致儀器，如寒暑表、風雨表，乃至濕度表。凡以此測得者，皆極可貴。

有通信人論將至之日食雲：——「少有人肯思及，若星期六之日食久而不已，日從天上抹去，其後果將如何。格致家謂，不獨黑暗之恐怖將籠罩大地，空中水氣亦將化為大雨傾注於地，氣温驟降至可怖之寒點，竟低至華氏零下一百三十度。大地將成黑暗之藪，荒涼過於北極。如此嚴寒，物無能活片刻者，猶之沸水中不能呼吸。降温既始，三日之內，凡受造之物皆死，惟存深海中翻滾之巨獸，與穴居地底深處之無目爬蟲。念及此事之或有，則今日下午五時三十分許，合城持『燻黑觀劇鏡』凝望之際，益增其趣。」
