L'eclissi parziale comincia in questa zona verso le 7:29 A. M., raggiunge il massimo verso le 8:47 A. M. e termina alle 10.14 A. M.
text.ja:
この市の多くの住民は、今年2回目で最後となる日食をひと目見ようと、今朝は早起きするだろう。日食は部分日食として見える。

部分日食はこの付近で午前7時29分ごろに始まり、午前8時47分ごろに最大となり、午前10時14分に終わる。

text_orig: It is horrible to think of; but suppose the eclipse does not come off? Astronomers can calculate the motions of the spheres, but they can't foretell the weather, and it is not at all impossible that the two or three hundred savants who have been running from all parts of the country to the belt of total obscuration, every man of them with a spy-glass under his arm, may see nothing after all but a cloudy sky. A pathetic dispatch reached us last night from Des Moines, where their professors sat helpless before twelve telescopes, feeling pretty certain of rain. They had not seen the sun for two days, and the barometer was in a bad […] way. However, we may console ourselves with the reflection that if clouds cheat us of the promised phenomenon this afternoon, the eclipse will be all the darker for their intervention.

text.zh-Hans: 思之可怖，然设若日食竟不发生，又当如何？天文学家能推算诸天体之运行，却不能预知天气。自各地奔赴全食带之博学之士，二三百人，人人腋下夹一具望远镜，终或所见唯阴云满天，亦非绝无可能。昨夜得一讯，情状可怜，发自得梅因：其地诸教授坐对十二具望远镜，束手无策，颇信必雨。两日不见太阳，气压表亦处于不佳[…]之境。然吾侪可自慰者：若今日午后，云遮而使所预告之天象不得见，则日食将因云之介入而愈暗。
text.zh-Hant: 思之可怖，然設若日食竟不發生，又當如何？天文學家能推算諸天體之運行，卻不能預知天氣。自各地奔赴全食帶之博學之士，二三百人，人人腋下夾一具望遠鏡，終或所見唯陰雲滿天，亦非絕無可能。昨夜得一訊，情狀可憐，發自得梅因：其地諸教授坐對十二具望遠鏡，束手無策，頗信必雨。兩日不見太陽，氣壓表亦處於不佳[…]之境。然吾儕可自慰者：若今日午後，雲遮而使所預告之天象不得見，則日食將因雲之介入而愈暗。
text.en: It is horrible to think of; but suppose the eclipse does not come off? Astronomers can calculate the motions of the spheres, but they can't foretell the weather, and it is not at all impossible that the two or three hundred savants who have been running from all parts of the country to the belt of total obscuration, every man of them with a spy-glass under his arm, may see nothing after all but a cloudy sky. A pathetic dispatch reached us last night from Des Moines, where their professors sat helpless before twelve telescopes, feeling pretty certain of rain. They had not seen the sun for two days, and the barometer was in a bad […] way. However, we may console ourselves with the reflection that if clouds cheat us of the promised phenomenon this afternoon, the eclipse will be all the darker for their intervention.
text.fr: C'est horrible d'y penser ; mais supposons que l'éclipse n'ait pas lieu ? Les astronomes peuvent calculer les mouvements des sphères, mais ils ne peuvent pas prédire le temps qu'il fera, et il n'est pas du tout impossible que les deux ou trois cents savants qui ont couru de toutes les parties du pays vers la bande d'obscuration totale, chacun d'eux avec une lunette sous le bras, ne voient finalement rien qu'un ciel nuageux. Une dépêche pathétique nous est parvenue la nuit dernière de Des Moines, où leurs professeurs étaient assis, impuissants, devant douze télescopes, à peu près certains qu'il pleuvrait. Ils n'avaient pas vu le Soleil depuis deux jours, et le baromètre était en fort mauvais […] état. Toutefois, nous pouvons nous consoler en songeant que si les nuages nous frustrent cet après-midi du phénomène promis, l'éclipse n'en sera que plus sombre par leur intervention.
text.es: Es horrible pensarlo; pero ¿y si el eclipse no se produce? Los astrónomos pueden calcular los movimientos de las esferas, pero no pueden predecir el tiempo, y no es en absoluto imposible que los doscientos o trescientos sabios que han venido corriendo de todas partes del país a la franja del oscurecimiento total, cada uno con un catalejo bajo el brazo, no vean al fin y al cabo nada más que un cielo nublado. Anoche nos llegó un despacho patético desde Des Moines, donde sus profesores estaban sentados, impotentes, ante doce telescopios, bastante seguros de que llovería. No habían visto el Sol en dos días, y el barómetro estaba en mal […] estado. Sin embargo, podemos consolarnos con la reflexión de que, si las nubes nos privan esta tarde del fenómeno prometido, el eclipse será tanto más oscuro por su intervención.
text.it: È orribile pensarci, ma supponiamo che l'eclissi non abbia luogo? Gli astronomi sanno calcolare i moti delle sfere, ma non possono predire il tempo, e non è affatto impossibile che i due o trecento dotti che sono accorsi da ogni parte del paese alla fascia dell'oscuramento totale, ciascuno con un cannocchiale sotto il braccio, non vedano alla fine altro che un cielo nuvoloso. Un patetico dispaccio ci è giunto ieri sera da Des Moines, dove i loro professori sedevano impotenti davanti a dodici telescopi, quasi certi della pioggia. Non vedevano il Sole da due giorni, e il barometro era in una brutta […] situazione. Tuttavia possiamo consolarci con la riflessione che, se le nuvole ci frustrano oggi pomeriggio del fenomeno promesso, l'eclissi sarà tanto più scura per il loro intervento.
text.ja: 考えるだに恐ろしいことだが、日食が起こらなかったらどうだろうか。天文学者は天球の運行を計算できるが、天気を予言することはできない。全国各地から皆既の帯へと駆けつけた二、三百人の学者たち、その一人一人が小脇に望遠鏡を抱えているのに、結局は曇り空のほかに何も見られないということも、決してあり得ないことではない。昨夜、デモインから哀れを誘う報せが私たちのもとに届いた。そこでは教授たちが12台の望遠鏡の前で手も足も出ずに座り込み、雨になるものとかなり確信していた。2日間太陽を見ておらず、気圧計は […] 悪い状態にあった。しかし、今日の午後、雲が約束された現象を私たちから奪ったとしても、雲が間に入ったことで日食はいっそう暗くなるのだと考えて、慰めとすることもできよう。

text_orig:
Eclipse of the Sun.—The total eclipse of the sun occurring this afternoon is the last one which will be visible during the present century in North America. Congress has appropriated $5000 to defray the expenses of observation. A coast-survey party is to be stationed at Springfield, Ill., and Des Moines, Iowa, through which places the line of totality will pass.

The beginning of the eclipse in this county will be a few minutes after 5 o'clock P.M. At the time of the greatest observation about one twelfth only of the sun's dise will be visible. Two hundred and fifty miles south of this the eclipse will be total.

In the Riverside Magazine for August, the characteristic features of such an unusual occurrence are thus stated:

The peculiar gloom which spreads itself, like a pall, over the landscape; the changing tints of the sky, black, orange, indigo, red, sickly yellow, and leaden hues appearing at one and the same time, in different portions of the heavens; the awful approach of the moon's shadow in the air; and lastly, the magnificent circle of light around the eclipsed sun, called the corona, which is compared to the "glory" around the head of a saint, in an old painting. We might add to these the rosy flames frequently seen issuing from the dark limb of the moon, but in reality connected with the solar atmosphere. These flames are often to be seen with the naked eye. During the past year they have been analyzed by the spectroscope, and found to be masses of self-luminous hydrogen. Finally, the larger planets, and some of the principal stars, are occasionally recognized by acute observers during the period of totality, as the gloomiest part of the eclipse is called.

text.zh-Hans:
日食。今日午后之日全食，乃本世纪内北美洲可见之最后一次。国会已拨款五千美元，以充观测之费。海岸测量队将分驻伊利诺伊州斯普林菲尔德与艾奥瓦州得梅因，全食线经此二处。

本县日食始于下午五时过数分。食最深时，日面仅见约十二分之一。此地以南二百五十英里，则为全食。

《河滨杂志》八月号述此等罕见之象，其特征如次：

一种异样之阴霾，如柩衣般覆于大地；天空之色屡变，黑、橙、靛、红、病黄与铅灰诸色，同时见于天之不同部分；月影在空中逼近，令人悚然；终则日被食而四周现一圈壮丽之光，称为日冕，可比古画中圣人头上之「荣光」。更可补述者，月之暗缘常有玫瑰色火焰喷出，实与日之大气相连。此等火焰肉眼往往可见。去年已以分光镜分析，知为自发光之氢气团。末则大行星与若干主要恒星，目力敏锐者有时能于全食期间辨出；所谓全食，即日食最暗之时。
text.zh-Hant:
日食。今日午後之日全食，乃本世紀內北美洲可見之最後一次。國會已撥款五千美元，以充觀測之費。海岸測量隊將分駐伊利諾伊州斯普林菲爾德與艾奧瓦州得梅因，全食線經此二處。

本縣日食始於下午五時過數分。食最深時，日面僅見約十二分之一。此地以南二百五十英里，則為全食。

《河濱雜誌》八月號述此等罕見之象，其特徵如次：

一種異樣之陰霾，如柩衣般覆於大地；天空之色屢變，黑、橙、靛、紅、病黃與鉛灰諸色，同時見於天之不同部分；月影在空中逼近，令人悚然；終則日被食而四周現一圈壯麗之光，稱為日冕，可比古畫中聖人頭上之「榮光」。更可補述者，月之暗緣常有玫瑰色火焰噴出，實與日之大氣相連。此等火焰肉眼往往可見。去年已以分光鏡分析，知為自發光之氫氣團。末則大行星與若干主要恆星，目力敏鋭者有時能於全食期間辨出；所謂全食，即日食最暗之時。
text.en:
Eclipse of the Sun.—The total eclipse of the sun occurring this afternoon is the last one which will be visible during the present century in North America. Congress has appropriated $5000 to defray the expenses of observation. A coast-survey party is to be stationed at Springfield, Ill., and Des Moines, Iowa, through which places the line of totality will pass.

The beginning of the eclipse in this county will be a few minutes after 5 o'clock P.M. At the time of the greatest observation about one twelfth only of the sun's dise will be visible. Two hundred and fifty miles south of this the eclipse will be total.

In the Riverside Magazine for August, the characteristic features of such an unusual occurrence are thus stated:

The peculiar gloom which spreads itself, like a pall, over the landscape; the changing tints of the sky, black, orange, indigo, red, sickly yellow, and leaden hues appearing at one and the same time, in different portions of the heavens; the awful approach of the moon's shadow in the air; and lastly, the magnificent circle of light around the eclipsed sun, called the corona, which is compared to the "glory" around the head of a saint, in an old painting. We might add to these the rosy flames frequently seen issuing from the dark limb of the moon, but in reality connected with the solar atmosphere. These flames are often to be seen with the naked eye. During the past year they have been analyzed by the spectroscope, and found to be masses of self-luminous hydrogen. Finally, the larger planets, and some of the principal stars, are occasionally recognized by acute observers during the period of totality, as the gloomiest part of the eclipse is called.
text.fr:
Éclipse de Soleil. — L'éclipse totale de Soleil qui se produit cet après-midi est la dernière qui sera visible dans le siècle présent en Amérique du Nord. Le Congrès a affecté 5 000 dollars pour couvrir les frais d'observation. Un groupe de la Coast Survey doit être posté à Springfield, Ill., et à Des Moines, Iowa, lieux par lesquels passera la ligne de totalité.

Le commencement de l'éclipse dans ce comté aura lieu quelques minutes après 5 heures de l'après-midi. Au moment de la plus grande obscuration, environ un douzième seulement du disque du Soleil sera visible. À deux cent cinquante milles au sud de là, l'éclipse sera totale.

Dans le Riverside Magazine d'août, les traits caractéristiques d'un événement aussi inhabituel sont ainsi exposés :

La sombre obscurité singulière qui s'étend, comme un drap mortuaire, sur le paysage ; les teintes changeantes du ciel, noires, orange, indigo, rouges, d'un jaune maladif, et des tons plombés apparaissant en même temps, en différentes parties du firmament ; l'approche terrible de l'ombre de la Lune dans l'air ; et enfin, le magnifique cercle de lumière autour du Soleil éclipsé, appelé la couronne, que l'on compare à la « gloire » autour de la tête d'un saint, dans un vieux tableau. Nous pourrions y ajouter les flammes roses que l'on voit fréquemment sortir du bord sombre de la Lune, mais qui en réalité se rattachent à l'atmosphère solaire. Ces flammes sont souvent visibles à l'œil nu. Au cours de l'année passée, elles ont été analysées au spectroscope, et reconnues pour des masses d'hydrogène auto-lumineux. Enfin, les grandes planètes, et quelques-unes des principales étoiles, sont parfois reconnues par des observateurs perspicaces pendant la période de la totalité, ainsi qu'on appelle la partie la plus sombre de l'éclipse.
text.es:
Eclipse de Sol. — El eclipse total de Sol que ocurre esta tarde es el último que será visible durante el presente siglo en Norteamérica. El Congreso ha asignado 5000 dólares para sufragar los gastos de observación. Un grupo del Coast Survey será estacionado en Springfield, Ill., y Des Moines, Iowa, lugares por los que pasará la línea de totalidad.

El comienzo del eclipse en este condado será pocos minutos después de las 5 de la tarde. En el momento de mayor oscurecimiento solo será visible aproximadamente una doceava parte del disco del Sol. A doscientas cincuenta millas al sur de aquí el eclipse será total.

En la Riverside Magazine de agosto, los rasgos característicos de tan insólito suceso se exponen así:

La peculiar penumbra que se extiende, como un paño mortuorio, sobre el paisaje; los matices cambiantes del cielo, con negro, anaranjado, índigo, rojo, amarillo enfermizo y tonos plomizos que aparecen a la vez en distintas partes de los cielos; la terrible aproximación de la sombra de la Luna en el aire; y por último, el magnífico círculo de luz en torno al Sol eclipsado, llamado corona, que se compara con la «gloria» alrededor de la cabeza de un santo en una pintura antigua. Podríamos añadir a estos las llamas rosadas que a menudo se ven brotar del borde oscuro de la Luna, pero que en realidad están ligadas a la atmósfera solar. Estas llamas pueden verse a menudo a simple vista. En el último año han sido analizadas con el espectroscopio, y se ha hallado que son masas de hidrógeno autoluminoso. Por último, los planetas mayores y algunas de las estrellas principales son reconocidos ocasionalmente por observadores agudos durante el período de la totalidad, como se llama a la parte más lúgubre del eclipse.
text.it:
Eclissi di Sole. — L'eclissi totale di Sole che si verifica questo pomeriggio è l'ultima che sarà visibile nel presente secolo in America del Nord. Il Congresso ha stanziato 5000 dollari per coprire le spese di osservazione. Un gruppo del Coast Survey sarà dislocato a Springfield, Ill., e a Des Moines, Iowa, luoghi attraverso cui passerà la linea della totalità.

L'inizio dell'eclissi in questa contea sarà pochi minuti dopo le 5 del pomeriggio. Al momento della massima oscurazione sarà visibile soltanto circa un dodicesimo del disco del Sole. A duecentocinquanta miglia a sud di qui l'eclissi sarà totale.

Nel Riverside Magazine di agosto, i tratti caratteristici di un evento così insolito sono così enunciati:

La particolare cupezza che si stende, come un drappo funebre, sul paesaggio; le tinte mutevoli del cielo, nero, arancione, indaco, rosso, giallo malaticcio e sfumature plumbee che appaiono nello stesso momento in diverse porzioni del cielo; l'angosciante avvicinarsi dell'ombra della Luna nell'aria; e infine il magnifico cerchio di luce attorno al Sole eclissato, detto corona, che è paragonato alla «gloria» attorno al capo di un santo in un antico dipinto. Potremmo aggiungere a questi le fiamme rosate spesso viste uscire dal lembo scuro della Luna, ma in realtà connesse con l'atmosfera solare. Queste fiamme sono spesso visibili a occhio nudo. Durante l'anno passato sono state analizzate con lo spettroscopio, e trovate essere masse di idrogeno autoluminoso. Infine, i pianeti maggiori e alcune delle stelle principali sono occasionalmente riconosciuti da osservatori acuti durante il periodo della totalità, come viene chiamata la parte più cupa dell'eclissi.
text.ja:
日食。今日の午後に起こる皆既日食は、今世紀中に北アメリカで見られる最後のものである。議会は観測の費用を賄うために5000ドルを支出した。沿岸測量隊が、皆既の線が通るイリノイ州スプリングフィールドとアイオワ州デモインに配置される。

この郡での日食の始まりは、午後5時を数分過ぎたころである。食が最大のときには、太陽の円盤の約12分の1しか見えない。ここから南へ250マイルのところでは、日食は皆既となる。

『リバーサイド・マガジン』誌の8月号には、このまれな出来事の特徴的な様相が次のように述べられている。

棺覆いのように風景の上に広がる独特の暗がり。天空のさまざまな部分に同時に現れる、黒、オレンジ、藍、赤、病的な黄色、鉛色という、移ろう空の色合い。空中に迫り来る月の影の恐ろしさ。そして最後に、食された太陽のまわりの壮麗な光の輪、コロナと呼ばれるもので、これは古い絵画の聖人の頭のまわりの「後光」にたとえられる。これらに加えて、月の暗い縁から噴き出すバラ色の炎をしばしば見ることがあるが、これは実際には太陽の大気とつながっている。これらの炎はしばしば肉眼で見える。昨年、それらは分光器で分析され、自ら光る水素の塊であることがわかった。最後に、大きな惑星やいくつかの主要な星が、皆既の間、すなわち日食の最も暗い部分がそう呼ばれる間に、鋭い観察者によってときおり見分けられる。

text_orig:
The eclipse to-day will be visible throughout the whole extent of North America as a partial eclipse, although but a narrow belt of about 140 miles in width, extending from Behring's straits to North Carolina, will be within the limit of the total obscuration of the sun. The partial shadow of the moon first touches the earth in longitude west of Washington 138 degrees and north latitude 37 degrees—just off the east coast of Japan—and the eclipse first becomes total in longitude 165 degrees west from Washington, in north latitude 53 degrees, in Siberia, at sunrise. The shadow then moves forward, advancing at the rate of about 40 miles per minute, until the sun sets to that portion of the globe a short distance east of the coast of North Carolina. The central line of the eclipse passes from the point at which it first becomes visible through Siberia, crossing Behring's straits, and entering this continent, passing through Alaska, British America, Montana, Dacota, Nebraska, Iowa, Missouri, Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Tennessee, Virginia, North Carolina and a portion of the Atlantic ocean.

Observations will be made at many points along the central line of the eclipse, commencing with the United States Naval Observatory expedition of Professor Hall at Alaska, and ending with the Coast Survey expedition on the coast of North Carolina. Observations of a scientific character will be made at most of the following places within the line of total obscuration: Iowa—Sioux City, Boonesboro, Des Moines, Cedar Rapids, Iowa City, Muscatine, Burlington, Keokuk; Illinois—Rock Island, Peoria, Bloomington, Quincy, Springfield, Alton; Indiana—Terra Haute, Vincennes, Columbus, Madison, Evansville; Kentucky—Louisville, Shelbyville, Frankfort, Lexington, Bardstown, Somerset, Danville, Abington; Tennessee—Greenville, Knoxville.

The duration of totality at these points varies according to their distance from the central line from seven seconds at Alton to two minutes nine seconds at Des Moines, and the eclipse lasts about two hours at any point. At Washington the eclipse will begin at 5h. 2m. 23s., and last an hour and fifty minutes, nearly nineteen-twentieths of the sun's disk being obscured at its middle.

A quiet, elevated position, free from smoke, should be selected where there is little noise and nothing to detract the attention of those wishing to make careful observations. (We trust this hint will have the effect to keep the curious from the observatory or other […] stead of smoking the glass irregularly to allow a choice of opacity in different parts, the observer should smoke several pieces to different extents, but each as uniformly as possible over its entire surface, and choose as necessary among the several pieces. Every one should avoid the use of pieces which have been scratched or touched by the finger so as to remove the opaque covering at any points; the observer should avoid also a single flash of untempered sunlight upon the retina, and particularly the repetition of such flashes or irritating conditions as would result from the use of a scratched or very unequally smoked plate. And especially should every one avoid fatiguing the eyes by looking too long or too often in advance. Let the glasses be prepared, if possible, the day before and the eyes held at ease observing the deepening gloom in the general landscape, with merely occasional glances, until near the period of the greatest obscuration. Those who have reason to believe themselves troubled with a tendency to weak eyes should be the more careful to observe these precautions. Those whose scientific observations on the eclipse may be of value are alone justified in risking any permanent or even serious temporary injury to these extremely delicate organs."

There are some facts which can be noticed by all, leaving to experts to report the result of exact scientific inquiry. The following are suggested by Col. Carrington, United States army, in a letter to the Cincinnati Courier:

1. The changes of foliage in color, and the effects upon plants and the general face of nature.

De LaRue (eclipse of 1742) says: "Terrestrial objects take, by degrees, a livid hue. Orange, yellow, vinous-red and copper-tints give to the landscape a singular appearance, which, joined to a very perceptible lowering of temperature, produce a profound impression on all animated beings. In 1860, in Algeria, Mr. Lausudat notes this fact." In spite of the short duration of totality, daturas, convolvoli, poppies and night shades, which had been closely shut, were observed to half open during the total eclipse. Halley, (1815,) Helper, (1590,) Ferrer, (1806,) and Piola (1842) unite in similar testimony as to the extraordinary effect upon all natural objects, and describe the tints as peculiar, strange, solemn and impressive. "At Campden Hill," says Teighmouth, "the crocus closed, and its color changed to the pink hepatica."

Mr. Hind, at Ravelsburg, (1851,) says: "All nature seemed to be overshadowed by an unnatural gloom. The distant hills were hardly visible, the sea turned lurid red, and persons standing near the observer had a pale, livid look, calculated to produce the most painful sensations."

2. The conduct of domestic animals.

At Engelholm, 1851, animals were strangely affected: "Cocks crowed at Elsinburg, though the sun was hidden but thirty seconds, and the birds sought their resting places, as if night had come on."

Mr. Glaiser, 1851, says: "The wet bulb thermometer read 2° 6' less; the rooks flew homeward; small birds flew wildly about; the larks ceased to rise and did not sing, and starlings took flight, whole flocks, together. At Greenwich Park, a thrush commenced his evening song. At Grantham pigeons returned to their cotes."

Dr. Martin notes the fact that at Venton "a fish confined in an aquarium and ordinarily visible at night only, was in full activity at the period of greatest gloom."

3. The appearance of stars.

Venus, Mercury, Jupiter, Mars, and Saturn, as well as stars even of the second magnitude, were observed by Airy, Carrington, Dawes, Hinds, Stevenson, Williams, Bruhm, and Feilitzsch. Hinds also noted Regulus, Procyon, Pollux, Capella, and Arcurus.

In 1851, at Dantzic, Venus continued in view ten minutes after the sun had reappeared.

4. The test of obscurity, by a newspaper or watch dial, held at arms length.

The impression on the mind can be determined by comparison with the darkness occasioned during the period of a heavy thunder storm, or the ordinary light of the full moon. Frequently candles have been required in order to record observations or read the instruments.

5. The change in the moon from the usual form of a dish to that of an obvious sphere.

6. The appearance of mountains or other inequalities in the moon, particularly, whether its outline be rough and jagged.

Vassenius, in 1733, and Ferrer, in 1806, unite in particular mention of such appearances, and of "bead like objects" standing out upon the sun disc, just before full immersion.

7. The corona of light formed at the instant of complete shadow.

This is described by Soomer, Airy, Chambers, Hinds and others, in contributing to the Royal Society, as "a great glory," like that emanating from the heads of saints in the pictures of great masters, but transcendantly beyond the range of art to paint, or the scope of language to describe.

8. The "red flames" from the surface of the sun.

De La Rue (1860) estimated one "to be 44,000 miles in vertical height above the sun's surface," and they have been observed by the naked eye.

Stannyan (1706) says of the sun: "His getting out of the eclipse was preceded by blood-red streaks of light from its left band."

M. Bruhn, Leipsic, says "flaming rays could be discerned, of a light rose color."

Although these suggestions are made in view of the observer being within the line of the total eclipse, they will be read with interest by those near the line and many of the phenomena noticed. Few persons, now adults, will ever see another total eclipse of the sun. If they will see all they possibly can of this, the scientific records which will be made public, will be of additional interest, and make clear to their minds the application of principles to the facts they remember.

While this event is engrossing the attention of the whole world, taking the firmest hold upon the wisest and greatest minds of the age, with millions gazing upon the spectacle with awe and wonder, it should induce us to attempt a comprehension of the insignificance of ourselves, our nation, age, country, world, as compared with the universe; and inspire us with adoration of the Great Founder and Builder of that universal system whose law is harmony and peace. If the solemn grandeur of this rare celestial event could enable us to grasp an idea of the greatness of Him who created the sun, moon and stars, we should acquire a knowledge far greater than that afforded by the most successful scientific observations.

text.zh-Hans:
今日之食，全北美洲皆可见偏食，惟全食之带仅宽约一百四十英里，自白令海峡延至北卡罗来纳。月之半影首触地球，在华盛顿以西一百三十八度、北纬三十七度——正当日本东岸之外；食于华盛顿以西一百六十五度、北纬五十三度处的西伯利亚，日出时始成全食。影随后前行，每分钟约四十英里，直至地球该部分日落，其处在北卡罗来纳海岸以东不远。食之中心线自初见之点经西伯利亚，越白令海峡，入此大陆，历阿拉斯加、英属美洲、蒙大拿、达科他、内布拉斯加、艾奥瓦、密苏里、伊利诺伊、印第安纳、肯塔基、田纳西、弗吉尼亚、北卡罗来纳及大西洋一隅。

沿食之中心线多处将作观测，始于美国海军天文台 Hall 教授赴阿拉斯加之远征队，终于北卡罗来纳海岸之海岸测量局远征队。全食线内下列诸地，多数将作科学性质之观测：艾奥瓦——Sioux City、布恩斯伯勒、得梅因、Cedar Rapids、Iowa City、Muscatine、伯灵顿、Keokuk；伊利诺伊——罗克艾兰、Peoria、Bloomington、昆西、斯普林菲尔德、Alton；印第安纳——Terre Haute、文森斯、哥伦布、麦迪逊、埃文斯维尔；肯塔基——路易斯维尔、谢尔比维尔、Frankfort、列克星敦、Bardstown、Somerset、丹维尔、Abington；田纳西——Greenville、诺克斯维尔。

全食之久暂，视各地距中心线之远近而异，自 Alton 之七秒至得梅因之二分九秒不等，任一处食皆历约两小时。华盛顿之食将始于五时二分二十三秒，历一小时五十分，至食最深时，日面几有二十分之十九被掩。

当择清静高敞、无烟无嚣、无物分心之处，供欲细心观测者所用。（吾侪盼此提示能使好奇之人不致涌入天文台或其他[…]「与其将玻璃熏得参差不齐，以求各部浓淡可择，观测者宜熏数片，浓淡各异，而每片尽量遍体均匀，临时就数片中择其所需。人人皆当避用曾被刮划或以指触碰、致某处遮光之层脱落之玻璃片；观测者亦当避免未经减弱之日光一闪射入视网膜，尤忌此类闪射之反复，或用划伤、熏得极不均之玻璃板所致之刺目情形。尤当避免预先看得过久过频而疲目。玻璃宜于前一日备妥，目则放松，观察大地景物渐深之阴暗，仅偶尔瞥日，直至近食最深之时。自觉易患目弱者，尤宜谨守此诸项。惟科学观测于食或有价值者，方可冒永久乃至严重暂时之伤，以损此极娇弱之器官。」

另有若干事实人人可察，精确科学考察之结果，留待专家报告。以下数端，系美国陆军 Carrington 上校致《辛辛那提信使报》函中所建议：

一、树叶颜色之变，及草木与大自然总貌所受之影响。

De LaRue（一七四二年之食）谓：「地上诸物渐现铅青之色。橙、黄、酒红与铜色，使景物呈奇异之观，加以气温明显下降，对一切有生之物皆生深刻之印象。一八六〇年，在阿尔及利亚，Lausudat 先生记有此事。」尽管全食历时甚短，原先紧闭之曼陀罗、旋花、罂粟与茄科植物，于全食期间见其半开。Halley（一八一五年）、Helper（一五九〇年）、Ferrer（一八〇六年）与 Piola（一八四二年）所述略同，皆谓一切自然物所受影响非凡，并称色调奇特、怪异、庄严而动人。Teighmouth 谓：「在 Campden Hill，番红花合拢，色变为粉红之獐耳细辛。」

Hind 先生于 Ravelsburg（一八五一年）谓：「万物似皆笼罩于不祥之阴郁。远山几不可见，海变为凄红色，立于观测者近旁之人面色苍白铅青，足以引起最难受之感觉。」

二、家畜之举动。

一八五一年在 Engelholm，动物所受影响甚奇：「Elsinburg 雄鸡啼鸣，虽日隐仅三十秒，鸟亦归栖，如夜之已临。」

Glaiser 先生一八五一年谓：「湿球温度表降二度六分；白嘴鸦飞归；小鸟乱飞；云雀不复升空，亦不鸣；椋鸟整群同时飞起。在 Greenwich Park，有鸫开始唱晚歌。在 Grantham，鸽归巢。」

Martin 博士记一事：在 Venton，「一鱼囚于水族箱，平日唯夜间可见，于最暗之时极为活跃。」

三、星之出现。

金星、水星、木星、火星、土星，以及二等星，Airy、Carrington、Dawes、Hinds、Stevenson、Williams、Bruhm 与 Feilitzsch 皆曾目睹。Hinds 又记有轩辕十四、Procyon、Pollux、Capella 与 Arcturus．一八五一年在 Dantzic，日重现后，金星仍可见十分钟。

四、以报纸或表盘持于臂长之处，试其暗度。

此印象可与大雷雨之时的暗，或寻常满月之光相较而定。往往须点烛，方能记录观测或读仪器。

五、月形自常见之盘状，变为显然之球状。

六、月上山岳或他种凹凸之状，尤其是其轮廓是否粗糙参差。

Vassenius（一七三三年）与 Ferrer（一八〇六年）皆特别述及此类景象，又述日轮将全没前，日面上有「珠状之物」凸出。

七、全影一刹那所成之光冕。

Soomer、Airy、Chambers、Hinds 诸人投稿皇家学会，皆称此为「大荣光」，如名家画中圣人头上所发之光，而其美超乎笔绘之所及、言语之所能状。

八、日面之「红焰」。

De La Rue（一八六〇年）估计一焰「在日面之上垂直高四万四千英里」，且肉眼亦曾得见。

Stannyan（一七〇六年）述日：「其复出于食，先有血红光条自其左缘见。」

Leipsic 之 M. Bruhn 谓：「可辨火焰般之光线，色淡玫瑰。」

此类建议虽为身在全食线内之观测者而设，近线之人读来亦必有味，因许多现象亦可得见。今之成人，鲜有能再见日全食者。若能尽其所能多观此次之食，则日后公布之科学记录将更添兴味，并使人心中明白诸原理如何应用于所记忆之事实。

此事正占全世界之注意，最牢地攫住当世最智最伟者之心，以百万计之人惊叹仰视此景之际，当使吾人试图领悟吾人自身、国家、时代、乡土、世界较之宇宙何其渺小，并使吾人生起对宇宙体系之伟大创立者与营造者之敬仰，此体系之律乃和谐与平安。若此稀有天象之庄严壮丽，能使吾人略悟造日月星辰者之伟大，则所得之知，将远胜于最成功之科学观测所予。

一、樹葉顏色之變，及草木與大自然總貌所受之影響。

此印象可與大雷雨之時的暗，或尋常滿月之光相較而定。往往須點燭，方能記錄觀測或讀儀器。

五、月形自常見之盤狀，變為顯然之球狀。
