text.fr:
L'éclipse eut lieu samedi dernier dans l'après-midi, selon l'arrangement antérieur, et fut tout ce que les almanachs et les journaux avaient prédit qu'elle serait. Les circonstances étaient favorables — pas un nuage dans le ciel.

IGNIS.
text.es:
El eclipse tuvo lugar el sábado pasado por la tarde según lo previsto, y fue todo lo que los almanaques y los periódicos predijeron que sería. Las circunstancias fueron favorables — ni una nube en el cielo.

IGNIS.
text.it:
L'eclissi si è svolta sabato scorso nel pomeriggio secondo l'accordo precedente, ed è stata tutto ciò che gli almanacchi e i giornali avevano previsto. Le circostanze erano favorevoli — non una nuvola nel cielo.

IGNIS.
text.ja:
日食は先週の土曜日の午後、前々からの取り決めどおりに起こり、暦や新聞が予言したとおりのものであった。状況は良好であった—空には雲ひとつなかった。

イグニス。

text_orig: This grand astronomical event came off according to the previously announced programme, and justified and verified scientific prognostication. An unclouded sky propitiously favored observations, and made the business a very interesting one from about five o'clock until near sunset. It may be truthfully put down as a perfect success in the line of exhibitions. It came off promptly upon time, and when it got through it was done, and nobody was vexed and tired with the bad taste often exhibited of an undue continuance. During its greatest obscuration a strange shadowy pallor of light overspread the earth, and gave to the countenance the hue and aspect of death. This fact imparted to it a feeling of awe, but was not of sufficient intensity or duration to make it perceptibly profitable and salutary upon Democratic ignorance or obduracy, so that the abandonment of the error of their ways may not be classed as among the fruits of this unusual event. Though this may cause some Republican disappointment, it could not be helped. At Raleigh, North Carolina, the eclipse was total. This was the nearest point of totality to us, but the belt of about one hundred and fifty miles extended across our continent from Alaska to Alabama. The rest of the world had nothing to do with it, for the reason, perhaps, that such a panoramic show could not have been gotten up anywhere else, if, indeed, it could have been adequately appreciated. If there was any mistake about the matter, it was, we think, that the chief point of obscuration was not at Jefferson, that the full effect of its awe and grandeur might have been there produced, and the power of the editor of the Sentinel, as the local divinity and spiritual afflatus of the place, might have been shown to its best advantage, and the editor of the Telegraph permitted to take personal cognizance of the dignity and potency of the phenomena.

text.zh-Hans: 此天文盛事依先前所布之程式而来，证验科学之预言。晴空无云，利于观测，自约五时至近日落，其事甚饶趣味。就各类展演而论，可谓大获成功，不虚。准时而来，既毕即毕，无人为常见之无谓拖延之恶趣所烦倦。食甚之际，一种奇异幽暗之苍白光色遍布大地，令人面呈死色死相。此象由是带敬畏之感，然强度与久暂不足，不能明显开导民主党人之愚昧或顽固，故其改弃谬途，不得列于此异事之成果。此虽或令共和党人略感失望，亦无可奈何。北卡罗来纳州 Raleigh，日食为全食。此为距吾侪最近之全食处，然宽约一百五十英里之带，横贯吾洲，自阿拉斯加至阿拉巴马。世界其余各处与之无涉，或因如此全景之盛演，别处办不成，纵办成，亦未必能得充分赏识。若此事有何差错，吾侪以为，在于食之主要处不在杰斐逊；设在彼处，则其敬畏与壮观之全效可得而生，而《哨兵报》主笔，作该地之地方神明与灵感，亦可尽显其威，且使《电讯报》主笔得亲验此象之威严与能力。
text.zh-Hant: 此天文盛事依先前所佈之程式而來，證驗科學之預言。晴空無雲，利於觀測，自約五時至近日落，其事甚饒趣味。就各類展演而論，可謂大獲成功，不虛。準時而來，既畢即畢，無人為常見之無謂拖延之惡趣所煩倦。食甚之際，一種奇異幽暗之蒼白光色遍佈大地，令人面呈死色死相。此象由是帶敬畏之感，然強度與久暫不足，不能明顯開導民主黨人之愚昧或頑固，故其改棄謬途，不得列於此異事之成果。此雖或令共和黨人略感失望，亦無可奈何。北卡羅來納州 Raleigh，日食為全食。此為距吾儕最近之全食處，然寬約一百五十英里之帶，橫貫吾洲，自阿拉斯加至阿拉巴馬。世界其餘各處與之無涉，或因如此全景之盛演，別處辦不成，縱辦成，亦未必能得充分賞識。若此事有何差錯，吾儕以為，在於食之主要處不在傑佛遜；設在彼處，則其敬畏與壯觀之全效可得而生，而《哨兵報》主筆，作該地之地方神明與靈感，亦可盡顯其威，且使《電訊報》主筆得親驗此象之威嚴與能力。
text.en: This grand astronomical event came off according to the previously announced programme, and justified and verified scientific prognostication. An unclouded sky propitiously favored observations, and made the business a very interesting one from about five o'clock until near sunset. It may be truthfully put down as a perfect success in the line of exhibitions. It came off promptly upon time, and when it got through it was done, and nobody was vexed and tired with the bad taste often exhibited of an undue continuance. During its greatest obscuration a strange shadowy pallor of light overspread the earth, and gave to the countenance the hue and aspect of death. This fact imparted to it a feeling of awe, but was not of sufficient intensity or duration to make it perceptibly profitable and salutary upon Democratic ignorance or obduracy, so that the abandonment of the error of their ways may not be classed as among the fruits of this unusual event. Though this may cause some Republican disappointment, it could not be helped. At Raleigh, North Carolina, the eclipse was total. This was the nearest point of totality to us, but the belt of about one hundred and fifty miles extended across our continent from Alaska to Alabama. The rest of the world had nothing to do with it, for the reason, perhaps, that such a panoramic show could not have been gotten up anywhere else, if, indeed, it could have been adequately appreciated. If there was any mistake about the matter, it was, we think, that the chief point of obscuration was not at Jefferson, that the full effect of its awe and grandeur might have been there produced, and the power of the editor of the Sentinel, as the local divinity and spiritual afflatus of the place, might have been shown to its best advantage, and the editor of the Telegraph permitted to take personal cognizance of the dignity and potency of the phenomena.
text.fr: Ce grand événement astronomique eut lieu conformément au programme annoncé d'avance, et justifia et vérifia les pronostics de la science. Un ciel sans nuages favorisa heureusement les observations et rendit l'affaire fort intéressante depuis environ cinq heures jusque près du coucher du soleil. On peut dire en toute vérité que ce fut un parfait succès dans le genre des exhibitions. Il se produisit ponctuellement à l'heure, et quand il fut terminé, il fut terminé, et personne ne fut importuné ni fatigué par le mauvais goût dont on fait souvent preuve en le prolongeant indûment. Pendant sa plus grande obscuration, une étrange pâleur ombreuse de lumière se répandit sur la terre et donna aux visages la teinte et l'aspect de la mort. Ce fait lui communiqua un sentiment de crainte respectueuse, mais n'eut ni l'intensité ni la durée suffisantes pour se révéler perceptiblement profitable et salutaire à l'ignorance ou à l'obstination démocrates, de sorte que l'abandon de l'erreur de leurs voies ne saurait être classé parmi les fruits de ce phénomène inhabituel. Si cela peut causer quelque déception aux républicains, on n'y pouvait rien. À Raleigh, en Caroline du Nord, l'éclipse fut totale. C'était le point de totalité le plus proche de nous, mais la bande, large d'environ cent cinquante milles, traversait notre continent, de l'Alaska à l'Alabama. Le reste du monde n'y eut aucune part, peut-être parce qu'un tel spectacle panoramique n'aurait pu être monté ailleurs, si tant est qu'il eût pu y être dûment apprécié. S'il y eut quelque erreur en la matière, ce fut, pensons-nous, que le point principal d'obscuration ne se trouvât pas à Jefferson, afin que l'effet complet de sa majesté et de sa grandeur y fût produit, que le pouvoir du rédacteur du Sentinel, divinité locale et souffle spirituel du lieu, pût y être montré à son meilleur avantage, et que le rédacteur du Telegraph pût prendre connaissance personnelle de la dignité et de la puissance du phénomène.
text.es: Este gran acontecimiento astronómico se produjo conforme al programa anunciado de antemano, y justificó y confirmó el pronóstico científico. Un cielo sin nubes favoreció propicio las observaciones e hizo del asunto uno muy interesante desde alrededor de las cinco hasta casi la puesta de sol. Con verdad puede anotarse como un éxito perfecto en materia de espectáculos. Llegó puntualmente a su hora, y cuando terminó, terminó, y nadie se sintió molesto y cansado por el mal gusto, tantas veces exhibido, de una prolongación indebida. Durante su mayor oscurecimiento, una extraña palidez sombría de luz se extendió sobre la tierra y dio al rostro el color y el aspecto de la muerte. Este hecho le infundió una sensación de temor reverencial, pero no tuvo intensidad ni duración suficientes para resultar perceptiblemente provechoso y saludable para la ignorancia o la obstinación demócratas, de modo que el abandono del error de sus caminos no puede contarse entre los frutos de este suceso insólito. Aunque esto pueda causar cierta decepción a los republicanos, no se pudo evitar. En Raleigh, Carolina del Norte, el eclipse fue total. Era el punto de totalidad más cercano a nosotros, pero la franja de unas ciento cincuenta millas se extendía por todo nuestro continente, desde Alaska hasta Alabama. El resto del mundo no tuvo nada que ver con él, quizá por la razón de que un espectáculo panorámico semejante no habría podido montarse en ningún otro lugar, si es que, en verdad, habría podido apreciarse como se debía. Si hubo algún error en el asunto, fue, a nuestro juicio, que el punto principal de oscurecimiento no estuviera en Jefferson, para que allí se hubiera producido todo el efecto de su temor reverencial y su grandeza, y se hubiera mostrado en su mejor luz el poder del director del Sentinel, como divinidad local y numen espiritual del lugar, y se hubiera permitido al director del Telegraph tomar conocimiento personal de la dignidad y la potencia de los fenómenos.
text.it: Questo grande avvenimento astronomico si svolse secondo il programma annunciato in precedenza, e giustificò e confermò la previsione scientifica. Un cielo senza nubi favorì propizio le osservazioni e rese la faccenda assai interessante dalle cinque circa fino quasi al tramonto. Si può dire con tutta verità che fu un perfetto successo nel genere degli spettacoli. Si svolse puntualmente all'ora stabilita e, quando ebbe finito, fu finita, e nessuno fu irritato e stancato dal cattivo gusto, spesso mostrato, di una durata eccessiva. Durante la sua massima oscurazione uno strano pallore ombroso di luce si stese sulla terra e conferì ai volti il colore e l'aspetto della morte. Questo fatto gli diede un senso di soggezione, ma non di intensità o durata sufficiente da renderlo percettibilmente utile e salutare per l'ignoranza o l'ostinazione dei Democratici, cosicché l'abbandono dell'errore delle loro vie non può essere annoverato fra i frutti di questo insolito avvenimento. Sebbene ciò possa causare una certa delusione fra i Repubblicani, non ci si poteva fare nulla. A Raleigh, nella Carolina del Nord, l'eclissi fu totale. Era il punto di totalità più vicino a noi, ma la fascia di circa centocinquanta miglia si estese attraverso il nostro continente dall'Alaska all'Alabama. Il resto del mondo non ebbe nulla a che fare con essa, forse perché uno spettacolo panoramico di tal genere non avrebbe potuto essere allestito in nessun altro luogo, ammesso che vi si potesse davvero apprezzarlo adeguatamente. Se vi fu qualche errore in questa faccenda, fu, pensiamo, che il punto principale di oscurazione non fosse a Jefferson, dove si sarebbe potuto produrre il pieno effetto del suo timore reverenziale e della sua grandiosità, e il potere del direttore del Sentinel, quale divinità locale e afflato spirituale del luogo, avrebbe potuto mostrarsi nel suo migliore vantaggio, e al direttore del Telegraph sarebbe stato permesso di prendere personale cognizione della dignità e della potenza del fenomeno.
text.ja: この壮大な天文の出来事は、あらかじめ告知されていたプログラムどおりに起こり、科学的な予測の正しさを裏づけ、立証した。雲一つない空が観測に幸いし、5時ごろから日没近くまで、この催しはたいへん興味深いものとなった。見世物としては申し分のない成功であったと、偽りなく記しておいてよい。時間どおりに始まり、終わったときにはすっかり済んでおり、だらだらと長引くというよく見られる悪趣味のために、誰かが苛立ったり疲れたりすることもなかった。最も暗くなった間、不思議な影のような青白い光が大地を覆い、人の顔に死の色と死の様相を与えた。このことはそれに畏怖の感を添えたが、その強さも長さも、民主党員の無知や頑迷に目に見えて益となり薬となるには足りなかったので、彼らが誤った道を捨てることは、この珍しい出来事の成果の一つには数えられないであろう。これは共和党員をいくらか失望させるかもしれないが、どうしようもなかった。ノースカロライナ州ローリーでは、日食は皆既であった。ここは私たちに最も近い皆既の地点であったが、約150マイルの帯が、アラスカからアラバマまで我が大陸を横切って延びていた。世界のほかの地域はこれとは無関係であった。おそらく、これほどのパノラマ的な見世物はほかのどこでも仕立てられなかったであろうし、そもそも十分に鑑賞されることができたかどうかも怪しいからである。もしこの件に何か手違いがあったとすれば、私たちの考えでは、最も暗くなる主要な地点がジェファーソンでなかったことである。そこであれば、その畏怖と壮大さの十全な効果が生じ得たであろうし、土地の守護神にして霊感の源である『センチネル』紙の編集者の力が最大限に示され、『テレグラフ』紙の編集者もこの現象の威厳と威力をみずから目の当たりにすることを許されたであろう。

text_orig: The Eclipse (Not Eclypse) came off in this city per announcement, and was witnessed by a large and attentive audience. It first became visible to close scrutinizers, with well prepared singed glasses, about 4 p. m., and by half past four was visible to the naked eye, though it did not become full until about five. Our streets and alleys presented a sight decidedly novel during the hour from 4:30 to 5:30. "Old men and maidens," Grandmas and six year old urchins, were alike intent looking "through glass darkly" to view the wonderful phenomenon. Over strained eyes dripped profuse tears that they could see no more, and aching necks assumed erect positions with much regret when the curtain fell over the great show give[…] by nature—when the dark shadow of the moon withdrew from across the face of the sun. The weather was propitious, and as the eclipse was well advertised, the people attended en masse, and made it a grand success.

text.zh-Hans: 日食（非 Eclypse）依预告而行于此城，观者众而专注。约午后四时，持备好之熏玻璃细察者始得见食；四时半，肉眼可见，然至五时许方达极盛。自四时三十分至五时三十分之一小时间，吾城街巷现一奇景。「老者与处子」，祖母与六岁顽童，同心「隔玻璃，暗然」观此奇象。劳目泪流不止，因不能再见；酸颈极不情愿地直起，及帷幕落于自然所[…]之大戏——月之黑影自日面退去之际。天气适宜，日食又预告充分，众人倾城而至，大获成功。
text.zh-Hant: 日食（非 Eclypse）依預告而行於此城，觀者眾而專注。約午後四時，持備好之燻玻璃細察者始得見食；四時半，肉眼可見，然至五時許方達極盛。自四時三十分至五時三十分之一小時間，吾城街巷現一奇景。「老者與處子」，祖母與六歲頑童，同心「隔玻璃，闇然」觀此奇象。勞目淚流不止，因不能再見；酸頸極不情願地直起，及帷幕落於自然所[…]之大戲——月之黑影自日面退去之際。天氣適宜，日食又預告充分，眾人傾城而至，大獲成功。
text.en: The Eclipse (Not Eclypse) came off in this city per announcement, and was witnessed by a large and attentive audience. It first became visible to close scrutinizers, with well prepared singed glasses, about 4 p. m., and by half past four was visible to the naked eye, though it did not become full until about five. Our streets and alleys presented a sight decidedly novel during the hour from 4:30 to 5:30. "Old men and maidens," Grandmas and six year old urchins, were alike intent looking "through glass darkly" to view the wonderful phenomenon. Over strained eyes dripped profuse tears that they could see no more, and aching necks assumed erect positions with much regret when the curtain fell over the great show give[…] by nature—when the dark shadow of the moon withdrew from across the face of the sun. The weather was propitious, and as the eclipse was well advertised, the people attended en masse, and made it a grand success.
text.fr: L'Éclipse (non Éclypse) a eu lieu dans cette ville selon l'annonce, et a été observée par un public nombreux et attentif. Elle devint d'abord visible, pour ceux qui scrutaient de près avec des verres enfumés bien préparés, vers 4 heures de l'après-midi, et à 4 heures et demie elle était visible à l'œil nu, bien qu'elle ne fût complète que vers 5 heures. Nos rues et nos ruelles offrirent un spectacle résolument nouveau pendant l'heure de 4:30 à 5:30. « Vieillards et jeunes filles », grands-mères et gamins de six ans, regardaient tous avec la même application « à travers un verre, obscurément » pour voir le phénomène merveilleux. Sur des yeux fatigués coulaient d'abondantes larmes de ne plus pouvoir rien voir, et des nuques endolories reprirent avec beaucoup de regret une position droite quand le rideau tomba sur le grand spectacle donné[…] par la nature — quand l'ombre noire de la Lune se retira de la face du Soleil. Le temps était propice, et comme l'éclipse avait été bien annoncée, les gens s'y rendirent en masse, et en firent un grand succès.
text.es: El Eclipse (no Eclypse) se produjo en esta ciudad según lo anunciado, y fue presenciado por un público numeroso y atento. Se hizo visible primero para los observadores minuciosos, con cristales chamuscados bien preparados, hacia las 4 p. m., y a las cuatro y media era visible a simple vista, aunque no llegó a su plenitud hasta cerca de las cinco. Nuestras calles y callejones presentaron un espectáculo decididamente novedoso durante la hora de 4:30 a 5:30. «Ancianos y doncellas», abuelas y chiquillos de seis años, miraban todos con igual empeño «a través de un cristal, oscuramente» el maravilloso fenómeno. Sobre los ojos fatigados corrían abundantes lágrimas porque ya no podían ver más, y los cuellos doloridos recobraron la posición erguida con mucho pesar cuando cayó el telón sobre el gran espectáculo dad[…] por la naturaleza — cuando la oscura sombra de la Luna se retiró del rostro del Sol. El tiempo fue propicio, y como el eclipse estaba bien anunciado, la gente acudió en masa y lo convirtió en un gran éxito.
text.it: L'eclissi (non Eclypse) ha avuto luogo in questa città come annunciato, ed è stata vista da un pubblico numeroso e attento. È diventata visibile per la prima volta a chi osservava con attenzione, con vetri affumicati ben preparati, verso le 4 p. m., e alle 4 e mezza era visibile a occhio nudo, anche se non è diventata piena fino alle 5 circa. Le nostre strade e i nostri vicoli offrivano uno spettacolo decisamente nuovo durante l'ora dalle 4:30 alle 5:30. «Vecchi e fanciulle», nonne e monelli di sei anni, guardavano tutti con uguale attenzione «attraverso un vetro, oscuramente» per vedere il meraviglioso fenomeno. Sugli occhi affaticati colavano copiose lacrime perché non potevano vedere di più, e i colli doloranti hanno assunto posizioni erette con molto rimpianto quando è calato il sipario sul grande spettacolo dato[…] dalla natura—quando l'ombra scura della Luna si è ritirata dalla faccia del Sole. Il tempo era propizio, e poiché l'eclissi era stata ben pubblicizzata, la gente è accorsa in massa e ne ha fatto un grande successo.
text.ja: 日食（日蝕ではない）は、予告どおりこの市で行われ、大勢の注意深い観衆に見守られた。よく用意した焦がしたガラスを持つ綿密な観察者には、4時ごろに最初に見えるようになり、4時半には肉眼でも見えたが、満ちたのは5時ごろであった。4時30分から5時30分までの1時間、我々の街路と路地は、まったく新奇な光景を呈した。「老人と乙女」、祖母たちと6歳の腕白小僧が、同じように熱心に「ガラスを通しておぼろに」眺め、この驚くべき現象を見ようとしていた。酷使された目からは、もう見えなくなったために、涙がたっぷり滴り落ち、痛む首は、自然が与[…]大きな見世物の幕が下りるとき—月の黒い影が太陽の面を横切って去るとき—、たいへん名残惜しげに直立の姿勢に戻った。天気は好都合で、日食はよく宣伝されていたので、人々は大挙して詰めかけ、大成功とした。

text_orig:
The Eclipse of the Sun on Saturday last proved a success, and on time to a dot. Smoked glass was in demand and spectators numerous. The next Eclipse will take place in the year 1900.

The eclipse of the Sun at this place begun at 4 minutes past 5 and ended at 10 minutes of 7 o'clock, making 1 hour and 46 minutes for the whole time. The central time and eleven twelfths obscured at 3 minutes of 6 o'clock, by the Court house time. The sun in its daily revolution about the earth overtook the moon in its daily revolution from east to west, and passed the latter body in the exact time of 1 hour and 46 minutes. The fact that the earth is the centre of the universe and not the sun has in this case been demonstrated on a large and comprehensive scale; while the earth revolves from west to east 22½ degrees south and marks the ecliptic line round its own body.

This great and occular demonstration between the heavenly bodies and the earth, which was witnessed by thousands and and tens of thousands closes up the artificial, or copernican system. By this mighty demonstration we learn that the sun is only 7200 miles in diameter; that it makes a daily revolution vertical at the equator at a distance of 432,000 miles from east to west, and passes the moon once in 29 days, 12 hours, 43 minutes and 51 501—669 seconds, precisely. This constitutes the synodical period, from which all the eclipses are recorded in time. The moon is 3600 miles in diameter and revolves from east to west about the earth daily, but falls back from the sun about 48 minutes and 45 seconds, at a distance of 216,000 miles, from the surface of the ear[…]h. By a very accurate calculation the radius line of the universe is only 1.728,000 miles, and the circumference of the inner concave surface of the rational heavens, only 10,800,000 miles. This being the boundary lines of the rational creation, there is no room for the sizes and distances of the heavenly bodies, as taught by the Copernicans, in all God's creation. Even the fixed stars are measured by thousands of miles instead of by millions and trillions of miles. By the transit of Venus in 1769, on the 3rd of June, at the Island of Otah[…]ati, it was determined that the distance to the sun was 95,000,000 of English miles. But the whole calculation was founded on the supposition that Venus did make an elipticle orbit about the sun in 224 days 16 hours and 48 minutes. When in reality Venus make a daily revolution about the earth from east to west in 24 hours and 2 minutes, and a trifle over 27 seconds. This gives the sun the advantage of gaining one revolution of Venus, and of passing that body in the heavens, once in 584 days, 16 hours and 48 minutes precisely. For this reason and this alone we can never see Venus in elongation on either side of the moon but about 47 or 48 degrees. Yet she is the morning and evening star 290 days in consecutive order. Deduct 360 days the time it takes the earth to roll round, from 584 days, 16 hours and 48 minutes, and we have 224 days, 16 hours and 48 minutes left, which is the time that the Copernicans require for Venus to make an elipticle orbit about the sun. We thus prove by there own books that their system is false, but, that practical observation is correct, They tell us too that when the earth is in its extreme orbit about the sun, that the fixed stars are comparatively by the best glasses, no nearer to us than when we are on the opposite of the earth's orbit. This is direct and positive evidence that the earth makes and has no such an orbit, neither does it make a daily revolution entirely round its axis, but only rolls 62½ miles on its surface, or one degree a day from west to east, 22½ degrees south, which makes the daily variations of longitude as admitted by Hershel's own book. The Copernican system then is false, their own books go to prove the fact while they themselves are to be the judges.

A. C.

text.zh-Hans:
上星期六之日食果成，准时分毫不差。熏玻璃抢手，观者甚众。下一次日食将在一九〇〇年。

此地日食始于五时四分，终于六时五十分，历时共一小时四十六分。中心与十二分之十一遮蔽之时为五时五十七分，按法院之时。日之逐日绕地运行，追上月之逐日自东向西绕行，而越过后者，恰历一小时四十六分。地为宇宙中心而非日，此事于此次以宏大而周详之规模得到证明；而地自西向东转，偏南二十二度半，并绕己身画出黄道线。

天体与地之间这一宏大而目见之证明，千万人所共睹，遂使人为之哥白尼体系就此了结。由此巨证，吾侪得知日径仅七千二百英里；其每日一周，于赤道垂直，距离为四十三万二千英里，自东向西，每二十九日十二时四十三分五十一又六百六十九分之五百零一秒，恰超月一次。此即朔望周期，诸日月食之时刻皆据以记。月径三千六百英里，每日自东向西绕地，月距地[…]表面二十一万六千英里，然落后于日约四十八分四十五秒。据极精确之推算，宇宙半径线仅一百七十二万八千英里，理性诸天内凹面之周长仅一千零八十万英里。此既为理性造化之界线，则哥白尼派所教之天体大小与距离，于神之全部造化中无容身之地。即恒星亦以数千英里计，不以百万、万亿英里计。一七六九年六月三日金星凌日，于 Otah[…]ati 岛，定得日距为九千五百万英里。然全部推算以金星确循椭圆轨道绕日、周期二百二十四日十六时四十八分为据。实则金星每日自东向西绕地一周，用二十四时二分，又稍逾二十七秒。此使日得多胜金星一周，每五百八十四日十六时四十八分，恰越过该星一次。单因此故，吾侪见金星于月两侧之大距，不过四十七或四十八度。然其为晨星昏星，先后相继共二百九十日。以地滚转一周之三百六十日，自五百八十四日十六时四十八分减去，余二百二十四日十六时四十八分，此即哥白尼派要求金星绕日椭圆一周之时。吾侪由此以其自家之书证其体系为误，而实地观测为正。彼辈又告吾侪，地处绕日轨道极远处时，以最佳之镜窥察，恒星比较而言并不比吾侪在地轨道对侧时更近。此乃地不作且无此轨道之直接确证，亦不绕轴作一整日之自转，只在其表面滚动六十二英里半，即每日自西向东一度，偏南二十二度半，由此成每日经度之变，Hershel 自家之书亦所承认。哥白尼体系于是为误，其自家之书足证其事，而判之者即彼辈自身。

A·C．
text.zh-Hant:
上星期六之日食果成，準時分毫不差。燻玻璃搶手，觀者甚眾。下一次日食將在一九〇〇年。

此地日食始於五時四分，終於六時五十分，歷時共一小時四十六分。中心與十二分之十一遮蔽之時為五時五十七分，按法院之時。日之逐日繞地運行，追上月之逐日自東向西繞行，而越過後者，恰歷一小時四十六分。地為宇宙中心而非日，此事於此次以宏大而周詳之規模得到證明；而地自西向東轉，偏南二十二度半，並繞己身畫出黃道線。

天體與地之間這一宏大而目見之證明，千萬人所共睹，遂使人為之哥白尼體系就此了結。由此巨證，吾儕得知日徑僅七千二百英里；其每日一週，於赤道垂直，距離為四十三萬二千英里，自東向西，每二十九日十二時四十三分五十一又六百六十九分之五百零一秒，恰超月一次。此即朔望週期，諸日月食之時刻皆據以記。月徑三千六百英里，每日自東向西繞地，月距地[…]表面二十一萬六千英里，然落後於日約四十八分四十五秒。據極精確之推算，宇宙半徑線僅一百七十二萬八千英里，理性諸天內凹面之周長僅一千零八十萬英里。此既為理性造化之界線，則哥白尼派所教之天體大小與距離，於神之全部造化中無容身之地。即恆星亦以數千英里計，不以百萬、萬億英里計。一七六九年六月三日金星凌日，於 Otah[…]ati 島，定得日距為九千五百萬英里。然全部推算以金星確循橢圓軌道繞日、週期二百二十四日十六時四十八分為據。實則金星每日自東向西繞地一週，用二十四時二分，又稍逾二十七秒。此使日得多勝金星一週，每五百八十四日十六時四十八分，恰越過該星一次。單因此故，吾儕見金星於月兩側之大距，不過四十七或四十八度。然其為晨星昏星，先後相繼共二百九十日。以地滾轉一週之三百六十日，自五百八十四日十六時四十八分減去，餘二百二十四日十六時四十八分，此即哥白尼派要求金星繞日橢圓一週之時。吾儕由此以其自家之書證其體系為誤，而實地觀測為正。彼輩又告吾儕，地處繞日軌道極遠處時，以最佳之鏡窺察，恆星比較而言並不比吾儕在地軌道對側時更近。此乃地不作且無此軌道之直接確證，亦不繞軸作一整日之自轉，只在其表面滾動六十二英里半，即每日自西向東一度，偏南二十二度半，由此成每日經度之變，Hershel 自家之書亦所承認。哥白尼體系於是為誤，其自家之書足證其事，而判之者即彼輩自身。

A·C．

text.fr:
L'éclipse de Soleil de samedi dernier s'est révélée un succès, et à l'heure à un point près. Le verre enfumé était demandé et les spectateurs nombreux. La prochaine éclipse aura lieu en l'an 1900.

L'éclipse de Soleil en cet endroit commença à 4 minutes après 5 heures et finit à 10 minutes avant 7 heures, faisant 1 heure et 46 minutes pour toute la durée. Le temps central et onze douzièmes obscurcis à 3 minutes avant 6 heures, à l'heure du palais de justice. Le Soleil, dans sa révolution quotidienne autour de la Terre, rattrapa la Lune dans sa révolution quotidienne d'est en ouest, et dépassa ce dernier corps en exactement 1 heure et 46 minutes. Le fait que la Terre est le centre de l'univers et non le Soleil a été démontré en ce cas sur une grande et vaste échelle ; tandis que la Terre tourne d'ouest en est à 22½ degrés au sud et marque la ligne écliptique autour de son propre corps.

Cette grande démonstration oculaire entre les corps célestes et la Terre, dont furent témoins des milliers et des dizaines de milliers de personnes, clôt le système artificiel, ou copernicien. Par cette puissante démonstration nous apprenons que le Soleil n'a que 7 200 milles de diamètre ; qu'il fait une révolution quotidienne verticale à l'équateur à une distance de 432 000 milles d'est en ouest, et dépasse la Lune une fois en 29 jours, 12 heures, 43 minutes et 51 secondes et 501/669, précisément. Cela constitue la période synodique, d'après laquelle toutes les éclipses sont consignées dans le temps. La Lune a 3600 milles de diamètre et tourne d'est en ouest autour de la Terre chaque jour, mais retarde sur le Soleil d'environ 48 minutes et 45 secondes, à une distance de 216 000 milles, de la surface de la Ter[…]re. Par un calcul très exact, la ligne de rayon de l'univers n'est que de 1 728 000 milles, et la circonférence de la surface intérieure concave des cieux rationnels, que de 10 800 000 milles. Telles étant les lignes frontières de la création rationnelle, il n'y a pas de place pour les grandeurs et les distances des corps célestes, telles qu'enseignées par les coperniciens, dans toute la création de Dieu. Même les étoiles fixes se mesurent par milliers de milles au lieu de millions et de billions de milles. Par le transit de Vénus en 1769, le 3 juin, à l'île d'Otah[…]ati, on détermina que la distance au Soleil était de 95 000 000 de milles anglais. Mais tout le calcul se fondait sur la supposition que Vénus décrivait bien une orbite elliptique autour du Soleil en 224 jours 16 heures et 48 minutes. Alors qu'en réalité Vénus fait une révolution quotidienne autour de la Terre d'est en ouest en 24 heures et 2 minutes, et un rien de plus de 27 secondes. Cela donne au Soleil l'avantage de gagner une révolution de Vénus, et de dépasser ce corps dans le ciel, une fois en 584 jours, 16 heures et 48 minutes précisément. Pour cette raison et pour celle-là seule nous ne pouvons jamais voir Vénus en élongation de part et d'autre de la Lune qu'à environ 47 ou 48 degrés. Pourtant elle est l'étoile du matin et du soir 290 jours consécutifs. Retranchez 360 jours, le temps que met la Terre à rouler sur elle-même, de 584 jours, 16 heures et 48 minutes, et il nous reste 224 jours, 16 heures et 48 minutes, ce qui est le temps que les coperniciens exigent pour que Vénus fasse une orbite elliptique autour du Soleil. Nous prouvons ainsi par leurs propres livres que leur système est faux, mais que l'observation pratique est correcte. Ils nous disent aussi que lorsque la Terre est au point extrême de son orbite autour du Soleil, les étoiles fixes ne sont comparativement, avec les meilleures lunettes, pas plus proches de nous que lorsque nous sommes du côté opposé de l'orbite de la Terre. C'est une preuve directe et positive que la Terre ne fait ni n'a une telle orbite, et qu'elle ne fait pas non plus une révolution quotidienne entièrement autour de son axe, mais seulement roule de 62½ milles sur sa surface, ou d'un degré par jour d'ouest en est, à 22½ degrés au sud, ce qui fait les variations quotidiennes de longitude comme l'admet le livre même de Hershel. Le système copernicien est donc faux, leurs propres livres tendent à en prouver le fait tandis qu'eux-mêmes en sont les juges.

A. C.
text.es:
El Eclipse de Sol del sábado pasado resultó un éxito, y puntual al detalle. El cristal ahumado tuvo demanda y los espectadores fueron numerosos. El próximo Eclipse tendrá lugar en el año 1900.

El eclipse de Sol en este lugar comenzó a las 5 y 4 minutos y terminó a las 7 menos 10, lo que hace 1 hora y 46 minutos de tiempo total. El tiempo central y las once doceavas partes oscurecidas fueron a las 6 menos 3 minutos, por la hora del tribunal. El Sol, en su revolución diaria alrededor de la Tierra, alcanzó a la Luna en su revolución diaria de este a oeste, y pasó este último cuerpo en el tiempo exacto de 1 hora y 46 minutos. El hecho de que la Tierra es el centro del universo y no el Sol ha quedado demostrado en este caso a gran escala y de manera comprensiva; mientras la Tierra gira de oeste a este 22½ grados al sur y marca la línea eclíptica alrededor de su propio cuerpo.

Esta gran demostración ocular entre los cuerpos celestes y la Tierra, presenciada por millares y decenas de millares de personas, cierra el sistema artificial, o copernicano. Por esta poderosa demostración sabemos que el Sol tiene solo 7200 millas de diámetro; que hace una revolución diaria vertical en el ecuador a una distancia de 432.000 millas de este a oeste, y pasa a la Luna una vez cada 29 días, 12 horas, 43 minutos y 51 segundos y 501/669, exactamente. Esto constituye el período sinódico, a partir del cual se registran todos los eclipses en el tiempo. La Luna tiene 3600 millas de diámetro y gira de este a oeste alrededor de la Tierra a diario, pero se queda atrás del Sol unos 48 minutos y 45 segundos, a una distancia de 216.000 millas de la superficie de la Tie[…]a. Según un cálculo muy exacto, la línea del radio del universo es de solo 1.728.000 millas, y la circunferencia de la superficie cóncava interior de los cielos racionales, de solo 10.800.000 millas. Siendo estas las líneas de límite de la creación racional, no hay lugar para los tamaños y distancias de los cuerpos celestes, tal como los enseñan los copernicanos, en toda la creación de Dios. Incluso las estrellas fijas se miden por millares de millas en vez de por millones y billones de millas. Por el tránsito de Venus de 1769, el 3 de junio, en la isla de Otah[…]ati, se determinó que la distancia al Sol era de 95.000.000 de millas inglesas. Pero todo el cálculo se fundaba en la suposición de que Venus describía una órbita elíptica alrededor del Sol en 224 días, 16 horas y 48 minutos. Cuando en realidad Venus hace una revolución diaria alrededor de la Tierra de este a oeste en 24 horas y 2 minutos, y una pizca más de 27 segundos. Esto da al Sol la ventaja de ganar una revolución a Venus y de pasar a ese cuerpo en el cielo una vez cada 584 días, 16 horas y 48 minutos, exactamente. Por esta razón, y solo por ella, nunca podemos ver a Venus en elongación a uno y otro lado de la Luna sino unos 47 o 48 grados. Sin embargo, es la estrella de la mañana y de la tarde durante 290 días en orden consecutivo. Réstense 360 días, el tiempo que tarda la Tierra en rodar, de 584 días, 16 horas y 48 minutos, y nos quedan 224 días, 16 horas y 48 minutos, que es el tiempo que los copernicanos requieren para que Venus describa una órbita elíptica alrededor del Sol. Así probamos por sus propios libros que su sistema es falso, pero que la observación práctica es correcta. Nos dicen también que cuando la Tierra está en su órbita extrema alrededor del Sol, las estrellas fijas, comparativamente, con los mejores anteojos, no están más cerca de nosotros que cuando estamos en el lado opuesto de la órbita de la Tierra. Esta es una prueba directa y positiva de que la Tierra no hace ni tiene tal órbita, ni hace tampoco una revolución diaria completa alrededor de su eje, sino que solo rueda 62½ millas sobre su superficie, o un grado al día de oeste a este, 22½ grados al sur, lo que produce las variaciones diarias de longitud, como admite el propio libro de Hershel. El sistema copernicano es, pues, falso; sus propios libros sirven para probar el hecho, y ellos mismos han de ser los jueces.

A. C.
text.it:
L'eclissi di Sole di sabato scorso si è rivelata un successo, e puntualissima. Il vetro affumicato era richiesto e gli spettatori numerosi. La prossima eclissi avrà luogo nell'anno 1900.

L'eclissi di Sole in questo luogo è cominciata alle 5 e 4 minuti e finita alle 7 meno 10 minuti, per un totale di 1 ora e 46 minuti per l'intera durata. Il tempo centrale e undici dodicesimi oscurati alle 6 meno 3 minuti, secondo l'ora del Palazzo di giustizia. Il Sole nella sua rivoluzione quotidiana attorno alla Terra ha raggiunto la Luna nella sua rivoluzione quotidiana da est a ovest, e ha superato quest'ultimo corpo nell'esatto tempo di 1 ora e 46 minuti. Il fatto che la Terra sia il centro dell'universo e non il Sole è stato in questo caso dimostrato su scala ampia e comprensiva; mentre la Terra ruota da ovest a est di 22½ gradi a sud e segna la linea eclittica attorno al proprio corpo.

Questa grande dimostrazione oculare tra i corpi celesti e la Terra, di cui sono stati testimoni migliaia e decine di migliaia di persone, chiude il sistema artificiale, o copernicano. Da questa possente dimostrazione impariamo che il Sole ha solo 7200 miglia di diametro; che compie una rivoluzione quotidiana verticale all'equatore a una distanza di 432.000 miglia da est a ovest, e supera la Luna una volta ogni 29 giorni, 12 ore, 43 minuti e 51 secondi e 501/669, precisamente. Questo costituisce il periodo sinodico, dal quale tutte le eclissi sono registrate nel tempo. La Luna ha 3600 miglia di diametro e ruota da est a ovest attorno alla Terra ogni giorno, ma resta indietro rispetto al Sole di circa 48 minuti e 45 secondi, a una distanza di 216.000 miglia, dalla superficie della Ter[…]a. Con un calcolo molto accurato la linea del raggio dell'universo è solo di 1.728.000 miglia, e la circonferenza della superficie concava interna dei cieli razionali, solo di 10.800.000 miglia. Essendo questi i confini della creazione razionale, non c'è spazio per le dimensioni e le distanze dei corpi celesti, come insegnate dai copernicani, in tutta la creazione di Dio. Persino le stelle fisse sono misurate in migliaia di miglia anziché in milioni e bilioni di miglia. Dal transito di Venere nel 1769, il 3 di giugno, all'isola di Otah[…]ati, fu determinato che la distanza dal Sole era di 95.000.000 di miglia inglesi. Ma l'intero calcolo si fondava sulla supposizione che Venere compisse un'orbita ellittica attorno al Sole in 224 giorni 16 ore e 48 minuti. Mentre in realtà Venere compie una rivoluzione quotidiana attorno alla Terra da est a ovest in 24 ore e 2 minuti, e un po' più di 27 secondi. Questo dà al Sole il vantaggio di guadagnare una rivoluzione su Venere, e di superare quel corpo nel cielo, una volta ogni 584 giorni, 16 ore e 48 minuti precisamente. Per questa ragione e solo per questa non possiamo mai vedere Venere in elongazione su nessuno dei due lati della Luna se non di circa 47 o 48 gradi. Eppure essa è la stella del mattino e della sera per 290 giorni consecutivi. Si sottraggano 360 giorni, il tempo che la Terra impiega a rotolare, da 584 giorni, 16 ore e 48 minuti, e ci restano 224 giorni, 16 ore e 48 minuti, che è il tempo che i copernicani richiedono perché Venere compia un'orbita ellittica attorno al Sole. Proviamo così con i loro stessi libri che il loro sistema è falso, ma che l'osservazione pratica è corretta. Essi ci dicono anche che quando la Terra è nella sua orbita estrema attorno al Sole, le stelle fisse sono comparativamente, con i migliori vetri, non più vicine a noi che quando siamo dal lato opposto dell'orbita terrestre. Questa è prova diretta e positiva che la Terra non compie e non ha un'orbita simile, né compie una rivoluzione quotidiana interamente attorno al proprio asse, ma rotola solo di 62½ miglia sulla sua superficie, ovvero di un grado al giorno da ovest a est, 22½ gradi a sud, il che dà le variazioni quotidiane di longitudine come ammesso dallo stesso libro di Hershel. Il sistema copernicano è dunque falso, i loro stessi libri servono a provare il fatto mentre essi stessi ne sono i giudici.

A. C.
text.ja:
先週土曜日の日食は成功となり、寸分違わず時刻どおりであった。燻したガラスが求められ、見物人は多かった。次の日食は1900年に起こる。

当地での日食は5時4分に始まり、7時10分前に終わった。全体で1時間46分である。中心の時刻、および12分の11が覆われた時刻は、裁判所の時計で6時3分前であった。太陽は、地球のまわりを毎日一周するなかで、東から西へ毎日一周する月に追いつき、ちょうど1時間46分でその天体を追い越した。地球が宇宙の中心であって太陽ではないという事実は、この場合、大規模かつ包括的に証明された。一方、地球は西から東へ南に22½度で回転し、自らの体のまわりに黄道線を描く。

天体と地球との間のこの大規模で目に見える証明は、数千、数万の人々に目撃され、人為的な、すなわちコペルニクス説の体系に終止符を打つ。この力強い証明によって、太陽の直径はわずか7200マイルにすぎないこと、赤道で垂直に毎日一周し、東から西へ432,000マイルの距離を行くこと、29日12時間43分51と669分の501秒ごとに、ちょうど一度月を追い越すことがわかる。これが朔望周期を成し、すべての日食と月食はここから時刻に従って記録される。月の直径は3600マイルで、毎日東から西へ地球のまわりを回るが、地[…]の表面から216,000マイルの距離で、太陽から約48分45秒遅れる。きわめて正確な計算によれば、宇宙の半径線はわずか1.728,000マイルで、理性的な天界の内側の凹面の円周は、わずか10,800,000マイルである。これが理性的な創造の境界線であるから、コペルニクス派の教えるような天体の大きさと距離は、神のすべての創造のなかに入る余地がない。恒星さえも、何百万マイル、何兆マイルではなく、何千マイルで測られる。1769年6月3日のオタハ[…]アティ島での金星の太陽面通過によって、太陽までの距離は9500万イングランド・マイルと決定された。しかし、その計算全体は、金星が実際に224日16時間48分で太陽のまわりに楕円軌道を描くという仮定の上に成り立っていた。実際には、金星は24時間2分と、わずかに27秒余りで、東から西へ毎日地球のまわりを一周する。このため太陽は、金星の一周分だけ得をし、584日16時間48分ごとに、ちょうど一度天空でその天体を追い越すことになる。この理由のみによって、私たちは金星を月の両側で離角47度か48度ほどにしか見ることができない。それでも金星は、290日間続けて順に明けの明星であり宵の明星である。地球が転がり回る時間である360日を、584日16時間48分から引くと、224日16時間48分が残り、これがコペルニクス派が金星に太陽のまわりの楕円軌道を描くために要求する時間である。このように私たちは、彼ら自身の書物によって彼らの体系が誤りであり、実地の観測が正しいことを証明する。彼らはまた、地球が太陽のまわりの軌道の端にあるとき、恒星は最良の望遠鏡で見ても、私たちが地球の軌道の反対側にいるときより近くはない、と私たちに告げる。これは、地球がそのような軌道を描かず、またその軸のまわりを完全に一周する毎日の回転もせず、その表面を62½マイル、すなわち西から東へ南に22½度、1日に1度だけ転がるにすぎないという、直接かつ明白な証拠であり、これが、ハーシェル自身の書物も認める毎日の経度の変化を生む。したがってコペルニクス説は誤りであり、彼ら自身の書物がその事実を裏づけているのに、彼ら自身が裁き手であることになる。

A. C.

text_orig: Perhaps no incident in science ever created the intense excitement among the scientific men of our country as did the great Solar eclipse of Saturday last. It is, in the first place, very seldom that we have a total eclipse of the sun visible to any part of the world. There must be, according to astronomers, five eclipses of the sun each year, but the disparity between the size of the sun and moon is so great that the two bodies must be in a peculiar position to eclipse any part of the sun to the earth; and even if this position occurs, but a small belt of the earth can possibly be thrown in the total line of the moon's shadow. The eclipse of Saturday last was observed all over this country, in various phases, but its totality embraced only a belt one hundred and thirty miles broad, extending from Alaska, in a South-west direction, until it passed into the sea off the coast of North Carolina. In this latitude about five-sixths of the sun's surface was obscured, but so powerful a source of light and heat is that luminary that, even with only one-sixth of its surface visible to the world, it gave a light equal to that which would be afforded by ten thousand of our moons. We witnessed the eclipse in Virginia, where 11½ of the twelve parts of the sun was obscured; but even then there was light sufficient to read the finest print. To witness a total eclipse of the sun, in all its grandeur, some point inside of the line of totality must be reached. At such a place it is overpowering in its awful sublimity.

text.zh-Hans: 科学中之事，恐无一能如上星期六之日食盛事，在吾国科学家中激起如此强烈之兴奋。首先，世界任何一处得见日全食者极罕。据天文学家云，每年日食必有五次，然日月大小悬殊，二者必处特殊位置，方使日之任何部分为地所见而食；纵有此位，地上亦仅一窄带可落于月影全食线内。上星期六之食，全国皆见，所见各异，而全食只及宽一百三十英里之带，自阿拉斯加向西南延伸，至北卡罗来纳州海岸外入海。此纬度日面约六分之五被掩，然日为光热之源，其力至强，纵仅六分之一露于世，所发之光仍等于一万个吾月所供。吾侪于弗吉尼亚观此食，日十二分之中十一分半被掩；纵然如此，光仍足以读最细之字。欲见日全食之壮，须抵全食线内某处。至其处，则其可畏之崇高，令人不堪承受。
text.zh-Hant: 科學中之事，恐無一能如上星期六之日食盛事，在吾國科學家中激起如此強烈之興奮。首先，世界任何一處得見日全食者極罕。據天文學家雲，每年日食必有五次，然日月大小懸殊，二者必處特殊位置，方使日之任何部分為地所見而食；縱有此位，地上亦僅一窄帶可落於月影全食線內。上星期六之食，全國皆見，所見各異，而全食只及寬一百三十英里之帶，自阿拉斯加向西南延伸，至北卡羅來納州海岸外入海。此緯度日面約六分之五被掩，然日為光熱之源，其力至強，縱僅六分之一露於世，所發之光仍等於一萬個吾月所供。吾儕於弗吉尼亞觀此食，日十二分之中十一分半被掩；縱然如此，光仍足以讀最細之字。欲見日全食之壯，須抵全食線內某處。至其處，則其可畏之崇高，令人不堪承受。
text.en: Perhaps no incident in science ever created the intense excitement among the scientific men of our country as did the great Solar eclipse of Saturday last. It is, in the first place, very seldom that we have a total eclipse of the sun visible to any part of the world. There must be, according to astronomers, five eclipses of the sun each year, but the disparity between the size of the sun and moon is so great that the two bodies must be in a peculiar position to eclipse any part of the sun to the earth; and even if this position occurs, but a small belt of the earth can possibly be thrown in the total line of the moon's shadow. The eclipse of Saturday last was observed all over this country, in various phases, but its totality embraced only a belt one hundred and thirty miles broad, extending from Alaska, in a South-west direction, until it passed into the sea off the coast of North Carolina. In this latitude about five-sixths of the sun's surface was obscured, but so powerful a source of light and heat is that luminary that, even with only one-sixth of its surface visible to the world, it gave a light equal to that which would be afforded by ten thousand of our moons. We witnessed the eclipse in Virginia, where 11½ of the twelve parts of the sun was obscured; but even then there was light sufficient to read the finest print. To witness a total eclipse of the sun, in all its grandeur, some point inside of the line of totality must be reached. At such a place it is overpowering in its awful sublimity.
text.fr: Peut-être aucun incident de la science n'a-t-il jamais créé parmi les hommes de science de notre pays une excitation aussi intense que la grande éclipse de Soleil de samedi dernier. Il est, en premier lieu, très rare que nous ayons une éclipse totale de Soleil visible d'une partie quelconque du monde. Il doit y avoir, selon les astronomes, cinq éclipses de Soleil chaque année, mais la disparité entre la grandeur du Soleil et celle de la Lune est si grande que les deux corps doivent se trouver dans une position particulière pour éclipser une partie quelconque du Soleil pour la Terre ; et même si cette position se produit, seule une petite bande de la Terre peut être jetée dans la ligne totale de l'ombre de la Lune. L'éclipse de samedi dernier fut observée dans tout ce pays, à diverses phases, mais sa totalité n'embrassa qu'une bande large de cent trente milles, s'étendant de l'Alaska, en direction du sud-ouest, jusqu'à ce qu'elle passât dans la mer au large de la côte de la Caroline du Nord. À cette latitude environ cinq sixièmes de la surface du Soleil furent obscurcis, mais si puissante est la source de lumière et de chaleur que cet astre, même avec seulement un sixième de sa surface visible pour le monde, donna une lumière égale à celle que fourniraient dix mille de nos Lunes. Nous avons observé l'éclipse en Virginie, où 11½ des douze parties du Soleil furent obscurcies ; mais même alors il y avait assez de lumière pour lire les caractères les plus fins. Pour voir une éclipse totale de Soleil, dans toute sa grandeur, il faut gagner quelque point à l'intérieur de la ligne de totalité. En un tel lieu elle est écrasante dans sa sublimité imposante.
text.es: Quizá ningún suceso de la ciencia produjo jamás entre los hombres de ciencia de nuestro país una emoción tan intensa como el gran eclipse de Sol del sábado pasado. Es, en primer lugar, muy raro que tengamos un eclipse total de Sol visible para alguna parte del mundo. Debe haber, según los astrónomos, cinco eclipses de Sol cada año, pero la disparidad entre el tamaño del Sol y el de la Luna es tan grande que los dos cuerpos deben hallarse en una posición peculiar para eclipsar cualquier parte del Sol a la Tierra; e incluso si se da esta posición, solo una pequeña franja de la Tierra puede quedar en la línea total de la sombra de la Luna. El eclipse del sábado pasado fue observado en todo este país, en diversas fases, pero su totalidad abarcó solo una franja de ciento treinta millas de ancho, que se extendía desde Alaska, en dirección suroeste, hasta que se adentró en el mar frente a la costa de Carolina del Norte. En esta latitud quedó oscurecido aproximadamente cinco sextos de la superficie del Sol, pero tan poderosa fuente de luz y de calor es ese astro que, aun con solo un sexto de su superficie visible para el mundo, dio una luz igual a la que darían diez mil de nuestras lunas. Presenciamos el eclipse en Virginia, donde quedaron oscurecidas 11½ de las doce partes del Sol; pero incluso entonces había luz suficiente para leer la letra más fina. Para presenciar un eclipse total de Sol, en toda su grandeza, debe llegarse a algún punto situado dentro de la línea de totalidad. En tal lugar resulta abrumador en su imponente sublimidad.
text.it: Forse nessun avvenimento della scienza ha mai suscitato tra gli uomini di scienza del nostro paese un'eccitazione tanto intensa quanto la grande eclissi solare di sabato scorso. È, in primo luogo, molto raro che si abbia un'eclissi totale di Sole visibile in qualche parte del mondo. Devono esserci, secondo gli astronomi, cinque eclissi di Sole ogni anno, ma la disparità tra le dimensioni del Sole e della Luna è così grande che i due corpi devono trovarsi in una posizione particolare per eclissare una qualsiasi parte del Sole alla Terra; e anche se questa posizione si verifica, solo una piccola fascia della Terra può cadere nella linea totale dell'ombra della Luna. L'eclissi di sabato scorso è stata osservata in tutto questo paese, in varie fasi, ma la sua totalità abbracciava solo una fascia larga centotrenta miglia, che si estendeva dall'Alaska, in direzione sudovest, finché passava in mare al largo della costa della Carolina del Nord. A questa latitudine circa cinque sesti della superficie del Sole erano oscurati, ma quel luminare è una fonte di luce e calore così potente che, anche con solo un sesto della sua superficie visibile al mondo, dava una luce pari a quella che sarebbe fornita da diecimila delle nostre lune. Abbiamo assistito all'eclissi in Virginia, dove 11½ delle dodici parti del Sole erano oscurate; ma anche allora c'era luce sufficiente per leggere la stampa più minuta. Per assistere a un'eclissi totale di Sole, in tutta la sua grandiosità, si deve raggiungere qualche punto all'interno della linea della totalità. In un tale luogo essa è sopraffacente nella sua imponente sublimità.
text.ja: 科学上の出来事で、先週土曜日の大日食ほど、わが国の科学者たちの間に強い興奮を生んだものは、おそらくないであろう。まず、世界のどこかの地で見える皆既日食は、きわめてまれである。天文学者によれば、日食は毎年5回なければならないが、太陽と月の大きさの隔たりが非常に大きいため、地球から見て太陽のどの部分かが食されるには、二つの天体が特別な位置にあらねばならない。たとえその位置が生じても、月の影の皆既の線に入りうるのは、地球上のわずかな帯だけである。先週土曜日の日食は、この国の全域で、さまざまな相で観測されたが、その皆既は幅130マイルの帯だけを覆い、アラスカから南西の方向に延びて、ノースカロライナの海岸沖で海に入った。この緯度では太陽の表面のおよそ6分の5が隠されたが、その天体は強力な光と熱の源であり、世界から見える表面がわずか6分の1であっても、私たちの月1万個が与えるのに等しい光を与えた。私たちはヴァージニアで日食を見たが、そこでは太陽の12の部分のうち11½が隠された。それでもなお、最も細かな活字を読むのに十分な光があった。皆既日食をその壮大さのすべてにおいて見るには、皆既の線の内側のどこかの地点に達しなければならない。そのような場所では、その畏怖すべき崇高さは圧倒的である。

text_orig: We witnessed the eclipse here on Saturday evening, it being very near total. The planet Venus was visible to the naked eye for some time, affording us a view of the sun, moon and this planet all visible high in the heavens at the same time.

text.zh-Hans: 星期六晚，吾侪于此观日食，几近全食。金星肉眼可见历时颇久，使吾侪得于高天同时见日、月与此行星。
text.zh-Hant: 星期六晚，吾儕於此觀日食，幾近全食。金星肉眼可見歷時頗久，使吾儕得於高天同時見日、月與此行星。
text.en: We witnessed the eclipse here on Saturday evening, it being very near total. The planet Venus was visible to the naked eye for some time, affording us a view of the sun, moon and this planet all visible high in the heavens at the same time.
text.fr: Nous avons observé l'éclipse ici samedi soir, elle était très près d'être totale. La planète Vénus fut visible à l'œil nu pendant quelque temps, nous offrant la vue du Soleil, de la Lune et de cette planète tous visibles ensemble haut dans le ciel au même moment.
text.es: Presenciamos el eclipse aquí el sábado por la tarde, estando muy cerca de ser total. El planeta Venus fue visible a simple vista durante algún tiempo, lo que nos permitió ver el Sol, la Luna y este planeta, todos visibles en lo alto del cielo al mismo tiempo.
text.it: Abbiamo assistito all'eclissi qui sabato sera, essendo molto vicina alla totale. Il pianeta Venere è stato visibile a occhio nudo per qualche tempo, offrendoci la vista del Sole, della Luna e di questo pianeta tutti visibili in alto nel cielo nello stesso tempo.
text.ja: 私たちは土曜日の夕方、ここで日食を見たが、ほぼ皆既であった。金星がしばらくの間、肉眼で見え、太陽、月、そしてこの惑星がすべて同時に高い空に見える光景を私たちに与えてくれた。

text_orig: There was much excitement here last Saturday, on account of the eclipse, which came in on the 5 o'clock train, and much smoked glass circulated among our citizens on account thereof. One industrious chap sat for two hours on top his house trying to look through a piece of smoked looking-glass, and not being able to "see it," gave it as his private opinion that it was a "d— humbug" Some few persons labored under the absurd idea that to see the eclipse in all its glory, it would be necessary to look through "a glass darkly," and many were the 'rye' faces of those who thus tried to keep in good spirits during the performance. Murphy, the Trenton correspondent of the New York Herald, says the reason the eclipse couldn't be seen very well here, is because one of the New York City judges put an injunction on it to prevent its going into a foreign country.

text.zh-Hans: 上星期六，此地因日食而颇为兴奋，日食乘五时之火车而至，熏玻璃在市民间大量流传。一勤勉之人坐屋顶两小时，试透一块熏黑镜片观日，不得「见」，私下断其为「该——骗局」。少数人荒唐地以为，欲尽见日食之盛，须「隔着暗玻璃」而观，故不少人苦着「歪」脸，以此强作欢颜于演出之际。《纽约先驱报》驻特伦顿通讯员墨菲云，日食此地不甚看得清，是因纽约市一法官下禁令，不许其入外国。
text.zh-Hant: 上星期六，此地因日食而頗為興奮，日食乘五時之火車而至，燻玻璃在市民間大量流傳。一勤勉之人坐屋頂兩小時，試透一塊燻黑鏡片觀日，不得「見」，私下斷其為「該——騙局」。少數人荒唐地以為，欲盡見日食之盛，須「隔着暗玻璃」而觀，故不少人苦着「歪」臉，以此強作歡顏於演出之際。《紐約先驅報》駐特倫頓通訊員墨菲雲，日食此地不甚看得清，是因紐約市一法官下禁令，不許其入外國。
text.en: There was much excitement here last Saturday, on account of the eclipse, which came in on the 5 o'clock train, and much smoked glass circulated among our citizens on account thereof. One industrious chap sat for two hours on top his house trying to look through a piece of smoked looking-glass, and not being able to "see it," gave it as his private opinion that it was a "d— humbug" Some few persons labored under the absurd idea that to see the eclipse in all its glory, it would be necessary to look through "a glass darkly," and many were the 'rye' faces of those who thus tried to keep in good spirits during the performance. Murphy, the Trenton correspondent of the New York Herald, says the reason the eclipse couldn't be seen very well here, is because one of the New York City judges put an injunction on it to prevent its going into a foreign country.
text.fr: Il y eut ici beaucoup d'agitation samedi dernier à cause de l'éclipse, qui arriva par le train de 5 heures, et beaucoup de verre enfumé circula parmi nos concitoyens à cause de cela. Un travailleur zélé resta deux heures sur le toit de sa maison à essayer de regarder à travers un morceau de miroir enfumé, et, ne parvenant pas à « la voir », donna pour son opinion privée que c'était « une m— de fumisterie ». Quelques personnes nourrissaient l'idée absurde que, pour voir l'éclipse dans toute sa gloire, il faudrait regarder à travers « un verre obscurément », et nombreux furent les visages « grimaçants » de ceux qui essayaient ainsi de garder le moral pendant le spectacle. Murphy, le correspondant à Trenton du New York Herald, dit que la raison pour laquelle l'éclipse n'a pas pu être très bien vue ici est qu'un des juges de la ville de New York a rendu une ordonnance contre elle pour l'empêcher d'entrer dans un pays étranger.
text.es: Hubo mucha agitación aquí el sábado pasado a causa del eclipse, que llegó en el tren de las 5, y por ello circuló mucho vidrio ahumado entre nuestros ciudadanos. Un individuo diligente estuvo dos horas sentado encima de su casa intentando mirar a través de un trozo de espejo ahumado, y al no poder «verlo», dio como opinión privada que era una «m— patraña». Algunas pocas personas sufrían la absurda idea de que, para ver el eclipse en toda su gloria, habría que mirar «a través de un cristal, oscuramente», y muchas fueron las caras «torcidas» de quienes intentaron así mantener el buen ánimo durante la función. Murphy, el corresponsal en Trenton del New York Herald, dice que la razón de que el eclipse no pudiera verse muy bien aquí es que uno de los jueces de la ciudad de Nueva York le impuso un interdicto para impedir que pasara a un país extranjero.
text.it: Vi fu molta eccitazione qui sabato scorso, a causa dell'eclissi, che giunse con il treno delle 5, e a causa di ciò molto vetro affumicato circolò tra i nostri cittadini. Un tipo industrioso rimase seduto per due ore sul tetto di casa sua cercando di guardare attraverso un pezzo di specchio affumicato, e non riuscendo a «vederla», diede come suo parere privato che fosse «una dann— buffonata». Alcune poche persone si trovavano sotto l'assurda idea che, per vedere l'eclissi in tutta la sua gloria, fosse necessario guardare «attraverso un vetro scuro», e molte erano le facce «storte» di coloro che tentavano così di mantenere il buonumore durante lo spettacolo. Murphy, il corrispondente da Trenton del New York Herald, dice che il motivo per cui l'eclissi non si poteva vedere molto bene qui è che uno dei giudici della città di New York le ha imposto un'ingiunzione per impedirle di entrare in un paese straniero.
text.ja: 先週の土曜日、この地は日食のために大いににぎわった。日食は5時の列車で到着し、そのため市民のあいだに燻したガラスがたくさん出回った。ある勤勉な男は、屋根の上に2時間座り、燻した鏡の破片を通して見ようとしたが、「見え」なかったので、それは「く—そいんちき」だというのが自分の私見だと述べた。ごく少数の者は、日食をその栄光のすべてにおいて見るには「ガラスを通しておぼろに」見なければならないという馬鹿げた考えにとらわれ、こうして催しのあいだ機嫌よく振る舞おうとした者たちの「ライ」顔が数多く見られた。『ニューヨーク・ヘラルド』紙のトレントン通信員マーフィー氏は、この地で日食があまりよく見えなかった理由は、ニューヨーク市の判事の一人が、外国へ入るのを防ぐために差し止め命令を出したからだと言っている。

text_orig:
The obscuration of the sun, in the recent eclipse, was much more complete in our section than we had been led to suppose by the almanac.

There had been much discussion about the eclipse in our little home circle, and lively anticipations were entertained of what we should see, we had read everything said on the subject in the newspapers.

Our housekeeper had seen the great eclipse in '34, as well as the falling stars, and was oracular on eclipses and meteorology. I wanted to have a good look at the eclipse, so I smoked several pieces of glass, as I knew all the children, as well as my wife and the housekeeper would wish to see it, and I wished a piece of glass all to myself.

That was all humbug about observing the phenomenon satisfactorily, simply by poking a hole through a card and finding an "accurate shadow of the eclipse on the floor or pavement." I tried it. At first the result was satisfactory, as a piece of the sun, as shown by the shadow, was bitten off like a biscuit; but the cut off did not seem to increase as it ought to have done, and I discovered that an almost imperceptible part of the jagged hole was the cause of the seemingly partial obscura[…]ion. We were all in a highly scientific humor, and this discovery established my preeminence for shrewd scientific observation in my household; I felt better for it.

But my housekeeper is a remarkable woman. She had had everything in the house straightened up preparatory to the eclipse.— She came out and took Johnny's smoked glass to make an observation. Miss Selina rather affected to look down upon eclipses. She had seen the great total eclipse in '34, and "they didn't have eclipses like that in these days." Johnny had held the smoked side of his glass too near to his nose, thereby transferring a little round black spot to the tip of that organ, and leaving a little clean round spot on the glass, which came near being fatal to the eclipse as far as our housekeeper was concerned. With an unfortunate facility of getting hold of the wrong end of everything, she looked first through the little round spot, and immediately pronounced that it was no eclipse at all; but a mild protest from my wife, who always dreaded a discussion between Miss Selina and myself, caused her to try again.

Miss Selina has some difficulty in closing one eye at a time; so she had to hold down the lid of the left eye with the three first fingers of her left hand, in consequence of which she makes three more little clear places on the smoked glass, and three little round black dots on and about the left eye lid, which imparts a rather unpleasant expression to Miss Selina's countenance.

Our Johnny, who wants his glass badly, glances to see whether his ma is looking, and finding that she is persistently rubbing her nose against the smoked side of her glass, looks scornfully at our housekeeper, who can't shut one eye without out holding it down.— "What sort of a hand would she make at shootin'?" thinks Johnny. And curly headed little "Pussy," our pet but one, who has got all the black off her glass on her face, is squinting awfully at the top of an oak to find the eclipse, and is satisfied it has "pcurple leaves on it."

Miss Selina has at last brought her right eye to bear on the eclipse, and Johnny has discovered that by a slight motion of the grape vine he can produce a fine effect with a leaf. As Miss Selina looks the grape leaf interposes, and she triumphantly hands Johnny his glass, pronouncing herself satisfied. The reason why it was not total for the rest of us was because we did not know how to look at it. She knew a total eclipse when she saw it, and as it would be dark soon, Miss Selina concludes to save time by taking a little nap while it was going on—one of Miss Selima's delusions is that she can not sleep in the day time, and hence she always availes herself of such occasions as total eclipses to indulge herself in a nap. The skepticism that marked Johnny's countenance at that announcement was as good as a play.

But Miss Selima insists that this eclipse was nothing, yes absolutely nothing to the old one. She says, at that time it was as bright as the blessed sun could make it at mid day, and in an instant it was pitch dark. The chickens went to roost as if the judgment day had come, the cows came lowing home, and the children commenced crying as they always did at sunset, because they did not want to go to bed.

Knowing that our housekeeper kept at least within sight of truth in her statements, I made inquiry as to the foundation for this one. It seems that Miss Selina, who was always an orderly person, had concluded to take a nap, preparatory to the fatigue of observing the eclipse, and no one had thought to wake her up. That event did not occur until about 12 o'clock at night, when waking suddenly and finding it pitchy dark, she concluded that the eclipse had just set in and the noise had waked her from one of those light "cat naps' which was all she ever got; she flew into the chamber, and seizing the then baby, rushed wildly over the cradle, and falling broke the nose of the little innocent, which accounts for the distortion in that organ of that member of the family to this day. I mentioned this little circumstance to my wife, who cautioned Johnny not to say anything about it to Miss Selina or any of the children, coupling the caution with a threat of punishment, by standing in the corner, in case of disobedience. I could not positively say that Johnny ever did say anything about it, but the nezt morning at breakfast, Miss Selina made her appearance, looking uncommonly dignified and resigned. She smoothed her snow white apron with portentious solemnity, as if she were the only lone lorn woman in the world, but entirely resigned to "the slings and arrows of outrageous fortune." Never was a teapot held with such a steady nerve; never was sugar so accurately adjusted. Something was wrong. My wife looked searchingly at Johnny, Johnny's glance was feutive. I am a stern man, and I bent my eye with awful portent upon the boy; he was just grabbing the last hot muffin on the plate to frustrate the handkering desire of his little sister for that luxury, and I do not think ever got the benefit of that frown.

When opportunity offered, I was about to ask Johnny if he had done what his mother told him he ought not to do about that eclipse story. But my wife interferes, and says I must not tempt him to tell a story. I insist that she shall punish him, shall send him to the corner, as she had promised. Very good, she would do so. She gave Johnny a sort of a lecture on badness and disobedience generally, and wounding people's feelings in particular, gave him an apple, which he was to eat in the corner, and made him say two short answers in the "Shorter Catechism," and that was the last of the total eclipse at our house.

text.zh-Hans:
前番日食，吾乡所见之掩蔽，较历书所示者为甚，远逾吾侪所料。

吾家小圈子里，对此次日食议论甚多，众人兴致勃勃，各自揣想将见何状；凡报纸所载此事，吾侪无不读过。

吾家管家妇曾见三四年之大日食，亦见流星坠落，故谈及日食与气象，口吻若神谕。余欲好好观看此次日食，故熏黑玻璃数片，余知诸儿与内人及管家妇皆欲一观，而余欲独得一片自用。

所谓只需在卡片上戳一孔，便可于地板或铺石路面上见到「日食之准确影像」，借此妥善观测此象，纯属荒唐。余试过了。起初结果尚令人满意，影中日轮缺去一块，如被咬去一口之饼干；然缺处并不如理应那般渐增，余遂察觉，其所以似为局部之掩[…]，乃锯齿状孔洞中一个几乎难以察觉之部分所致。吾侪皆有格致之兴，此一发现，使余在家中以洞察入微之格致观测而居首位；余为此心情大好。

然吾家管家妇殊非常人。日食之前，她已将屋中诸物收拾齐整。——她走出来，取约翰尼熏黑之玻璃以作观测。塞琳娜小姐颇有不屑日食之态。她曾见三四年之大全食，称「如今可没有那样的日食了」。约翰尼将玻璃熏黑的一面执得太近鼻端，鼻尖因而染了一小圆黑点，玻璃上则留下一小圆净处，这对管家妇观日食几成致命之碍。她有凡事皆抓错头尾之不幸本领，先从那小圆净处窥去，旋即断言这根本不是日食；内人素惧塞琳娜小姐与余争论，温言抗议一句，她乃重试。

塞琳娜小姐不易一次只闭一目，故须以左手前三指按住左眼睑，因此在熏黑玻璃上又蹭出三处小净处，左眼睑上及其周围则添三个小圆黑点，使塞琳娜小姐之面容平添几分难看之相。

吾家约翰尼急欲取回玻璃，瞥一眼看其母是否在望，见她仍执意以鼻蹭玻璃熏黑之面，遂轻蔑地望着管家妇，那人不用手按住便闭不了一目。——「她打起枪来，会是怎样的手段？」约翰尼心想。卷发的小「普茜」，吾家次宠，已把玻璃上的黑烟全蹭到脸上，正眯着眼死盯一株橡树之顶以寻日食，且认定上面「有紫色的叶子」。

塞琳娜小姐终于让右眼对准了日食，而约翰尼发现，稍摇葡萄藤，便可借一片叶子造出绝妙之效。塞琳娜小姐正望时，葡萄叶遮于其前，她得意洋洋将玻璃递还约翰尼，宣称已看得满意。吾侪其余诸人所见之所以不为全食，是因不知如何看。她一见全食便识得，且天将转黑，塞琳娜小姐遂决意趁日食进行之际小睡片刻以省时——塞琳娜小姐有一妄念，谓自己白昼不能入睡，故每逢全食一类场合，必借机放纵自己睡上一觉。约翰尼闻此宣告，面露怀疑之色，直如看戏。

然塞琳娜小姐执称，此次日食不算什么，真个全然不算什么，远不及昔年那一回。她说，彼时日光犹如那蒙福之太阳在正午所能给的那般明亮，转瞬之间却漆黑一团。鸡群登架而栖，仿佛审判日已至，牛群哞哞而归，诸儿则啼哭起来，一如日落时他们总要哭的那样，只因不愿上床。

余知管家妇陈述至少不离事实太远，遂探问此说之所本。原来塞琳娜小姐向来循规，当时已决定先小睡，以备观日食之劳，却无人想到唤醒她。直至夜间约十二时，她才骤然惊醒，见四下漆黑如墨，便断定日食方起，且是喧闹声把她自浅浅之「猫盹」中吵醒，而那已是她仅有的睡眠；她冲入卧室，抱起当时尚在襁褓中的婴孩，狂奔越过摇篮，跌倒之际压断了那无辜小儿的鼻子，家中那一员之鼻至今变形，缘由即在此。余将此小事告知内人，内人叮嘱约翰尼切勿对塞琳娜小姐或任何孩子提起，并附以威胁：若违，罚站墙角。余不敢断言约翰尼是否果真说过，然翌晨早餐时，塞琳娜小姐现身，神情异常庄重而认命。她以不祥之肃穆抚平雪白围裙，仿佛世上唯一孤苦女子，却全然顺受「命运无常之矢石」。执茶壶从未如此手稳；加糖从未如此精准。必有不对。内人审视约翰尼，约翰尼目光闪躲。余是严厉之人，遂以凶兆般的可怕目光瞪向那男孩；他正抢盘中最后一块热松饼，以阻其小妹对此美味的渴念，余想那一瞪他终究没有领受分毫。

得便时，余欲问约翰尼，对那日食故事，他是否做了他母亲嘱他不可做之事。然内人从中阻拦，说余不该诱他撒谎。余坚持她须惩罚他，须送他去墙角，如她所许。很好，她照办了。她对约翰尼训诫一番，泛论顽劣与悖命，尤论伤人情面，继而给他一只苹果，令他在墙角吃下，又命他背诵《小教理问答》中两条简短答语，吾家全食之事遂以此告终。
text.zh-Hant:
前番日食，吾鄉所見之掩蔽，較曆書所示者為甚，遠逾吾儕所料。

吾家管家婦曾見三四年之大日食，亦見流星墜落，故談及日食與氣象，口吻若神諭。余欲好好觀看此次日食，故燻黑玻璃數片，余知諸兒與內人及管家婦皆欲一觀，而余欲獨得一片自用。
