text_orig:
THE COURSE OF THE ECLIPSE IN THE UNITED STATES.

Mr. A. N. Skinner, of the Dearborn Observatory of Chicago, has prepared the following exact statement of the course of the eclipse across the North American Continent, the places which lie in the track of the shadowy cone of the moon, and also a time-table, giving the hours and minutes of its beginning and end at the principal cities touched. The following are his calculations:—

The partial shadow of the moon first touches the earth in longitude west from Washington 138 degrees, and north latitude 37 degrees. The umbra, or the total shadow, touches the earth in longitude 165 degrees west from Washington, and in north latitude 53 degrees. In other words, at the first of these localities the dark body of the moon is seen to touch the sun earlier than at any place, just as the sun is rising. At the second locality the dark body of the moon is seen to wholly obscure the sun when the sun's centre is in the horizon. The umbra of the moon travels at first in a northeasterly direction toward Behring Straits, where it bends gradually eastward, and from Behring Straits it begins to travel in a southeasterly direction, which general direction it holds across British America and the United States. To speak definitely, the central line of the path of the umbra enters the territory of the United States about 200 miles northwest of Fort Union, which is situated at the junction of the Yellowstone and the Missouri rivers.

It sweeps southeast across the territory of Dacotah and enters the State of Iowa near its northwestern boundary, and passes near the following places:—

In Iowa—Cherokee, Cherokee county; New Munich, Sac county; Calhoun, Calhoun county; Quincy, Boone county; Boonsboro, Boone county; Belle Point, Boone county; Monroe, Jasper county; Oskaloosa, Mahaska county; Marysville, Wapello county; Fairfield, Jefferson county; Salem, Henry county; Lee City, Lee county; Fort Madison, Lee county.

In Illinois—In the State of Illinois the following places are near the central line:—Colchester, McDonough county; Astoria, Fulton county; Bath, Mason county; New Salem, Menard county; Springfield, Sangamon county; Moawequa, Shelby county; Shelbyville, Shelby county; Neoga, Cumberland county; Rose Hill, Jasper county.

In Indiana—The central line passes near the following places:—Washington, Daviess county, Corydon, Harrison county.

In Kentucky—The following places are near the central line:—Fairfield, Nelson county; Danville, Boyle county; Manchester, Clay county.

In Virginia—The following places are near the central line:—Estillville, Scott county; Bristol, Washington county.

In Tennessee—Taylorsville, Johnson county, is near the central line.

In North Carolina—The central line passes near the following places:—Boone, Watauga county; Carthage, Moore county; Fayetteville, Cumberland county; Leesburg, New Hanover county.

The Northern Limit of the Umbra—Or total shadow, passes near the following places in Iowa:—Forrest City, Winnebago county, just outside; Mason City, Cerro Gordo county, just outside; Clear Lake City, quite near the line; Clarksville, Butler county, just outside; Cedar Falls, Black Hawk county, inside; Independence, Buchanan county, outside; Anamosa, Jones county, outside; Wolcott, Scott county, inside; Davenport, Iowa.

In Illinois—The northern edge of the umbra passes near the following places:—Rock Island, Rock Island county, inside; Hampton, Rock Island county, near the line; Colona, Henry county, inside; Neponset, Bureau county, near the line; Lacon, Marshall county, inside; Chenoa, McLean county, inside; Paxton, Ford county, inside; Danville, Vermillion county, inside.

Indiana.—The following places in Indiana are near the northern edge of the umbra:—Bainbridge, Putnam county, inside; Franklin, Johnson county, inside; Versailles, Ripley county, inside; Rising Sun, Ohio county, near the line.

Kentucky.—The following places in Kentucky are near the northern line of the umbra:—Warsaw, Gallatin county, inside; Williams, Grant county, inside; Carlisle, Bourbon county, inside; Triplet, Rowan county, near the line; Paintville, Johnson county.

In Virginia—The following places are near the northern edge:—Arrocoina, Logan county, near the line; Mechanicsburg, Bland county, inside; Newburn, Pulaski county, inside; Danville, Pittsylvania county, inside.

In North Carolina—The following places are near the northern limit of the umbra:—Roxboro, Person county, inside; Greenville, Pitt county, inside; Hatteras Inlet, near the line.

The Southern Limit of the Umbra—Passes near the following places in Iowa:—Council Bluffs, near the line; Frankford, Montgomery county, inside; Mt. Ayr, Ringgold county, inside.

In Missouri—The southern line of total eclipse passes near the following places:—Princeton, Mercer county, near the line; Shelbyville, Shelby county, inside; Bowling Green, Pike county, inside.

In Illinois—The following places are near the southern limit of the umbra:—Alton, Madison county, inside; Edwardsville, Madison county, inside; Covington, Washington county, inside; Mt. Vernon, Jefferson county, inside; McLeansboro, Hamilton county, inside; New Haven, Gallatin county.

The State of Indiana—Barely extends, at its southwestern point, to the southern limit of the umbra.

Kentucky—The following places in Kentucky are near the southern line of the umbra:—Smithville, Henderson county, inside; Morgantown, Butler county, inside; Burksville, Cumberland county, inside.

In Tennessee—The following are near the southern edge of the umbra:—Huntsville, Scott county, inside; Knoxville, Knox county, near the line; Sevierville, Sevier county, inside.

In North Carolina—Asheville, Buncombe county, is within, and Columbus, Polk county, is near the line.

In South Carolina—The following places are near the southern line of the umbra:—Yorkville, York county, inside; Marion, Marion county, near the line; Cherry Grove, Horry county, near the line.

Places which are within the northern and southern limits, as above described, will be within the total shadow, and at these places the eclipse will be total. Places outside of these lines will have a partial eclipse of greater or less magnitude, according as it is near or far from these limits.

text.zh-Hans:
日食行经合众国之路径

芝加哥迪尔伯恩天文台 A. N. Skinner 先生，已就日食横贯北美大陆之路径、月影之锥所经之地，具一确切之陈述，并列时刻表，载各主要城市所触及者食始食终之时刻。其所推算如下：——

月之半影初触地球，在华盛顿以西经度一百三十八度，北纬三十七度。本影，即全影，触地于华盛顿以西经度一百六十五度，北纬五十三度。换言之，前一处所见月之暗体触日，较他处为早，时则日方出；后一处所见月之暗体全掩日轮，时则日心适在地平。月之本影初向东北行，趋白令海峡，渐折而东；自白令海峡起转向东南行，其大势经英属美洲及合众国皆如是。确言之，本影路径之中线入合众国境，在 Fort Union 西北约二百英里，Fort Union 居黄石河与密苏里河合流处。

斜向东南，横贯达科他地，入艾奥瓦州，近其西北界，所过近旁诸地如下：——

艾奥瓦州——Cherokee 县之 Cherokee；Sac 县之 New Munich；Calhoun 县之 Calhoun；Boone 县之昆西；Boone 县之布恩斯伯勒；Boone 县之 Belle Point；贾斯珀县之门罗；Mahaska 县之奥斯卡卢萨；Wapello 县之马里斯维尔；杰斐逊县之 Fairfield；亨利县之塞勒姆；Lee 县之 Lee City；Lee 县之 Fort Madison．

伊利诺伊州——该州近中线诸地如下：——McDonough 县之 Colchester；富尔顿县之 Astoria；Mason 县之 Bath；Menard 县之 New Salem；Sangamon 县之斯普林菲尔德；Shelby 县之 Moawequa；Shelby 县之谢尔比维尔；Cumberland 县之 Neoga；贾斯珀县之 Rose Hill．

印第安纳州——中线近旁经过下列诸地：——Daviess 县之华盛顿；Harrison 县之 Corydon．

肯塔基州——近中线诸地如下：——Nelson 县之 Fairfield；Boyle 县之丹维尔；Clay 县之曼彻斯特。

弗吉尼亚州——近中线诸地如下：——Scott 县之 Estillville；华盛顿县之布里斯托尔。

田纳西州——Johnson 县之 Taylorsville 近中线。

北卡罗来纳州——中线近旁经过下列诸地：——Watauga 县之 Boone；Moore 县之 Carthage；Cumberland 县之费耶特维尔；New Hanover 县之 Leesburg．

本影之北界——即全影——过艾奥瓦州下列诸地之近旁：——Winnebago 县之 Forrest City，恰在界外；Cerro Gordo 县之 Mason City，恰在界外；Clear Lake City，甚近界线；巴特勒县之克拉克斯维尔，恰在界外；Black Hawk 县之锡达福尔斯，在界内；Buchanan 县之因迪彭登斯，在界外；Jones 县之 Anamosa，在界外；Scott 县之 Wolcott，在界内；艾奥瓦州之达文波特。

text.en:
THE COURSE OF THE ECLIPSE IN THE UNITED STATES.

Mr. A. N. Skinner, of the Dearborn Observatory of Chicago, has prepared the following exact statement of the course of the eclipse across the North American Continent, the places which lie in the track of the shadowy cone of the moon, and also a time-table, giving the hours and minutes of its beginning and end at the principal cities touched. The following are his calculations:—

The partial shadow of the moon first touches the earth in longitude west from Washington 138 degrees, and north latitude 37 degrees. The umbra, or the total shadow, touches the earth in longitude 165 degrees west from Washington, and in north latitude 53 degrees. In other words, at the first of these localities the dark body of the moon is seen to touch the sun earlier than at any place, just as the sun is rising. At the second locality the dark body of the moon is seen to wholly obscure the sun when the sun's centre is in the horizon. The umbra of the moon travels at first in a northeasterly direction toward Behring Straits, where it bends gradually eastward, and from Behring Straits it begins to travel in a southeasterly direction, which general direction it holds across British America and the United States. To speak definitely, the central line of the path of the umbra enters the territory of the United States about 200 miles northwest of Fort Union, which is situated at the junction of the Yellowstone and the Missouri rivers.

It sweeps southeast across the territory of Dacotah and enters the State of Iowa near its northwestern boundary, and passes near the following places:—

In Iowa—Cherokee, Cherokee county; New Munich, Sac county; Calhoun, Calhoun county; Quincy, Boone county; Boonsboro, Boone county; Belle Point, Boone county; Monroe, Jasper county; Oskaloosa, Mahaska county; Marysville, Wapello county; Fairfield, Jefferson county; Salem, Henry county; Lee City, Lee county; Fort Madison, Lee county.

In Illinois—In the State of Illinois the following places are near the central line:—Colchester, McDonough county; Astoria, Fulton county; Bath, Mason county; New Salem, Menard county; Springfield, Sangamon county; Moawequa, Shelby county; Shelbyville, Shelby county; Neoga, Cumberland county; Rose Hill, Jasper county.

In Indiana—The central line passes near the following places:—Washington, Daviess county, Corydon, Harrison county.

In Kentucky—The following places are near the central line:—Fairfield, Nelson county; Danville, Boyle county; Manchester, Clay county.

In Virginia—The following places are near the central line:—Estillville, Scott county; Bristol, Washington county.

In Tennessee—Taylorsville, Johnson county, is near the central line.

In North Carolina—The central line passes near the following places:—Boone, Watauga county; Carthage, Moore county; Fayetteville, Cumberland county; Leesburg, New Hanover county.

The Northern Limit of the Umbra—Or total shadow, passes near the following places in Iowa:—Forrest City, Winnebago county, just outside; Mason City, Cerro Gordo county, just outside; Clear Lake City, quite near the line; Clarksville, Butler county, just outside; Cedar Falls, Black Hawk county, inside; Independence, Buchanan county, outside; Anamosa, Jones county, outside; Wolcott, Scott county, inside; Davenport, Iowa.

In Illinois—The northern edge of the umbra passes near the following places:—Rock Island, Rock Island county, inside; Hampton, Rock Island county, near the line; Colona, Henry county, inside; Neponset, Bureau county, near the line; Lacon, Marshall county, inside; Chenoa, McLean county, inside; Paxton, Ford county, inside; Danville, Vermillion county, inside.

Indiana.—The following places in Indiana are near the northern edge of the umbra:—Bainbridge, Putnam county, inside; Franklin, Johnson county, inside; Versailles, Ripley county, inside; Rising Sun, Ohio county, near the line.

Kentucky.—The following places in Kentucky are near the northern line of the umbra:—Warsaw, Gallatin county, inside; Williams, Grant county, inside; Carlisle, Bourbon county, inside; Triplet, Rowan county, near the line; Paintville, Johnson county.

In Virginia—The following places are near the northern edge:—Arrocoina, Logan county, near the line; Mechanicsburg, Bland county, inside; Newburn, Pulaski county, inside; Danville, Pittsylvania county, inside.

In North Carolina—The following places are near the northern limit of the umbra:—Roxboro, Person county, inside; Greenville, Pitt county, inside; Hatteras Inlet, near the line.

The Southern Limit of the Umbra—Passes near the following places in Iowa:—Council Bluffs, near the line; Frankford, Montgomery county, inside; Mt. Ayr, Ringgold county, inside.

In Missouri—The southern line of total eclipse passes near the following places:—Princeton, Mercer county, near the line; Shelbyville, Shelby county, inside; Bowling Green, Pike county, inside.

In Illinois—The following places are near the southern limit of the umbra:—Alton, Madison county, inside; Edwardsville, Madison county, inside; Covington, Washington county, inside; Mt. Vernon, Jefferson county, inside; McLeansboro, Hamilton county, inside; New Haven, Gallatin county.

The State of Indiana—Barely extends, at its southwestern point, to the southern limit of the umbra.

Kentucky—The following places in Kentucky are near the southern line of the umbra:—Smithville, Henderson county, inside; Morgantown, Butler county, inside; Burksville, Cumberland county, inside.

In Tennessee—The following are near the southern edge of the umbra:—Huntsville, Scott county, inside; Knoxville, Knox county, near the line; Sevierville, Sevier county, inside.

In North Carolina—Asheville, Buncombe county, is within, and Columbus, Polk county, is near the line.

In South Carolina—The following places are near the southern line of the umbra:—Yorkville, York county, inside; Marion, Marion county, near the line; Cherry Grove, Horry county, near the line.

LA TRAJECTOIRE DE L'ÉCLIPSE AUX ÉTATS-UNIS.

M. A. N. Skinner, de l'observatoire Dearborn de Chicago, a préparé l'exposé exact suivant de la trajectoire de l'éclipse à travers le continent nord-américain, des lieux qui se trouvent sur la route du cône d'ombre de la Lune, ainsi qu'un tableau horaire donnant les heures et minutes de son début et de sa fin dans les principales villes touchées. Voici ses calculs :—

L'ombre partielle de la Lune touche d'abord la Terre à 138 degrés de longitude ouest depuis Washington et à 37 degrés de latitude nord. L'umbra, ou ombre totale, touche la Terre à 165 degrés de longitude ouest depuis Washington et à 53 degrés de latitude nord. En d'autres termes, au premier de ces lieux, on voit le corps sombre de la Lune toucher le Soleil plus tôt qu'en tout autre endroit, juste au lever du soleil. Au second lieu, on voit le corps sombre de la Lune obscurcir entièrement le Soleil lorsque le centre du Soleil est à l'horizon. L'umbra de la Lune se déplace d'abord dans une direction nord-est vers le détroit de Behring, où elle s'infléchit peu à peu vers l'est, et à partir du détroit de Behring elle commence à se déplacer dans une direction sud-est, direction générale qu'elle garde à travers l'Amérique britannique et les États-Unis. Pour parler avec précision, la ligne centrale de la trajectoire de l'umbra entre dans le territoire des États-Unis à environ 200 milles au nord-ouest de Fort Union, qui est situé au confluent des rivières Yellowstone et Missouri.

Elle balaie le sud-est à travers le territoire de Dakota et entre dans l'État d'Iowa près de sa limite nord-ouest, et passe près des lieux suivants :—

Vernon, comté de Jefferson, à l'intérieur ; McLeansboro, comté de Hamilton, à l'intérieur ; New Haven, comté de Gallatin.

L'État d'Indiana — Atteint à peine, par sa pointe sud-ouest, la limite sud de l'umbra.

text.es:
EL RECORRIDO DEL ECLIPSE EN LOS ESTADOS UNIDOS.

El señor A. N. Skinner, del Observatorio Dearborn de Chicago, ha preparado la siguiente exposición exacta del recorrido del eclipse a través del continente norteamericano, de los lugares que se hallan en la trayectoria del cono de sombra de la Luna, y también un cuadro de horas, que da las horas y los minutos de su comienzo y su fin en las principales ciudades tocadas. Sus cálculos son los siguientes:—

La sombra parcial de la Luna toca por primera vez la Tierra en la longitud 138 grados al oeste de Washington y la latitud 37 grados norte. La umbra, o sombra total, toca la Tierra en la longitud 165 grados al oeste de Washington y la latitud 53 grados norte. En otras palabras, en la primera de estas localidades se ve que el cuerpo oscuro de la Luna toca el Sol antes que en ningún otro lugar, justo cuando el Sol sale. En la segunda localidad se ve que el cuerpo oscuro de la Luna oculta por completo el Sol cuando el centro del Sol está en el horizonte. La umbra de la Luna viaja al principio en dirección nordeste hacia el estrecho de Bering, donde gira poco a poco hacia el este, y desde el estrecho de Bering comienza a viajar en dirección sudeste, dirección general que mantiene a través de la América británica y los Estados Unidos. Para hablar con precisión, la línea central de la trayectoria de la umbra entra en el territorio de los Estados Unidos unas 200 millas al noroeste de Fort Union, situado en la confluencia de los ríos Yellowstone y Missouri.

Barre hacia el sudeste el territorio de Dacotah y entra en el estado de Iowa cerca de su límite noroeste, y pasa cerca de los lugares siguientes:—

En Iowa — Cherokee, condado de Cherokee; New Munich, condado de Sac; Calhoun, condado de Calhoun; Quincy, condado de Boone; Boonsboro, condado de Boone; Belle Point, condado de Boone; Monroe, condado de Jasper; Oskaloosa, condado de Mahaska; Marysville, condado de Wapello; Fairfield, condado de Jefferson; Salem, condado de Henry; Lee City, condado de Lee; Fort Madison, condado de Lee.

En Illinois — En el estado de Illinois los siguientes lugares están cerca de la línea central:—Colchester, condado de McDonough; Astoria, condado de Fulton; Bath, condado de Mason; New Salem, condado de Menard; Springfield, condado de Sangamon; Moawequa, condado de Shelby; Shelbyville, condado de Shelby; Neoga, condado de Cumberland; Rose Hill, condado de Jasper.

En Indiana — La línea central pasa cerca de los lugares siguientes:—Washington, condado de Daviess, Corydon, condado de Harrison.

En Kentucky — Los siguientes lugares están cerca de la línea central:—Fairfield, condado de Nelson; Danville, condado de Boyle; Manchester, condado de Clay.

En Virginia — Los siguientes lugares están cerca de la línea central:—Estillville, condado de Scott; Bristol, condado de Washington.

En Tennessee — Taylorsville, condado de Johnson, está cerca de la línea central.

En Carolina del Norte — La línea central pasa cerca de los lugares siguientes:—Boone, condado de Watauga; Carthage, condado de Moore; Fayetteville, condado de Cumberland; Leesburg, condado de New Hanover.

El límite norte de la umbra — O sombra total, pasa cerca de los lugares siguientes de Iowa:—Forrest City, condado de Winnebago, justo fuera; Mason City, condado de Cerro Gordo, justo fuera; Clear Lake City, muy cerca de la línea; Clarksville, condado de Butler, justo fuera; Cedar Falls, condado de Black Hawk, dentro; Independence, condado de Buchanan, fuera; Anamosa, condado de Jones, fuera; Wolcott, condado de Scott, dentro; Davenport, Iowa.

En Illinois — El borde norte de la umbra pasa cerca de los lugares siguientes:—Rock Island, condado de Rock Island, dentro; Hampton, condado de Rock Island, cerca de la línea; Colona, condado de Henry, dentro; Neponset, condado de Bureau, cerca de la línea; Lacon, condado de Marshall, dentro; Chenoa, condado de McLean, dentro; Paxton, condado de Ford, dentro; Danville, condado de Vermillion, dentro.

Indiana. — Los siguientes lugares de Indiana están cerca del borde norte de la umbra:—Bainbridge, condado de Putnam, dentro; Franklin, condado de Johnson, dentro; Versailles, condado de Ripley, dentro; Rising Sun, condado de Ohio, cerca de la línea.

Kentucky. — Los siguientes lugares de Kentucky están cerca de la línea norte de la umbra:—Warsaw, condado de Gallatin, dentro; Williams, condado de Grant, dentro; Carlisle, condado de Bourbon, dentro; Triplet, condado de Rowan, cerca de la línea; Paintville, condado de Johnson.

En Virginia — Los siguientes lugares están cerca del borde norte:—Arrocoina, condado de Logan, cerca de la línea; Mechanicsburg, condado de Bland, dentro; Newburn, condado de Pulaski, dentro; Danville, condado de Pittsylvania, dentro.

En Carolina del Norte — Los siguientes lugares están cerca del límite norte de la umbra:—Roxboro, condado de Person, dentro; Greenville, condado de Pitt, dentro; Hatteras Inlet, cerca de la línea.

El límite sur de la umbra — Pasa cerca de los lugares siguientes de Iowa:—Council Bluffs, cerca de la línea; Frankford, condado de Montgomery, dentro; Mt. Ayr, condado de Ringgold, dentro.

En Missouri — La línea sur del eclipse total pasa cerca de los lugares siguientes:—Princeton, condado de Mercer, cerca de la línea; Shelbyville, condado de Shelby, dentro; Bowling Green, condado de Pike, dentro.

En Illinois — Los siguientes lugares están cerca del límite sur de la umbra:—Alton, condado de Madison, dentro; Edwardsville, condado de Madison, dentro; Covington, condado de Washington, dentro; Mt. Vernon, condado de Jefferson, dentro; McLeansboro, condado de Hamilton, dentro; New Haven, condado de Gallatin.

El estado de Indiana — Alcanza apenas, en su extremo suroeste, el límite sur de la umbra.

Kentucky — Los siguientes lugares de Kentucky están cerca de la línea sur de la umbra:—Smithville, condado de Henderson, dentro; Morgantown, condado de Butler, dentro; Burksville, condado de Cumberland, dentro.

En Tennessee — Los siguientes están cerca del borde sur de la umbra:—Huntsville, condado de Scott, dentro; Knoxville, condado de Knox, cerca de la línea; Sevierville, condado de Sevier, dentro.

En Carolina del Norte — Asheville, condado de Buncombe, está dentro, y Columbus, condado de Polk, está cerca de la línea.

En Carolina del Sur — Los siguientes lugares están cerca de la línea sur de la umbra:—Yorkville, condado de York, dentro; Marion, condado de Marion, cerca de la línea; Cherry Grove, condado de Horry, cerca de la línea.

Los lugares que están dentro de los límites norte y sur, tal como se han descrito, estarán dentro de la sombra total, y en esos lugares el eclipse será total. Los lugares fuera de esas líneas tendrán un eclipse parcial de mayor o menor magnitud, según estén cerca o lejos de esos límites.

text.it:
IL PERCORSO DELL'ECLISSI NEGLI STATI UNITI.

Il signor A. N. Skinner, dell'Osservatorio Dearborn di Chicago, ha preparato la seguente esposizione esatta del percorso dell'eclissi attraverso il continente nordamericano, dei luoghi che si trovano sulla traccia del cono d'ombra della Luna, e anche una tabella oraria che dà le ore e i minuti del suo inizio e della sua fine nelle principali città toccate. Ecco i suoi calcoli:—

La penombra della Luna tocca per la prima volta la Terra a una longitudine di 138 gradi a ovest di Washington e a una latitudine di 37 gradi nord. L'ombra, ovvero l'ombra totale, tocca la Terra a una longitudine di 165 gradi a ovest di Washington e a una latitudine di 53 gradi nord. In altre parole, nella prima di queste località si vede il corpo oscuro della Luna toccare il Sole prima che in qualsiasi altro luogo, proprio mentre il Sole sorge. Nella seconda località si vede il corpo oscuro della Luna oscurare completamente il Sole quando il centro del Sole è all'orizzonte. L'ombra della Luna viaggia dapprima in direzione nord-est verso lo Stretto di Bering, dove piega gradualmente verso est, e dallo Stretto di Bering comincia a viaggiare in direzione sud-est, direzione generale che mantiene attraverso l'America britannica e gli Stati Uniti. Per parlare con precisione, la linea centrale del percorso dell'ombra entra nel territorio degli Stati Uniti circa 200 miglia a nord-ovest di Fort Union, che si trova alla confluenza dei fiumi Yellowstone e Missouri.

Essa spazza il sud-est attraverso il territorio del Dacotah ed entra nello Stato dell'Iowa presso il suo confine nord-occidentale, e passa vicino ai luoghi seguenti:—

合衆国における日食の経路

シカゴのディアボーン天文台のA・N・スキナー氏は、北アメリカ大陸を横切る日食の経路、月の影の円錐の通り道にあたる場所、さらに、通過する主要な都市での食の始まりと終わりの時と分を示す時刻表について、次のような正確な報告を用意した。以下が彼の計算である：—

月の半影が最初に地球に触れるのは、ワシントンから西経138度、北緯37度のところである。本影、すなわち完全な影が地球に触れるのは、ワシントンから西経165度、北緯53度のところである。言い換えれば、この最初の場所では、ちょうど太陽が昇るときに、月の暗い天体がどこよりも早く太陽に触れるのが見られる。二番目の場所では、太陽の中心が地平線上にあるときに、月の暗い天体が太陽を完全に覆い隠すのが見られる。月の本影ははじめ北東の方向にベーリング海峡へ向かって進み、そこで次第に東へ曲がり、ベーリング海峡からは南東の方向に進み始め、この大まかな方向をイギリス領アメリカと合衆国を横切って保つ。はっきり言えば、本影の経路の中心線は、イエローストーン川とミズーリ川の合流点にあるフォート・ユニオンの北西約200マイルのところで、合衆国の領域に入る。

text_orig:
At about five o'clock this afternoon,—or, to be precise,—at just three minutes after five o'clock, if the weather is such as to admit of seeing it—for their will be no postponement on account of the weather—a round, dark screen or cover may be seen touching the lower edge of the face of the "glorious orb of day," and gradually extend itself over the sun's disc until all except the northern edge will be completely covered. If the sky happens to be unusually clear, it will become dark enough only to render lights necessary to read indoors; but if it happens to be cloudy, the darkness will be equal, considerably before sundown, to an ordinary moonless night.

The cause of this marvelous deviation from the ordinary every day routine of nature, is the great eclipse. It is nothing to be alarmed about, startling as are its phenomena, for it is a very ordinary occurrence, one or two happening every year, but not often on so large a scale. Twice in every year, about the 1st of February and the 1st of August, the sun and earth get so nearly in a position to place the moon exactly on a line between them, that a portion, and sometimes the whole shadow of the moon falls upon the earth, and at whatever positions of the earth this shadow falls, the sun is eclipsed.

Astronomers say that there are three kinds of eclipses of the sun, partial, total, and annular. A partial eclipse is, of course, when only a portion, or one side of the sun's disc is hidden; a total eclipse is when the whole disc is hidden, and an annular eclipse when the moon don't appear to be large enough to cover the whole face of the sun, and there is a bright ring left around it. Now why, the reader may ask, is it that the eclipse of the sun is sometimes total and sometimes annular? Are there times when the moon is larger, or the sun smaller? No—but sometimes the sun as well as the moon is further off than at other times. Standing some distance from a pane of glass in your room, it appears nearly as large as a building a square or two away: but go nearer the window, and we shall see the pane larger proportionably than the building. So when the moon is nearer, or the sun farther off, the shadow falling upon the earth is proportionably larger, and vice versa.

The eclipse this afternoon will be of the kind called total, except that Ottawa lies a little to far north too have it total here. To see it exactly over the center of the sun we must be at Springfield, or anywhere on a straight line running diagonally across the earth from northern Siberia, through Alaska, Iowa, Illinois, Kentucky and North Carolina.

Of all phenomena in the way of eclipses, a total eclipse of the sun is the most sublime. "During a space of time not exceeding eight minutes," says a writer on eclipses, " we observe the passage from a sunlight to a darkness almost like that of night and back again. The sky, as the partial eclipse grows larger and larger, changes its tints to various hues, described sometimes as livid, but mingled with orange yellow, or purple, sometimes much before the beginning of the total eclipse proper. The moon advances slowly over the solar disc, covering more and more of it with its blackness, and making more and more obscure objects, till, when the last gleam of sunlight is about to pass away, the observer sees the moon and what remains of the sun surrounded by a bright corona or glory, such as surrounds the heads of the Lord and the saints in religious pictures. When the sunlight totally disappears, nothing is left to enlighten objects around, save the scattered rays of twilight and the corona itself. This glory is intersected here and there with flashing rays, extending often to considerable distances from the sun, and has been itself seen nearly as broad as the sun's diameter. When the corona gives the light by which objects are seen, they naturally appear very differently from what we see in daylight, or even at night. The sharpness and blackness of distant hills have often been noticed.

"Besides this corona, the protuberances of a rosy color and irregular shape are a very marked feature. These are cloud-like masses seen projecting beyond the dark edge of the moon, are not generally visible without telescopes, and have long been, as well as the corona, mysterious in their origin. But it is now made certain by the spectroscope that they are gaseous in nature; it was found out by photographing them that they were connected with the sun, and that as the moon passed over them it hid them by degrees. If they were phenomena of the lunar atmosphere they would move with the moon itself, which they do not do."

The pity is, that grand as are these phenomena, we are a trifle too far north to see them at Ottawa, were the sky even all that could be wished. Yet the show will be far from trivial here, and as all our subscribers will have a free ticket, we advise them to make the most of it, as they will hardly live to see another eclipse of the sun so nearly total as this will be at Ottawa.

text.zh-Hans:
今日午后约五时——或谓，确切言之——恰在五时三分，倘天气容人得见——因不会为天气而延期——则一圆形黑幕或覆盖物，将见其触及「光荣日轮」之下缘，渐渐展于日面，直至除北缘外全被遮蔽。天若特别晴朗，所暗仅使室内读书须点灯；天若有云，则日落前许久，其暗已与寻常无月之夜相等。

自然寻常日常之程序，忽有此惊人之偏离，其故乃大日食。其象虽骇人，实不必惊慌，因其为极寻常之事，每年有一二次，唯少有如此大者。每年二次，约在二月一日与八月一日，日与地所处近乎使月正在二者连线之上，月影之一部，有时为全影，落于地，影所落之地无论何处，日即被食。

天文学家云日食有三种：偏食、全食、环食。偏食，自然是日面仅一部分，或一侧被遮；全食则全面被遮；环食则月似不足以尽掩日之全面，周围留一明亮之环。今读者或问：日食何以有时全，有时环？岂有时月较大，或日较小？否——乃日与月有时较他时更远。立于离室中窗玻璃稍远处，其似与一二个街区外之房屋相若；然近窗，则见玻璃按比例较房屋大。故月近，或日远，则落于地之影按比例大，反之亦然。

今午后之食将属所谓全食，唯渥太华稍偏北，此处不得全食。欲见其正在日心之上，须在斯普林菲尔德，或沿一直线任何地方，此线斜贯地球，自西伯利亚北部，经阿拉斯加、艾奥瓦、伊利诺伊、肯塔基、北卡罗来纳。

日食诸象之中，日全食最为壮丽。「不过八分钟之间」，一论食之作者云，「吾人见由日光入近乎夜之暗，复返于光。偏食愈来愈大，天色变为各种色调，或谓铅青而杂橙黄，或紫，有时远在全食本时之前。月缓缓进于日面，以其黑色愈掩愈多，使物愈见模糊，及最后一缕日光将逝，观者见月与日之余，围以明亮之日冕或荣光，如宗教画中围主与诸圣头之荣光。日光尽逝，周围物无可照，惟余曙暮散光与日冕本身。此荣光处处为闪射之线所交错，常远射至距日甚远之处，其本身所见几与日径等阔。日冕供光使见物，则物自然与日间所见，甚至夜间所见皆大异。远山之尖锐与黑，常为人所注意。

「除此日冕外，玫瑰色而形状不规则之突起，亦是极显著之特征。此为云状之团块，见突出于月之暗缘之外，无望远镜一般不可见，与日冕一样，久为来源之谜。然今已由分光镜证定其为气体；由摄影查出其与日相连，月过其上，渐次遮蔽。若为月大气之象，则当随月而动，而其不然。」

可惜者，此诸象虽壮，吾辈在渥太华稍偏北，不能得见，纵天空尽如人愿亦然。然此处之景亦远非微末，且吾报订户皆得一张免费入场券，劝其善用，因其恐难复见一次日食，近于全食如渥太华所见之此次者。
text.zh-Hant:

自然尋常日常之程序，忽有此驚人之偏離，其故乃大日食。其象雖駭人，實不必驚慌，因其為極尋常之事，每年有一二次，唯少有如此大者。每年二次，約在二月一日與八月一日，日與地所處近乎使月正在二者連線之上，月影之一部，有時為全影，落於地，影所落之地無論何處，日即被食。

今午後之食將屬所謂全食，唯渥太華稍偏北，此處不得全食。欲見其正在日心之上，須在斯普林菲爾德，或沿一直線任何地方，此線斜貫地球，自西伯利亞北部，經阿拉斯加、艾奧瓦、伊利諾伊、肯塔基、北卡羅來納。

日食諸象之中，日全食最為壯麗。「不過八分鐘之間」，一論食之作者雲，「吾人見由日光入近乎夜之暗，復返於光。偏食愈來愈大，天色變為各種色調，或謂鉛青而雜橙黃，或紫，有時遠在全食本時之前。月緩緩進於日面，以其黑色愈掩愈多，使物愈見模糊，及最後一縷日光將逝，觀者見月與日之餘，圍以明亮之日冕或榮光，如宗教畫中圍主與諸聖頭之榮光。日光盡逝，周圍物無可照，惟餘曙暮散光與日冕本身。此榮光處處為閃射之線所交錯，常遠射至距日甚遠之處，其本身所見幾與日徑等闊。日冕供光使見物，則物自然與日間所見，甚至夜間所見皆大異。遠山之尖鋭與黑，常為人所注意。

「除此日冕外，玫瑰色而形狀不規則之突起，亦是極顯著之特徵。此為雲狀之團塊，見突出於月之暗緣之外，無望遠鏡一般不可見，與日冕一樣，久為來源之謎。然今已由分光鏡證定其為氣體；由攝影查出其與日相連，月過其上，漸次遮蔽。若為月大氣之象，則當隨月而動，而其不然。」

可惜者，此諸象雖壯，吾輩在渥太華稍偏北，不能得見，縱天空盡如人願亦然。然此處之景亦遠非微末，且吾報訂户皆得一張免費入場券，勸其善用，因其恐難復見一次日食，近於全食如渥太華所見之此次者。
text.en:
At about five o'clock this afternoon,—or, to be precise,—at just three minutes after five o'clock, if the weather is such as to admit of seeing it—for their will be no postponement on account of the weather—a round, dark screen or cover may be seen touching the lower edge of the face of the "glorious orb of day," and gradually extend itself over the sun's disc until all except the northern edge will be completely covered. If the sky happens to be unusually clear, it will become dark enough only to render lights necessary to read indoors; but if it happens to be cloudy, the darkness will be equal, considerably before sundown, to an ordinary moonless night.

The cause of this marvelous deviation from the ordinary every day routine of nature, is the great eclipse. It is nothing to be alarmed about, startling as are its phenomena, for it is a very ordinary occurrence, one or two happening every year, but not often on so large a scale. Twice in every year, about the 1st of February and the 1st of August, the sun and earth get so nearly in a position to place the moon exactly on a line between them, that a portion, and sometimes the whole shadow of the moon falls upon the earth, and at whatever positions of the earth this shadow falls, the sun is eclipsed.

Astronomers say that there are three kinds of eclipses of the sun, partial, total, and annular. A partial eclipse is, of course, when only a portion, or one side of the sun's disc is hidden; a total eclipse is when the whole disc is hidden, and an annular eclipse when the moon don't appear to be large enough to cover the whole face of the sun, and there is a bright ring left around it. Now why, the reader may ask, is it that the eclipse of the sun is sometimes total and sometimes annular? Are there times when the moon is larger, or the sun smaller? No—but sometimes the sun as well as the moon is further off than at other times. Standing some distance from a pane of glass in your room, it appears nearly as large as a building a square or two away: but go nearer the window, and we shall see the pane larger proportionably than the building. So when the moon is nearer, or the sun farther off, the shadow falling upon the earth is proportionably larger, and vice versa.

The eclipse this afternoon will be of the kind called total, except that Ottawa lies a little to far north too have it total here. To see it exactly over the center of the sun we must be at Springfield, or anywhere on a straight line running diagonally across the earth from northern Siberia, through Alaska, Iowa, Illinois, Kentucky and North Carolina.

Of all phenomena in the way of eclipses, a total eclipse of the sun is the most sublime. "During a space of time not exceeding eight minutes," says a writer on eclipses, " we observe the passage from a sunlight to a darkness almost like that of night and back again. The sky, as the partial eclipse grows larger and larger, changes its tints to various hues, described sometimes as livid, but mingled with orange yellow, or purple, sometimes much before the beginning of the total eclipse proper. The moon advances slowly over the solar disc, covering more and more of it with its blackness, and making more and more obscure objects, till, when the last gleam of sunlight is about to pass away, the observer sees the moon and what remains of the sun surrounded by a bright corona or glory, such as surrounds the heads of the Lord and the saints in religious pictures. This glory is intersected here and there with flashing rays, extending often to considerable distances from the sun, and has been itself seen nearly as broad as the sun's diameter. When the corona gives the light by which objects are seen, they naturally appear very differently from what we see in daylight, or even at night. The sharpness and blackness of distant hills have often been noticed.

"Besides this corona, the protuberances of a rosy color and irregular shape are a very marked feature. These are cloud-like masses seen projecting beyond the dark edge of the moon, are not generally visible without telescopes, and have long been, as well as the corona, mysterious in their origin. But it is now made certain by the spectroscope that they are gaseous in nature; it was found out by photographing them that they were connected with the sun, and that as the moon passed over them it hid them by degrees. If they were phenomena of the lunar atmosphere they would move with the moon itself, which they do not do."

The pity is, that grand as are these phenomena, we are a trifle too far north to see them at Ottawa, were the sky even all that could be wished. Yet the show will be far from trivial here, and as all our subscribers will have a free ticket, we advise them to make the most of it, as they will hardly live to see another eclipse of the sun so nearly total as this will be at Ottawa.
text.fr:
Vers cinq heures cet après-midi, — ou, pour être précis, — à cinq heures trois minutes précises, si le temps permet de le voir — car il n'y aura aucun report à cause du temps — un écran ou couvercle rond et sombre pourra être vu touchant le bord inférieur de la face du « glorieux astre du jour », et s'étendant peu à peu sur le disque du Soleil jusqu'à ce que tout, sauf le bord nord, soit complètement couvert. Si le ciel se trouve exceptionnellement clair, il ne deviendra assez sombre que pour rendre les lumières nécessaires afin de lire à l'intérieur ; mais s'il se trouve nuageux, l'obscurité égalera, bien avant le coucher du soleil, celle d'une nuit ordinaire sans clair de lune.

La cause de cet écart merveilleux par rapport à la routine ordinaire de tous les jours de la nature est la grande éclipse. Il n'y a pas lieu de s'alarmer, si saisissants que soient ses phénomènes, car c'est un événement très ordinaire, une ou deux se produisant chaque année, mais pas souvent sur une aussi grande échelle. Deux fois par an, vers le 1ᵉʳ février et le 1ᵉʳ août, le Soleil et la Terre se trouvent si près d'être en position de placer la Lune exactement sur une ligne entre eux, qu'une partie, et parfois toute l'ombre de la Lune tombe sur la Terre, et en quelque point de la Terre que cette ombre tombe, le Soleil est éclipsé.

Les astronomes disent qu'il y a trois sortes d'éclipses de Soleil, partielle, totale et annulaire. Une éclipse partielle, c'est évidemment quand une partie seulement, ou un côté du disque du Soleil est caché ; une éclipse totale, quand le disque entier est caché, et une éclipse annulaire, quand la Lune ne paraît pas assez grande pour couvrir toute la face du Soleil, et qu'il reste un anneau brillant autour de lui. Pourquoi donc, demandera peut-être le lecteur, l'éclipse de Soleil est-elle tantôt totale et tantôt annulaire ? Y a-t-il des moments où la Lune est plus grande, ou le Soleil plus petit ? Non — mais tantôt le Soleil, aussi bien que la Lune, est plus éloigné qu'à d'autres moments. Placé à quelque distance d'une vitre de votre chambre, elle paraît presque aussi grande qu'un bâtiment situé à un pâté de maisons ou deux : mais approchez-vous de la fenêtre, et nous verrons la vitre proportionnellement plus grande que le bâtiment. Ainsi, quand la Lune est plus proche, ou le Soleil plus éloigné, l'ombre qui tombe sur la Terre est proportionnellement plus grande, et inversement.

L'éclipse de cet après-midi sera de celles que l'on appelle totales, sauf qu'Ottawa se trouve un peu trop au nord pour qu'elle y soit totale. Pour la voir exactement au-dessus du centre du Soleil, il faut être à Springfield, ou n'importe où sur une ligne droite courant en diagonale à travers la Terre depuis le nord de la Sibérie, en passant par l'Alaska, l'Iowa, l'Illinois, le Kentucky et la Caroline du Nord.

De tous les phénomènes en matière d'éclipses, une éclipse totale de Soleil est le plus sublime. « Pendant un laps de temps n'excédant pas huit minutes », dit un auteur sur les éclipses, « nous observons le passage d'une lumière du soleil à une obscurité presque semblable à celle de la nuit, et le retour. Le ciel, à mesure que l'éclipse partielle grandit de plus en plus, change ses teintes en diverses nuances, décrites parfois comme livides, mais mêlées de jaune orangé ou de pourpre, parfois bien avant le début de l'éclipse totale proprement dite. La Lune avance lentement sur le disque solaire, le couvrant de plus en plus de sa noirceur et rendant les objets de plus en plus obscurs, jusqu'à ce que, au moment où la dernière lueur du Soleil va disparaître, l'observateur voie la Lune et ce qui reste du Soleil entourés d'une couronne ou gloire brillante, comme celle qui entoure la tête du Seigneur et des saints dans les images religieuses. Quand la lumière du soleil disparaît totalement, il ne reste rien pour éclairer les objets alentour, hormis les rayons épars du crépuscule et la couronne elle-même. Cette gloire est coupée çà et là de rayons étincelants, s'étendant souvent à des distances considérables du Soleil, et on l'a vue elle-même presque aussi large que le diamètre du Soleil. Quand la couronne donne la lumière par laquelle les objets sont vus, ils apparaissent naturellement très différents de ce que nous voyons en plein jour, ou même la nuit. On a souvent remarqué la netteté et la noirceur des collines lointaines.

« Outre cette couronne, les protubérances de couleur rosée et de forme irrégulière sont un trait très marqué. Ce sont des masses semblables à des nuages, vues en saillie au-delà du bord sombre de la Lune, qui ne sont en général pas visibles sans télescopes, et qui ont longtemps été, comme la couronne, mystérieuses quant à leur origine. Mais le spectroscope a maintenant établi avec certitude qu'elles sont de nature gazeuse ; on a découvert en les photographiant qu'elles étaient reliées au Soleil, et qu'à mesure que la Lune passait sur elles, elle les cachait peu à peu. Si elles étaient des phénomènes de l'atmosphère lunaire, elles se déplaceraient avec la Lune elle-même, ce qu'elles ne font pas. »

Le dommage est que, si grandioses que soient ces phénomènes, nous sommes un peu trop au nord pour les voir à Ottawa, même si le ciel était tout ce qu'on pourrait souhaiter. Pourtant le spectacle sera loin d'être insignifiant ici, et comme tous nos abonnés auront un billet gratuit, nous les engageons à en tirer le meilleur parti, car ils vivront difficilement assez pour voir une autre éclipse de Soleil aussi proche de la totalité que celle-ci le sera à Ottawa.
text.es:
A eso de las 5 de esta tarde,—o, para ser precisos,—a las 5:03, si el tiempo permite verlo — pues no habrá aplazamiento por causa del tiempo — podrá verse una pantalla o cubierta redonda y oscura que toca el borde inferior de la faz del «glorioso astro del día» y se extiende poco a poco sobre el disco del Sol hasta cubrirlo por completo, salvo el borde norte. Si el cielo resulta estar inusualmente despejado, solo oscurecerá lo bastante para hacer necesarias las luces para leer en el interior; pero si resulta estar nublado, la oscuridad será igual, bastante antes de la puesta del sol, a la de una noche corriente sin Luna.

La causa de esta maravillosa desviación de la rutina ordinaria de todos los días de la naturaleza es el gran eclipse. No hay motivo para alarmarse, por sorprendentes que sean sus fenómenos, pues es un suceso muy corriente, ocurren uno o dos cada año, aunque no a menudo en tan gran escala. Dos veces cada año, hacia el 1 de febrero y el 1 de agosto, el Sol y la Tierra se hallan tan cerca de una posición que pone a la Luna exactamente en una línea entre ellos, que una parte, y a veces toda la sombra de la Luna cae sobre la Tierra, y en cualesquiera posiciones de la Tierra en que cae esta sombra, el Sol está eclipsado.

Los astrónomos dicen que hay tres clases de eclipses de Sol: parcial, total y anular. Un eclipse parcial es, desde luego, cuando solo una parte, o un lado del disco del Sol, queda oculto; un eclipse total es cuando queda oculto todo el disco, y un eclipse anular, cuando la Luna no parece lo bastante grande para cubrir toda la faz del Sol y queda a su alrededor un anillo brillante. Ahora bien, puede preguntar el lector, ¿por qué el eclipse de Sol es a veces total y a veces anular? ¿Hay ocasiones en que la Luna es mayor, o el Sol más pequeño? No — pero a veces tanto el Sol como la Luna están más lejos que otras veces. Puesta a cierta distancia de un cristal de su habitación, la hoja parece casi tan grande como un edificio a una manzana o dos de distancia; pero acérquese a la ventana, y veremos el cristal proporcionalmente mayor que el edificio. Así, cuando la Luna está más cerca, o el Sol más lejos, la sombra que cae sobre la Tierra es proporcionalmente mayor, y viceversa.

El eclipse de esta tarde será de la clase llamada total, salvo que Ottawa queda un poco demasiado al norte para que aquí sea total. Para verlo exactamente sobre el centro del Sol tenemos que estar en Springfield, o en cualquier punto de una línea recta que corre en diagonal a través de la Tierra desde el norte de Siberia, pasando por Alaska, Iowa, Illinois, Kentucky y Carolina del Norte.

De todos los fenómenos en materia de eclipses, un eclipse total de Sol es el más sublime. «Durante un lapso de tiempo que no pasa de ocho minutos», dice un escritor sobre eclipses, «observamos el paso de la luz del sol a una oscuridad casi como la de la noche y de nuevo de vuelta. El cielo, a medida que el eclipse parcial se hace mayor y mayor, cambia sus tintes a diversos matices, descritos a veces como lívidos, pero mezclados con amarillo anaranjado, o púrpura, a veces mucho antes del comienzo del eclipse total propiamente dicho. La Luna avanza lentamente sobre el disco solar, cubriendo más y más de él con su negrura, y haciendo más y más oscuros los objetos, hasta que, cuando está a punto de pasar el último destello de luz solar, el observador ve la Luna y lo que queda del Sol rodeados por una brillante corona o gloria, como la que rodea las cabezas del Señor y de los santos en las pinturas religiosas. Cuando la luz solar desaparece por completo, nada queda para iluminar los objetos de alrededor, salvo los rayos dispersos del crepúsculo y la propia corona. Esta gloria está atravesada aquí y allá por rayos fulgurantes, que se extienden a menudo a distancias considerables del Sol, y se la ha visto casi tan ancha como el diámetro del Sol. Cuando la corona da la luz con la que se ven los objetos, estos aparecen, naturalmente, muy distintos de lo que vemos a la luz del día, o incluso de noche. A menudo se ha notado la nitidez y la negrura de las colinas lejanas.

«Además de esta corona, las protuberancias de color rosado y forma irregular son un rasgo muy marcado. Son masas parecidas a nubes que se ven sobresalir más allá del borde oscuro de la Luna, no son visibles por lo general sin telescopios, y durante mucho tiempo, igual que la corona, han sido misteriosas en su origen. Pero ahora el espectroscopio ha establecido con certeza que son de naturaleza gaseosa; se descubrió al fotografiarlas que estaban conectadas con el Sol, y que, al pasar la Luna sobre ellas, las ocultaba poco a poco. Si fueran fenómenos de la atmósfera lunar, se moverían con la propia Luna, lo que no hacen».

Lo lamentable es que, por grandiosos que sean estos fenómenos, estamos un poco demasiado al norte para verlos en Ottawa, aunque el cielo fuera todo lo que pudiera desearse. Sin embargo, el espectáculo distará mucho de ser insignificante aquí, y como todos nuestros suscriptores tendrán un billete gratuito, les aconsejamos que lo aprovechen al máximo, pues difícilmente vivirán para ver otro eclipse de Sol tan cercano al total como este lo será en Ottawa.
text.it:
Oggi pomeriggio verso le 5,—o, per essere precisi,—alle 5h 3′ esatte, se il tempo sarà tale da permettere di vederla—perché non vi sarà alcun rinvio a causa del tempo—si potrà vedere uno schermo o copertura rotonda e scura toccare il bordo inferiore del volto del «glorioso astro del giorno» e stendersi gradualmente sul disco del Sole finché tutto, tranne il bordo settentrionale, sarà completamente coperto. Se il cielo sarà insolitamente sereno, diventerà abbastanza buio solo da rendere necessarie le luci per leggere in casa; ma se sarà nuvoloso, l'oscurità sarà pari, ben prima del tramonto, a quella di una normale notte senza chiaro di luna.

La causa di questa meravigliosa deviazione dalla routine ordinaria di ogni giorno della natura è la grande eclissi. Non c'è nulla di cui allarmarsi, per quanto sorprendenti siano i suoi fenomeni, perché è un evento molto ordinario, ne avvengono uno o due ogni anno, ma non spesso su una scala così grande. Due volte ogni anno, verso il 1º febbraio e il 1º agosto, il Sole e la Terra si trovano in una posizione così vicina a porre la Luna esattamente su una linea tra loro, che una parte, e talvolta l'intera ombra della Luna cade sulla Terra, e in qualunque punto della Terra cada questa ombra, il Sole è eclissato.

Gli astronomi dicono che vi sono tre tipi di eclissi di Sole: parziale, totale e anulare. Un'eclissi parziale è, naturalmente, quella in cui è nascosta solo una parte, o un lato, del disco del Sole; un'eclissi totale è quella in cui è nascosto l'intero disco, e un'eclissi anulare quella in cui la Luna non sembra abbastanza grande da coprire l'intera faccia del Sole, e resta intorno ad esso un anello luminoso. Ora, può chiedersi il lettore, perché l'eclissi di Sole è talvolta totale e talvolta anulare? Vi sono momenti in cui la Luna è più grande, o il Sole più piccolo? No—ma talvolta il Sole, come pure la Luna, è più lontano che in altri momenti. Stando a una certa distanza da un vetro nella vostra stanza, esso appare grande quasi quanto un edificio a un isolato o due di distanza: ma avvicinandosi alla finestra, vedremo il vetro proporzionalmente più grande dell'edificio. Così, quando la Luna è più vicina, o il Sole più lontano, l'ombra che cade sulla Terra è proporzionalmente più grande, e viceversa.

L'eclissi di questo pomeriggio sarà del tipo detto totale, salvo che Ottawa si trova un po' troppo a nord per averla qui totale. Per vederla esattamente sul centro del Sole dobbiamo trovarci a Springfield, o in qualunque punto di una linea retta che corre diagonalmente attraverso la Terra dalla Siberia settentrionale, passando per l'Alaska, l'Iowa, l'Illinois, il Kentucky e la Carolina del Nord.

Tra tutti i fenomeni in fatto di eclissi, un'eclissi totale di Sole è il più sublime. «In uno spazio di tempo non superiore a otto minuti», dice uno scrittore di eclissi, «osserviamo il passaggio da una luce solare a un'oscurità quasi come quella della notte, e di nuovo indietro. Il cielo, man mano che l'eclissi parziale si fa sempre più grande, cambia le sue tinte in vari colori, descritti talvolta come livido, ma misto con giallo arancio, o porpora, talvolta ben prima dell'inizio della vera eclissi totale. La Luna avanza lentamente sul disco solare, coprendone sempre di più con il suo nero, e rendendo gli oggetti sempre più oscuri, finché, quando l'ultimo bagliore di luce solare sta per svanire, l'osservatore vede la Luna e ciò che resta del Sole circondati da una brillante corona o gloria, come quella che circonda il capo del Signore e dei santi nelle immagini religiose. Quando la luce solare scompare del tutto, non resta nulla a illuminare gli oggetti intorno, tranne i raggi diffusi del crepuscolo e la corona stessa. Questa gloria è intersecata qua e là da raggi scintillanti, che si estendono spesso a distanze considerevoli dal Sole, ed è stata vista essa stessa larga quasi quanto il diametro del Sole. Quando la corona dà la luce con cui si vedono gli oggetti, essi appaiono naturalmente molto diversi da come li vediamo alla luce del giorno, o anche di notte. La nitidezza e la nerezza delle colline lontane sono state spesso notate.

«Oltre a questa corona, le protuberanze di colore roseo e di forma irregolare sono una caratteristica molto marcata. Sono masse simili a nubi viste sporgere oltre il bordo scuro della Luna, non sono in genere visibili senza telescopi, e sono state a lungo, come la corona, misteriose nella loro origine. Ma ora lo spettroscopio ha reso certo che sono di natura gassosa; fotografandole si è scoperto che erano connesse con il Sole, e che man mano che la Luna passava su di esse le nascondeva a poco a poco. Se fossero fenomeni dell'atmosfera lunare, si muoverebbero con la Luna stessa, cosa che non fanno».

Il peccato è che, per quanto grandiosi siano questi fenomeni, siamo un po' troppo a nord per vederli a Ottawa, anche se il cielo fosse tutto ciò che si potrebbe desiderare. Eppure lo spettacolo sarà tutt'altro che banale qui, e poiché tutti i nostri abbonati avranno un biglietto gratuito, consigliamo loro di trarne il massimo, perché difficilmente vivranno abbastanza per vedere un'altra eclissi di Sole così vicina alla totalità come questa sarà a Ottawa.
text.ja:
今日の午後5時ごろ—正確に言えば、ちょうど5時3分に—天候が見ることを許すものであれば—天候を理由とする延期はないので—円形の暗い幕あるいは覆いが、「栄光ある日の天体」の面の下の縁に触れているのが見え、やがて北の縁を除いて完全に覆われるまで、太陽の円盤の上へ次第に広がってゆくであろう。空がたまたま格別に澄んでいれば、室内で読書するのに明かりが要る程度にしか暗くならない。しかし曇っていれば、日没よりかなり前に、月のない普通の夜と同じ暗さになるであろう。

自然の日々の普段の営みからのこの驚くべき逸脱の原因は、大日食である。その現象は驚くべきものではあるが、うろたえるには及ばない。それはきわめてありふれた出来事で、毎年一、二度起こるのであって、ただこれほど大規模なものは少ない。毎年二度、およそ2月1日と8月1日ごろに、太陽と地球が、月をちょうどその間の一線上に置くほどの位置に近づき、月の影の一部が、ときには全体が地球の上に落ち、地球上でこの影が落ちる位置ではどこでも、太陽が食される。

天文学者の言うところでは、日食には三種類あり、部分食、皆既食、金環食である。部分食とは、もちろん、太陽の円盤のただ一部分、あるいは一方の側だけが隠れるときであり、皆既食とは円盤全体が隠れるときであり、金環食とは月が太陽の面全体を覆うほど大きく見えず、そのまわりに明るい環が残るときである。さて、読者は尋ねるかもしれない。日食がときに皆既となり、ときに金環となるのはなぜか。月が大きくなったり、太陽が小さくなったりするときがあるのか。否、そうではなく、太陽も月も、ときに他のときより遠くにあるのである。部屋の窓ガラスから少し離れて立つと、それは一、二ブロック先の建物とほぼ同じ大きさに見える。ところが窓に近づけば、窓ガラスは建物に比べてそれ相応に大きく見える。だから、月が近いか太陽が遠いかすれば、地球に落ちる影はそれ相応に大きく、その逆もまたそうなのである。

今日の午後の日食は皆既と呼ばれる種類のものになるが、オタワはやや北にありすぎて、ここでは皆既にならない。太陽の中心のちょうど真上に見るには、スプリングフィールドか、シベリア北部からアラスカ、アイオワ、イリノイ、ケンタッキー、ノースカロライナを通って地球を斜めに横切る直線上のどこかにいなければならない。

日食に関する諸現象のうちで、皆既日食は最も崇高である。「8分を超えない時間のうちに」と、日食に関するある著述家は言う。「私たちは、日光から夜にも似た闇への移り変わりと、その逆戻りとを目にする。空は、部分食が大きくなるにつれてさまざまな色合いに変わり、それはときに鉛色と言われるが、橙黄色や紫が混じっていて、ときには本来の皆既の始まりのずっと前からそうなる。月は太陽の円盤の上をゆっくり進み、その黒さでますます多くを覆い、ものをますます見分けにくくし、ついに最後の日光の一筋が消え去ろうとするとき、観測者は月と太陽の残りが、宗教画の主や聖人たちの頭を取り巻くような、明るいコロナあるいは栄光の輪に囲まれているのを見る。日光が完全に消えると、まわりのものを照らすものは、薄明の散乱光とコロナそのもののほかには何も残らない。この栄光の輪には、ところどころに閃く光線が交差し、しばしば太陽からかなりの距離まで伸び、それ自体が太陽の直径とほとんど同じ幅に見られたこともある。コロナがものを見る光を与えるとき、ものは当然、昼間に見るものとも、夜に見るものとさえ、大いに異なって見える。遠くの丘の鋭さと黒さは、しばしば注目されてきた。

「このコロナのほかに、バラ色で不規則な形の隆起物も、きわめて顕著な特徴である。これらは月の暗い縁の向こうに突き出して見える雲のような塊で、望遠鏡がなければ一般には見えず、コロナと同じく、その起源は長らく謎であった。しかし今では、分光器によって、それらが気体の性質のものであることが確かめられている。それらを写真に撮ることで、太陽につながっていること、そして月がその上を通り過ぎるにつれて少しずつそれらを隠してゆくことがわかった。もしそれらが月の大気の現象であるなら、月そのものとともに動くはずだが、そうはならない。」

残念なのは、これらの現象が壮大であるにもかかわらず、たとえ空が望みうるかぎりの状態であったとしても、私たちはオタワでそれを見るにはやや北にありすぎることである。それでも、ここでの見ものはとるに足りないものからはほど遠く、購読者の皆様はみな無料の入場券をお持ちなので、存分に楽しまれるようお勧めする。オタワで見られるこの日食ほど皆既に近い日食を、もう一度見るまで生きている人は、ほとんどいないであろうから。

text_orig:
The great event of the period was the eclipse of the sun which occurred yesterday. It was generally understood that such an event would take place, and our people generally were on the lookout for this important phenomenon. Theory and observation alike prove that in the period of eighteen years and eleven days in which the moon passes to the same position in reference to the sun and its nodes—i. e. one of the two points in which the orbit of the satellite intersects that of its primary—there are in general seventy eclipses, of which forty-one are of the sun and twenty-nine of the moon. There cannot be more than seven eclipses in one year, nor less than two; and if the latter, they must both be eclipses of the sun. Eclipses of the sun can only be seen at one zone of the earth, and that a very narrow one; for the dimensions of the shadow of the moon are small as compared with the earth. Out of the forty-one solar eclipses which may occur in eighteen years, there are in general twenty-eight of those which may become central according to circumstances—that is, either total or annular. It results from Du Sejour's calculations that the greatest possible duration of an eclipse of the sun cannot be more than 4 hours 29 min. 44 sec. at the equator, or 3 hours 26 min. 32 sec. for the latitude of Paris. In total eclipses the greatest possible duration of total obscuration may only be 7 min. 58 sec. at the equator, and 6 min. 10 sec. at the latitude of Paris. Such combinations are of course very rare.

It was about twenty-three minutes after four when the line of shade began to creep gradually up over the disc of the sun, covering the lower limb gradually in its progress. It continued until twenty-two minutes past 5 o'clock. At its greatest obscuation, about eleven and a quarter twelfths of the sun's surface was darkened, at which time the sky changed its azure blue to a livid purple or violet, and a gloom pervaded all nature, and the earth and skies assumed a lurid, unearthly hue

We were not favored at this point with a total eclipse, but so near the belt, as to form some idea of the grandeur which must attend such a phenomenon, and to feel that “The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament showeth his handiwork.”

text.zh-Hans:
当代之大事，为昨日所生之日食。众人大抵知有此事，吾邑人亦多留心此重要之象。理论与观测皆证明，月于日及其交点之关系复至同一位置之十八年十一日之期内——交点，即月轨与其主星轨相交之二点之一——大抵有七十次食，其中日食四十一次，月食二十九次。一年之内食不得多于七次，不得少于二次；若为少者，则二次必皆日食。日食仅能于地上一带得见，且甚狭；因月影之大小较地为小。十八年内可有之四十一次日食中，视情形可成中心食，即或全或环者，大抵有二十八次。据 Du Sejour 之推算，日食至长之时，赤道上不得过四小时二十九分四十四秒，巴黎纬度则不得过三小时二十六分三十二秒。全食中，全掩至长之时，赤道上不得过七分五十八秒，巴黎纬度不得过六分十秒。此等相合自然极罕。

约四时二十三分，阴影之线始渐渐爬上日面，渐掩其下缘。延至五时二十二分。至最大掩蔽时，日面约十二分之十一又四分之一被暗，其时天由蔚蓝变为铅紫或紫罗兰，一片阴沉遍布万物，大地与天空皆呈骇人、非尘世之色。

吾处此时未蒙全食之幸，然距食带甚近，足以略想此象所必伴之壮观，并觉「诸天述说神的荣耀，穹苍传扬他的手段」。

text.fr:
Le grand événement de l'époque a été l'éclipse de Soleil qui s'est produite hier. On savait généralement qu'un tel événement aurait lieu, et nos gens étaient en général à l'affût de cet important phénomène. La théorie et l'observation prouvent également que, dans la période de dix-huit ans et onze jours au cours de laquelle la Lune revient à la même position par rapport au Soleil et à ses nœuds — c'est-à-dire l'un des deux points où l'orbite du satellite coupe celle de son astre principal — il y a en général soixante-dix éclipses, dont quarante et une de Soleil et vingt-neuf de Lune. Il ne peut y avoir plus de sept éclipses en une année, ni moins de deux ; et si c'est le cas pour ce dernier nombre, elles doivent être toutes deux des éclipses de Soleil. Les éclipses de Soleil ne peuvent être vues que sur une seule zone de la Terre, et une zone très étroite ; car les dimensions de l'ombre de la Lune sont petites comparées à la Terre. Sur les quarante et une éclipses de Soleil qui peuvent survenir en dix-huit ans, il y en a en général vingt-huit qui peuvent devenir centrales selon les circonstances — c'est-à-dire soit totales soit annulaires. Il résulte des calculs de Du Sejour que la plus grande durée possible d'une éclipse de Soleil ne peut dépasser 4 heures 29 min. 44 sec. à l'équateur, ou 3 heures 26 min. 32 sec. pour la latitude de Paris. Dans les éclipses totales, la plus grande durée possible de l'obscuration totale ne peut être que de 7 min. 58 sec. à l'équateur, et de 6 min. 10 sec. à la latitude de Paris. De telles combinaisons sont bien sûr très rares.

Il était environ quatre heures vingt-trois minutes lorsque la ligne d'ombre commença à monter peu à peu sur le disque du Soleil, couvrant graduellement le limbe inférieur dans sa progression. Elle dura jusqu'à cinq heures vingt-deux minutes. À sa plus grande obscuration, environ onze douzièmes et un quart de la surface du Soleil étaient obscurcis, moment auquel le ciel changea son bleu d'azur en un pourpre livide ou violet, et une sombre tristesse se répandit sur toute la nature, et la terre et les cieux prirent une teinte blafarde et surnaturelle.

Nous n'avons pas été favorisés en ce point d'une éclipse totale, mais nous étions si près de la bande que nous avons pu nous faire quelque idée de la grandeur qui doit accompagner un tel phénomène, et sentir que « les cieux racontent la gloire de Dieu, et l'étendue céleste annonce l'œuvre de ses mains ».
text.es:
El gran acontecimiento de la época fue el eclipse de Sol que ocurrió ayer. Se sabía en general que tal acontecimiento iba a tener lugar, y nuestra gente estaba en general a la espera de este importante fenómeno. La teoría y la observación prueban por igual que en el período de dieciocho años y once días en que la Luna pasa a la misma posición con respecto al Sol y a sus nodos (es decir, uno de los dos puntos en que la órbita del satélite corta la de su planeta principal) hay, en general, setenta eclipses, de los cuales cuarenta y uno son de Sol y veintinueve de Luna. No puede haber más de siete eclipses en un año, ni menos de dos; y si son estos últimos, ambos tienen que ser eclipses de Sol. Los eclipses de Sol solo pueden verse en una zona de la Tierra, y muy estrecha; pues las dimensiones de la sombra de la Luna son pequeñas en comparación con la Tierra. De los cuarenta y un eclipses solares que pueden ocurrir en dieciocho años, hay en general veintiocho de los que pueden llegar a ser centrales según las circunstancias, es decir, o totales o anulares. De los cálculos de Du Sejour resulta que la mayor duración posible de un eclipse de Sol no puede pasar de 4 horas 29 min. 44 seg. en el ecuador, o 3 horas 26 min. 32 seg. para la latitud de París. En los eclipses totales la mayor duración posible de la obscuración total puede ser solo de 7 min. 58 seg. en el ecuador, y de 6 min. 10 seg. en la latitud de París. Tales combinaciones son por supuesto muy raras.

Eran aproximadamente las cuatro y veintitrés minutos cuando la línea de sombra comenzó a trepar poco a poco sobre el disco del Sol, cubriendo gradualmente el limbo inferior en su avance. Continuó hasta las 5 y veintidós minutos. En su mayor obscuración, unas once doceavas partes y cuarto de la superficie del Sol quedaron oscurecidas; en ese momento el cielo cambió su azul azur por un púrpura lívido o violeta, una penumbra invadió toda la naturaleza, y la tierra y los cielos adoptaron un tinte lúgubre y sobrenatural.

No nos favoreció en este punto un eclipse total, pero estábamos tan cerca de la franja que pudimos formarnos alguna idea de la grandeza que debe acompañar a tal fenómeno, y sentir que «Los cielos cuentan la gloria de Dios, y el firmamento anuncia la obra de sus manos».
text.it:
Il grande evento del periodo fu l'eclissi di Sole avvenuta ieri. Si sapeva in generale che un tale evento avrebbe avuto luogo, e la nostra gente era in generale in attesa di questo importante fenomeno. La teoria e l'osservazione provano ugualmente che nel periodo di diciotto anni e undici giorni, in cui la Luna passa alla stessa posizione rispetto al Sole e ai suoi nodi—cioè uno dei due punti in cui l'orbita del satellite interseca quella del suo primario—vi sono in generale settanta eclissi, delle quali quarantuno sono di Sole e ventinove di Luna. Non possono esserci più di sette eclissi in un anno, né meno di due; e se due, devono essere entrambe eclissi di Sole. Le eclissi di Sole si possono vedere soltanto in una zona della Terra, e questa assai stretta; poiché le dimensioni dell'ombra della Luna sono piccole in confronto alla Terra. Delle quarantuno eclissi solari che possono verificarsi in diciotto anni, ve ne sono in generale ventotto che possono diventare centrali secondo le circostanze—cioè, o totali o anulari. Dai calcoli di Du Sejour risulta che la massima durata possibile di un'eclissi di Sole non può essere superiore a 4 ore 29 min. 44 sec. all'equatore, o a 3 ore 26 min. 32 sec. per la latitudine di Parigi. Nelle eclissi totali la massima durata possibile dell'oscurazione totale può essere soltanto di 7 min. 58 sec. all'equatore, e di 6 min. 10 sec. alla latitudine di Parigi. Simili combinazioni sono naturalmente assai rare.

Erano circa le 4h 23′ quando la linea d'ombra cominciò a salire gradualmente sul disco del Sole, coprendo gradualmente il lembo inferiore nel suo avanzare. Continuò fino alle 5h 22′. Alla massima oscurazione, circa undici dodicesimi e un quarto della superficie del Sole fu oscurata, e in quel momento il cielo mutò il suo blu azzurro in un livido porpora o viola, un buio pervase tutta la natura, e la terra e i cieli assunsero una tinta spettrale, non terrena.

In questo punto non fummo favoriti da un'eclissi totale, ma tanto vicini alla fascia da formarci qualche idea della grandiosità che deve accompagnare un simile fenomeno, e da sentire che «I cieli narrano la gloria di Dio, e il firmamento annuncia l'opera delle sue mani».
text.ja:
この時期の大事件は、昨日起こった日食であった。そのような出来事が起こることは広く知られており、我々の住民の多くは、この重要な現象を待ち構えていた。理論と観測はともに、月が太陽およびその交点—すなわち、衛星の軌道が主星の軌道と交わる二つの点の一つ—に対して同じ位置を通る18年11日の周期の間に、概して70回の食があり、そのうち41回が日食、29回が月食であることを証明している。一年のうちに7回を超える食はなく、2回を下回ることもない。後者の場合には、それらは両方とも日食でなければならない。日食は地球上のただ一つの帯でしか見えず、しかもそれはきわめて狭い。月の影の大きさは地球に比べて小さいからである。18年の間に起こりうる41回の日食のうち、概して28回は、状況に応じて中心食、すなわち皆既または金環となりうるものである。デュ・セジュールの計算から、日食の最大可能継続時間は、赤道で4時間29分44秒、パリの緯度では3時間26分32秒を超ええないことが導かれる。皆既食では、完全な掩蔽の最大可能継続時間は、赤道で7分58秒、パリの緯度で6分10秒にしかなりえない。そのような組み合わせはもちろんきわめてまれである。

4時23分ごろ、影の線が太陽の円盤の上をじわじわと這い上がり始め、その進行につれて下縁を徐々に覆っていった。それは5時22分まで続いた。最大の掩蔽のとき、太陽の表面のおよそ12分の11と4分の1が暗くなり、そのとき空は青空の青から鉛色の紫またはすみれ色に変わり、陰鬱さが万物に行き渡り、大地と空は不気味で超自然的な色合いを帯びた。

我々はこの地点では皆既日食の恵みを受けなかったが、帯にきわめて近く、そのような現象に伴うに違いない壮大さをいくらか思い描き、「諸天は神の栄光を語り、大空はその御手の業を示す」と感じるには十分であった。

text_orig: SPRINGFIELD, Aug. 7.—The total eclipse of the sun, at Springfield, Ill., has come off with a perfectly cloudless sky, and a beautiful transparent atmosphere. At the head of the working force stationed here for the past three weeks, making the necessary preparations for observing the eclipse, is Charles A. Scott, for a long time one of the principal assistants on the Coast Survey. Under him are Mr. L. N. Pauntalis, Major J. W. Black, and Mr. Fitzgerald, in charge of the department for photographing the sun as often as possible during the progress of the eclipse. To assist Mr. Scott in the determination of time, and recording as well as making certain observations on the corona and red protuberances, were assigned Mr. Robert A. McLeed, and two young gentlemen from Cambridge, whose names were not ascertained. During the scientific observations with the instruments, it was necessary to have perfect silence and fixed attention on the part of the observers, hence, instead of observing the eclipse at any point within the city, the Coast Survey party selected a point about two miles from the center of this town. This spot is within the grounds surrounding the reservoir which supplies Springfield with the water of the Sangamon River, on the south-west side of the river. Just below its elevated sloping sides a temporary observatory was erected to shelter the principal instruments of observation. Within the building was mounted a fine transit instrument, for obtaining the local time of Springfield, and for determining its difference of longitude from Washington. This morning (August 7) the superintendent of the coast survey arrived. His son, Professor James M. Pierce of Harvard, has been here some days. New Haven is represented by Professor Twining; the New-York University by its Professor of Astronomy the Kingston University, Canada, by Prof. Dupuis; and the State of Maryland by the Hon. Mr. Evans, formerly member of Congress, and an enthusiastic amateur astronomer. There are probably others of whom I have not heard. Soon after 1 o'clock this afternoon the astronomers began to take their positions and prepare their numerous and varied instruments for observation. The predicted time for the meridian of the little observatory were: Beginning of eclipse, 4h. 35m. 5-10s., Springfield, mean time, beginning of totality, 5h. 5m. 20 7-10s.; end of totality, 5h. 8m. 10 2-10s.; mean time of eclipse, 6h. 3m. 41 2-10s. Quite a number of people were collected outside the fence and cord which inclosed the astronomers. Somewhat later numerous carriages and farm wagons began to arrive, and the horses were tied to the fence. Crowdt of people on foot and some or horseback began to stream from the town toward the reservoir. Finding they were not permitted within the astronomical lines, the people, men, […] ladies and children, stormed the hights of the reservoir and took possession, where they remained standing or seated on the grassy slope awaiting the eclipse. At 4 o'clock the astronomers were looking in silence through their telescopes for the first contact, and it came at last within a very few seconds of the predicted time. In a moment more the whole crowd recognized the black dent in the sun's north-western limit through their pieces of smoked glass. As the eclipse progressed, the photographic party took impressions rapidly, and recorded at the same time the instant of obtaining their pictures. Not less than 235 impressions of the sun were taken from the beginning to the close of the eclipse. At 4 h., 45 min., the diminution of light was very perceptible, and at 5 o'clock a singular leaden hue began to spread over the heavens, especially toward the north-west. At three minutes past 5, or a little more than two minutes before the total obscuration, the planet Venus was seen, and the boys began to cry out—"I see a star." Within six seconds of the prediction, the last rays of the sun disappeared, and that instant the corona burst forth in all its splendor and beauty. Another moment and the red flash of a protuberance burst forth on the left hand limb of the sun, like a tongue of flame jetting out horizontally. Soon another jet flashed vertically downward from the lowest limb of the sun. Others, observing with the aid of the telescope, saw several more of these protuberances. Meanwhile the heavens had darkened sufficiently to permit a view of the following planets and stars, besides Venus; viz.: Mercury, Mars, Saturn, Regulus and Arcturus. One gentleman relates that his neighbor's fowls went tto heir roost; but probably owing to the extreme clearness of the atmsophere, and its absolute freedom from all clouds, every one was impressed with the fact that the darkness was not nearly as great as they expected. A herd of cattle feeding at a little distance from the reservoir did not seem to pay any attention to the change. The horizon all around was lightened up by a sort of dim twilight, for four or five degrees in breadth, and above this rim of light hung a dark, leaden canopy, increasing in depth of shade toward the zenith. Suddenly the sun burst out again from behind the beautiful corona, and almost instantly the corona and red protuberances vanished. The people immediately threw away their smoked and shade glasses, which went crashing in all directions with a ringing sound, and the crowd dispersed at once, not waiting for the end, but took up their course for the town far more rapidly than they arrived. The astronomers almost alone continued to the close of the performance. The spectroscrope was not employed in the observances at this place, nearly all the instruments, and those skilled in their use, having gone to Shelby, Ky., and Des Moines, Iowa. Most of the astronomical observers of this eclipse have come to the conclusion that by far the greater part of the phenomenon called the corona, if not the whole of it, belongs to our own atmospere, rather than to any atmosphere either of the sun or moon. In fact, just as we see a small corona, or ring light around the moon, so the reflection and refraction of our atmosphere produces the greater part, if not all, of the corona around the sun. It is only seen best during the solar eclipse, because the brightness of its rays obscures it at other times, just as he puts out the planets and stars in the day. The red projections seem to belong peculiarly to the sun. At least the astronomers have not yet abandoned that idea.

text.zh-Hans: 斯普林菲尔德，八月七日电。伊利诺伊州斯普林菲尔德之日全食，已于万里无云、空气澄澈之下举行。驻此三周、为观食预备诸事之一队人员，其首为 Charles A. Scott，久为海岸测量局主要助手之一。其下有 L. N. Pauntalis 先生、J. W. Black 少校及 Fitzgerald 先生，掌食时尽可能频频摄日之一部。襄助 Scott 先生测定时刻、记录并兼作光冕与红色凸起之某些观测者，为 Robert A. McLeed 先生及自剑桥来之青年二人，其姓名未能问知。以仪器作科学观测，观者须绝对肃静、专注不移，故海岸测量局一行不在城内任何一处观食，而择一地，距此镇中心约二英里。其地在蓄水池四周地界之内，池引 Sangamon 河之水以供斯普林菲尔德，处河之西南岸。池之高坡下方，搭一临时观象台，以庇主要观测仪器。室内装一精良之子午仪，用以测斯普林菲尔德之地方时，并定其与华盛顿之经度差。今晨（八月七日），海岸测量局局长至。其子哈佛大学 James M. Pierce 教授已在此数日。纽黑文由 Twining 教授代表；纽约大学由其天文学教授代表；加拿大金斯敦大学由 Dupuis 教授代表；马里兰州由 Evans 阁下代表，阁下前为国会议员，亦酷好天文之业余者。想尚有他人，余未之闻。今日午后一时稍过，诸天文学家始各就其位，整备所携种种仪器以待观测。小观象台子午线上之预推时刻如下：食始，斯普林菲尔德平时四时三十五分十分之五秒；全食始，五时五分二十又十分之七秒；全食终，五时八分十又十分之二秒；食之平时，六时三分四十一又十分之二秒。围栏与绳索之外，已聚不少人，诸天文学家即在其内。稍后，马车与农家大车络绎而至，马皆系于栅栏。徒步之众及骑马者，自镇中涌向蓄水池。众人见不得入天文学家界线之内，男子、[…]、妇女与小儿，遂攻上蓄水池之高处占据，或立或坐于草坡之上，以候食。四时，诸天文学家默然以望远镜候初触，终至，距预推之时仅数秒。须臾，满场之人隔熏黑玻璃片，皆见日之西北缘有黑色缺口。食渐进，摄影一队速摄影像，同时记各像摄得之刹那。自食始至食终，所摄日像不下二百三十五帧。四时四十五分，光之减退已甚明显；五时，天空始布一种奇异之铅灰色，西北方尤甚。五时三分，即全晦前稍逾二分钟，见金星，童子辈始大呼——「我见一星。」距预推之时六秒以内，日之余光尽没，当下光冕迸发，极其光华绚丽。又须臾，日之左缘红色凸起闪现，如火舌平射而出。未几，日之最下缘又有一道向下直射。他人借望远镜观察，又见此类凸起数处。其间天已转暗，足可望见金星以外诸星，即水星、火星、土星、轩辕十四与大角。有一人述其邻家鸡群归栖；然或因空气极澄、全无云翳，故众人皆觉天暗远不如所预期。蓄水池稍远处有牛群吃草，似不以此变为意。四面地平，有微弱曙暮光之照亮，宽约四五度，此光环之上，悬一暗沉铅灰之幕，愈近天顶，色愈深。忽然日又自瑰丽之光冕后迸出，光冕与红色凸起几乎立时消失。众人旋即抛弃所持熏黑与遮光之玻璃，纷纷四散，铿然作响，人群立散，不待食终，径取道返镇，其速远过来时。惟诸天文学家几乎独留至全程终了。此地观测未用分光镜，因善用此器之人及器具几尽往肯塔基州 Shelby 与艾奥瓦州得梅因。此次观食之天文学家，大半已得结论：所谓光冕者，其绝大部分，若非其全部，属于吾地之大气，而不属日或月之任何大气。实则犹吾侪见月旁有小光冕，即环状光，吾地大气之反射与折射，亦生日旁光冕之大部，甚或其全。唯日食时最清晰可见，因他时日光之亮所掩，犹日于白昼使诸星不显。红色突出之物，似为日所独有。至少诸天文学家尚未弃此说。
